```
c26a244 gpu: on a discrete GPU the rings every draw's shaders read - the constant-buffer copies (87% of the constant buffers bound in an RTX 5090's log since b5b20bb) and the params blocks - go in video memory the CPU writes (DEVICE_LOCAL | HOST_VISIBLE: the BAR, or all of it with Resizable BAR; host memory when there is none or it is full), where they were in host memory and every shader's constant reads crossed the bus - on the integrated GPU they were placed and measured on it is the same RAM. Unmeasured on NVIDIA; BBHOST_RINGS_IN_VRAM=0 puts them back, =1 forces it (the Radeon 8060S runs the same either way: 158-167 fps uncapped at the Altar of Despair). The light grid's one tile is the larger of the window and the render size on each side, and follows a live change of the render size: sized to the window alone, a window a little smaller than the render made it 2x2 tiles, every light drawn once a tile it touches and each tile a pass. A device loss's report also names a submission's edges (its buffer-shadow uploads, which run after the wait for their sparse binds; its recording's start; its end): three RTX 2060 losses (Windows 617.42, Linux 615.71) stopped after one frame's last draw and before the next one's first, with nothing that told where between.
817851e Merge remote-tracking branch 'github/fix/vram-retire-reused' into test/combined-latest
b68ed17 occlusion: the game's own GPU occlusion culling works - real ZPASS sample counts from Vulkan occlusion queries, written into the guest's query blocks on the GPU's timeline, and SET_PREDICATION. Until now every PIXEL_PIPE_STAT_DUMP wrote a rising fake count at parse time, so every object Bloodborne tests (GX GetData 0x256a2f0, ~180 blocks a frame in a dense view) read visible and nothing was culled; on the same Radeon 8060S Kyo measured ~51% GPU with real counts against ~89% without, 90 -> 130 fps uncapped in a heavy spot, 86-88% of the tested objects occluded (KyoPS4x #217-#220, the design ported natively here, no code). The hardware model: each DB keeps a running sample count and a dump stores it, bit 63 set, at addr + 16 * db; Gnm's query is begin at +0 and end at +8, which the game zeroes and diffs. Now the draws after a dump carry an occlusion query each (DrawCall::query_pool, begun and ended around the draw on bb-record, so never across a pass) - up to 64 after a block's first dump (BBHOST_OCCLUSION_CAP), one after any other; a draw past those or one that reached no query (failed, skipped, a full pool) makes its interval read plainly visible. The command processor records the stream as items (query, unmeasured, dump) and at the submission's end, before the label fills, the results are copied with their availability and a one-invocation compute shader (shaders/occlusion.comp, checked-in SPIR-V) walks them keeping the running total T across command buffers and writes T over the eight DBs with the valid bit into guest memory by device address: the counts are in place when the game's fence says the GPU is done, the PS4's order, no CPU round trip, nothing predicted. A dump whose interval holds an unavailable query (AMD resolves none while the window is unfocused, Kyo #220) is not written - the block stays as the game zeroed it, not ready - and the copy never waits, so such a query cannot hang the GPU (BBHOST_OCCLUSION_WAIT=1 makes it wait, a diagnostic). Precise queries where occlusionQueryPrecise exists (the game sets PERFECT_ZPASS_COUNTS); otherwise a nonzero count reads plainly visible, not as one sample (NVIDIA's 0/1, Kyo #219's black world). SET_PREDICATION (0x20, ignored until now): the draws between a ZPASS set and its clear (GX tokens carry no predicate bit) are skipped at host_gpu_draw's start when every dump into the block has retired and the CPU reads it occluded; with a dump still in flight the items so far are resolved at once and the shader also writes a predicate the draws read through VK_EXT_conditional_rendering (enabled when the device has it); without it, or for an unknown block, they draw - a wrong "occluded" makes geometry vanish. DB_COUNT_CONTROL is not honoured (the context registers are not kept for token draws; counting more only reads more visible). BBHOST_OCCLUSION=0 restores the fake (also the fallback for a block outside imported memory), BBHOST_PREDICATION=0 ignores SET_PREDICATION; the glitch hunt turns it off. Logged: the start-up "occlusion: real sample counts ..." line, and "occlusion:" in the 300-flip report and "occlusion totals:" at exit - dumps, queries, unmeasured draws, resolves, dumps the GPU wrote or left not ready, pairs visible / occluded, predication sets and draws skipped on the CPU / GPU-predicated / drawn; the first SET_PREDICATION packets are logged. SET_PREDICATION (0x20, ignored until now): the draws between a ZPASS set and its clear (GX tokens carry no predicate bit) are skipped at host_gpu_draw's start when every dump into the block has retired and the CPU reads it occluded; with a dump still in flight the items so far are resolved at once and the shader also writes a predicate the draws read through VK_EXT_conditional_rendering (enabled when the device has it); without it, or for an unknown block, they draw - a wrong "occluded" makes geometry vanish. DB_COUNT_CONTROL is not honoured (the context registers are not kept for token draws; counting more only reads more visible). BBHOST_OCCLUSION=0 restores the fake (also the fallback for a block outside imported memory), BBHOST_PREDICATION=0 ignores SET_PREDICATION; the glitch hunt turns it off. Logged: the start-up "occlusion: real sample counts ..." line, and "occlusion:" in the 300-flip report and "occlusion totals:" at exit - dumps, queries, unmeasured draws, resolves, dumps the GPU wrote or left not ready, pairs visible / occluded, predication sets and draws skipped on the CPU / GPU-predicated / drawn; the first SET_PREDICATION packets are logged. Built on Windows (MSYS2 UCRT64), no new warnings; not run here (the lead tests on the hardware).
200af54 occlusion: the game's own GPU occlusion culling works - real ZPASS sample counts from Vulkan occlusion queries, written into the guest's query blocks on the GPU's timeline, and SET_PREDICATION. Until now every PIXEL_PIPE_STAT_DUMP wrote a rising fake count at parse time, so every object Bloodborne tests (GX GetData 0x256a2f0, ~180 blocks a frame in a dense view) read visible and nothing was culled; on the same Radeon 8060S Kyo measured ~51% GPU with real counts against ~89% without, 90 -> 130 fps uncapped in a heavy spot, 86-88% of the tested objects occluded (KyoPS4x #217-#220, the design ported natively here, no code). The hardware model: each DB keeps a running sample count and a dump stores it, bit 63 set, at addr + 16 * db; Gnm's query is begin at +0 and end at +8, which the game zeroes and diffs. Now the draws after a dump carry an occlusion query each (DrawCall::query_pool, begun and ended around the draw on bb-record, so never across a pass) - up to 64 after a block's first dump (BBHOST_OCCLUSION_CAP), one after any other; a draw past those or one that reached no query (failed, skipped, a full pool) makes its interval read plainly visible. The command processor records the stream as items (query, unmeasured, dump) and at the submission's end, before the label fills, the results are copied with their availability and a one-invocation compute shader (shaders/occlusion.comp, checked-in SPIR-V) walks them keeping the running total T across command buffers and writes T over the eight DBs with the valid bit into guest memory by device address: the counts are in place when the game's fence says the GPU is done, the PS4's order, no CPU round trip, nothing predicted. A dump whose interval holds an unavailable query (AMD resolves none while the window is unfocused, Kyo #220) is not written - the block stays as the game zeroed it, not ready - and the copy never waits, so such a query cannot hang the GPU (BBHOST_OCCLUSION_WAIT=1 makes it wait, a diagnostic). Precise queries where occlusionQueryPrecise exists (the game sets PERFECT_ZPASS_COUNTS); otherwise a nonzero count reads plainly visible, not as one sample (NVIDIA's 0/1, Kyo #219's black world). SET_PREDICATION (0x20, ignored until now): the draws between a ZPASS set and its clear (GX tokens carry no predicate bit) are skipped at host_gpu_draw's start when every dump into the block has retired and the CPU reads it occluded; with a dump still in flight the items so far are resolved at once and the shader also writes a predicate the draws read through VK_EXT_conditional_rendering (enabled when the device has it); without it, or for an unknown block, they draw - a wrong "occluded" makes geometry vanish. DB_COUNT_CONTROL is not honoured (the context registers are not kept for token draws; counting more only reads more visible). BBHOST_OCCLUSION=0 restores the fake (also the fallback for a block outside imported memory), BBHOST_PREDICATION=0 ignores SET_PREDICATION; the glitch hunt turns it off. Logged: the start-up "occlusion: real sample counts ..." line, and "occlusion:" in the 300-flip report and "occlusion totals:" at exit - dumps, queries, unmeasured draws, resolves, dumps the GPU wrote or left not ready, pairs visible / occluded, predication sets and draws skipped on the CPU / GPU-predicated / drawn; the first SET_PREDICATION packets are logged. Built on Windows (MSYS2 UCRT64), no new warnings; not run here (the lead tests on the hardware).
```

```
      #pragma once
      
      #include <cstdint>
      
      // Bloodborne 1.09 address spaces. Ghidra uses the
      // 0x800000000 image base; bbhost maps the ELF at GuestMemory::slide
      // (preferred 0x400000). ELF file VA = Ghidra VA - kGhidraBase.
      
      constexpr std::uint64_t kGhidraBase = 0x800000000ull;
      constexpr std::uint64_t kPreferredGuestSlide = 0x400000ull;
      
      // SHA-256 of eboot-109-decrypted.bin. Address-based patches and named
      // layouts apply only to this build.
      constexpr const char kEboot109Sha256[] =
          "941f887a562aae054fac35af8cc8f27cf075f3d4cc2e029fb5ae2a663aaa5ae7";
      
      inline constexpr std::uint64_t elf_from_ghidra(std::uint64_t ghidra_va) {
          return ghidra_va - kGhidraBase;
      }
      
      inline constexpr std::uint64_t guest_from_elf(std::uint64_t elf_va, std::uint64_t slide) {
          return slide + elf_va;
      }
      
      inline constexpr std::uint64_t guest_from_ghidra(std::uint64_t ghidra_va, std::uint64_t slide) {
          return guest_from_elf(elf_from_ghidra(ghidra_va), slide);
      }

      # No 12-second minimum on a load after a death or lamp travel.
      #
      # The in-game step (vtable 0x5730480, run by sub_1d386e0) is made for every
      # load. Its first state (sub_1d38870) sets two countdowns sub_1d386e0 takes
      # down by the frame's time: +0x27c to 15 s, how long the last state waits for
      # the other players of a multiplayer session, and +0x278 to 12 s when the
      # step's +0xe4 is set - every load after a death or a lamp's travel - or to 0
      # (the first load from the title). The last state (sub_1d3a3e0) starts the
      # game (InGameStart) once +0x278 is down to 0 and the area says it is ready.
      # On a PC the loading itself is done in 1.5-2.7 s; the screen then waited
      # out the rest of the 12 s with every loader idle (respawn loads 12.1-12.5 s
      # on this project's Linux box and the Windows test laptop alike). The `je`
      # that picks the 0 becomes a `jmp`, so every load takes it; the multiplayer
      # wait and the readiness check stay the game's. Measured: respawns 2.2-2.7 s,
      # a lamp's travel 2.6 s; the first frames after arrival hitch no more than
      # after a 12 s load. On unless `quick_reentry = false` under [loading] in
      # bbhost.toml (BBHOST_QUICK_REENTRY=0 or 1 overrides).
      [patch]
      name = "quick-reentry"
      eboot = "941f887a562aae054fac35af8cc8f27cf075f3d4cc2e029fb5ae2a663aaa5ae7"
      description = "a load after a death or lamp travel ends when the area is ready, not after a 12-second minimum"
      option = "loading.quick_reentry"
      
      # sub_1d38870: cmp byte [r12+0xe4], 0 / je +10 (to the 0) / vmovss xmm0, [12.0f]
      [site.reentry-minimum]
      address = "0x01d38b59"
      expect = "41 80 bc 24 e4 00 00 00 00 74 0a c5 fa 10 05"
      bytes = "41 80 bc 24 e4 00 00 00 00 eb 0a c5 fa 10 05"

- path: /Users/sandvault-dn/bbwork/bbhost-nocrash/src/engine/patch_manifest.h
  content: |
      // Patch manifests: byte patches to the loaded eboot as data
      // files, so a patch is a file next to the host rather than code in it, and a
      // mod can ship its own. docs/modding.md is the format; the short of it:
      //
      //   [patch]
      //   name = "skip-intro"
      //   eboot = "941f887a..."            # the SHA-256 the addresses belong to
      //   description = "..."
      //   option = "startup.skip_intro"    # optional: a config switch that enables it
      //   [site.fromsoft]
      //   address = "0x04d99138"           # guest VA at the preferred 0x400000 base
      //   expect = "4c 00 6f 00"           # what must be there
      //   bytes = "00 00 00 00"            # what is written
      //   kind = "code"                    # or "data": how the page is protected after
      //
      // A manifest applies only when its eboot hash is the loaded image's, and
      // only whole: every site's expected bytes are checked before any is
      // written. Files come from <exe dir>/patches, <exe dir>/../patches (a build
      // tree) and <mods>/patches, in that order; a later file with the same name
      // replaces an earlier one.
      //
      // A player leaves one out with `<name> = false` under [patches] in
      // bbhost.toml, which the setup window's Patches tab writes.
      #pragma once
      
      #include <string>
      #include <vector>
      
      struct ElfImage;
      
      // Reads the manifests and applies the ones that match; one log line each.
      void patch_manifests_apply(ElfImage* image);
      
      // One manifest as the setup window's Patches tab lists it (host/launcher.cpp):
      // read the way patch_manifests_apply reads it, nothing applied.
      struct PatchListing {
          std::string path;  // the file it was read from
          std::string name, description, option, eboot;
          bool enabled = true;  // its own [patch] enabled
          std::string error;    // why it does not parse ("" when it does)
      };
      // Every manifest patch_manifests_apply would read, by file name, a later
      // directory's replacing an earlier one's. `mods` is the mods directory ("" for none).
      std::vector<PatchListing> patch_manifests_list(const std::string& mods);
      // Whether the player left this manifest out: [patches] <name> = false.
      bool patch_manifest_off(const std::string& name);
      // Whether `option` is one a manifest may name (startup.skip_intro, ...).
      bool patch_manifest_option_known(const std::string& option);
```

```
      #!/usr/bin/env python3
      """Generate the FPS++ code sites engine/frame_rate.cpp applies beyond its own value tables, from Kyo's
      "60 FPS++" and "90 FPS++" lists for Bloodborne 1.09 (shadPS4's patch list, user/patches/shadPS4/
      Bloodborne.xml) and the eboot:
      
          tools/fps_sites.py Bloodborne.xml eboot-109-decrypted.bin
      
      writes src/engine/sixty_fps_sites.inc and src/engine/ninety_fps_sites.inc. Addresses in the lists are
      Binary Ninja's (the ELF's VA + 0x400000), the same as frame_rate.cpp's.
      
      Each list's lines are applied in order to a copy of the image (later lines overwrite earlier ones, as a
      patch loader does), then every byte the list changes is kept except:
        - bytes engine/frame_rate.cpp's value tables write (kConstants, kCounts, kBytes): those values are
          computed there for the rate the game runs at;
        - the frame-time manager, 0x2434770..0x2435480 - ours replaces that function whole
          (its 60 mode is case 2 with no history, which is what those edits make of it);
        - EXCLUDE below, each with the reason.
      Contiguous kept bytes become one site: its address, the bytes the eboot holds there, the bytes the list
      leaves. frame_rate.cpp checks every site's old bytes before writing any.
      
      The 90 file holds the cloth's six stiffness caves from "90 FPS++" (1.0): what it does beyond "60 FPS++",
      a run of the bytes either list changes kept when any byte in it differs from what the 60 sites leave,
      less EXCLUDE_90. Above 60 frame_rate.cpp writes the 60 sites, then these over them, so the old bytes
      recorded are the eboot's; it writes the scalars the caves read (0x4d3bd00) itself, every frame. The tool
      checks that each cave reads those scalars. Kyo's 1.3 lists put the caves at 0x5490000 and compute the
      scale there; frame_rate.cpp keeps the 1.0 caves and does the 1.3 arithmetic.
      """
      import os
      import re
      import struct
      import sys
      import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET
      
      FRAME_MANAGER = (0x2434770, 0x2435480)
      EXCLUDE = [
          # sub_2435630: a local's zeroing turned into a store of mode 2 into the flipper; ours picks the mode.
          (0x243565e, 0x2435666, 'frame mode'),
          # The frame modes' name table (debug display); absolute pointers valid only at the default load
          # address, and relocated at load, so not what the file holds.
          (0x575a920, 0x575a928, 'mode names'), (0x575a930, 0x575a938, 'mode names'),
          # The engine's timed condition wait returns at once instead of waiting: every job worker spins.
          # An emulator's latency workaround; the host's waits wake on time.
          (0x2483ec1, 0x2483ec6, 'timed wait'),
          # The sound thread's sleep, capped through a cave written over the tail of a live function
          # (sub_4632d0); frame_rate.cpp sets that thread's update time instead (MainThreadUpdateTime).
          (0x463300, 0x463312, 'sleep cave'), (0x2c0137d, 0x2c01382, 'sleep cave'),
          # The later list's version of that cap: the stub written into the loop itself (0x2c012cc).
          (0x2c012cc, 0x2c012de, 'sleep cave'),
          # The same loop's three profiling clock reads skipped: not needed with a host gettimeofday.
          (0x2c0118a, 0x2c0118c, 'profiling'), (0x2c011eb, 0x2c011ed, 'profiling'), (0x2c012ca, 0x2c012cc, 'profiling'),
          # The ragdoll/clip drive's path B load moved to a converted constant: frame_rate.cpp's kFrameTimeSites
          # point it at the frame's time instead.
          (0x1915fab, 0x1915fb3, 'clip step'),
          # Durations, not steps (a frame count's seconds, two shortest-duration floors): they stay 1/30, as in
          # Kyo's 1.3 list.
          (0x4c88688, 0x4c8868c, 'duration'), (0x4cadc08, 0x4cadc0c, 'duration'), (0x4cadd28, 0x4cadd2c, 'duration'),
          # Seconds the list converted as if they were frames (frame_rate.cpp says what each is): an attack hit's
          # lifetime from a param frame count, the menu's auto-repeat interval, network timers drained by the
          # real dt (a sign's refresh, a position record's period, remote objects' lifetimes, a peer's session
          # protection), and the Havok AI's braking limit in m/s^2.
          (0x4d28418, 0x4d2841c, 'duration'), (0x4d27720, 0x4d27724, 'duration'),
          (0x1ca975a, 0x1ca975e, 'duration'), (0x1ca9892, 0x1ca9896, 'duration'), (0x1c9f889, 0x1c9f88d, 'duration'),
          (0x187305d, 0x1873061, 'duration'), (0x187458d, 0x1874591, 'duration'), (0x18b254d, 0x18b2551, 'duration'),
          (0x18b382d, 0x18b3831, 'duration'), (0x187afec, 0x187aff0, 'duration'), (0x187b0ad, 0x187b0b1, 'duration'),
          (0x1880cfd, 0x1880d01, 'duration'), (0x1880e1a, 0x1880e1e, 'duration'), (0x21bb004, 0x21bb008, 'physical'),
      ]
      # Left out of the 90 file (Kyo's 1.3 package drops them): the damping exponent's load, the integrator's
      # dt * dt scale (its hook and cave), the fixed 0.0125 turn step, and the scalars (frame_rate.cpp writes them).
      EXCLUDE_90 = [
          (0xb6fbd4, 0xb6fbd8, 'damping exponent'),
          (0xb73f84, 0xb73f8d, 'integrator hook'), (0xb73fa8, 0xb73fc1, 'integrator cave'),
          (0x1cbdb42, 0x1cbdb52, 'turn step'),
          (0x4d3bd00, 0x4d3bd20, 'cloth scalars'),
      ]
      ROOT = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), '..')
      CLOTH_SCALARS = 0x4d3bd00  # 4 x constraint stiffness, then 4 x the integrator's acceleration scale
      
      
      def load_eboot(path):
          eb = open(path, 'rb').read()
          phoff, phnum = struct.unpack_from('<Q', eb, 0x20)[0], struct.unpack_from('<H', eb, 0x38)[0]
          segs = []
          for i in range(phnum):
              t, fl, off, va, pa, fs, ms, al = struct.unpack_from('<IIQQQQQQ', eb, phoff + i * 56)
              if t == 1:
                  segs.append((va + 0x400000, off, fs))
      
          def orig(a):
              for va, off, fs in segs:
                  if va <= a < va + fs:
                      return eb[off + a - va]
              raise SystemExit('0x%x is not in the image' % a)
          return orig
      
      
      def list_image(root, name):
          md = next((m for m in root.iter('Metadata') if m.attrib.get('Name') == name and m.attrib.get('AppVer') == '01.09'),
                    None)
          if md is None:
              raise SystemExit('no "%s" for 01.09 in the list' % name)
          image = {}
          for line in md.find('PatchList'):
              a, ty, v = int(line.attrib['Address'], 16), line.attrib['Type'], line.attrib['Value']
              data = bytes.fromhex(v) if ty == 'bytes' else struct.pack('<I', int(v, 16)) if ty == 'bytes32' else None
              if data is None:
                  raise SystemExit('line type %s' % ty)
              for k, b in enumerate(data):
                  image[a + k] = b
          return image
      
      
      def table_bytes():
          """Every byte frame_rate.cpp's value tables write."""
          src = open(os.path.join(ROOT, 'src/engine/frame_rate.cpp')).read()
          ours = set()
          # kConstants: {0xADDR, 0xWAS, 0xNOW[, Kind::...]}
          for m in re.finditer(r'\{0x([0-9a-f]+), 0x[0-9a-f]+, 0x[0-9a-f]+[,}]', src):
              ours.update(range(int(m.group(1), 16), int(m.group(1), 16) + 4))
          # kCounts and kBytes: {0xADDR, N, ...}
          for m in re.finditer(r'\{0x([0-9a-f]+), (\d+), ', src):
              ours.update(range(int(m.group(1), 16), int(m.group(1), 16) + int(m.group(2))))
          return ours
      
      
      def changed_runs(image, orig, ours, also=()):
          """Runs of the bytes the list changes (and `also`), less the ones left out."""
          kept = sorted(a for a in set(a for a, b in image.items() if b != orig(a)) | set(also)
                        if a not in ours and not FRAME_MANAGER[0] <= a < FRAME_MANAGER[1]
                        and not any(lo <= a < hi for lo, hi, _ in EXCLUDE))
          # One site per run of changed bytes, joined across up to three unchanged bytes of the list's own
          # writes so a rewritten instruction stays whole.
          sites = []
          for a in kept:
              if sites and a - (sites[-1][0] + sites[-1][1]) <= 3 and all(x in image for x in range(sites[-1][0] + sites[-1][1], a)):
                  sites[-1][1] = a - sites[-1][0] + 1
              else:
                  sites.append([a, 1])
          return sites
      
      
      def write_inc(path, header, sites, image, orig):
          total = 0
          with open(path, 'w', newline='\n') as f:
              for line in header:
                  f.write('// ' + line + '\n')
              for a, n in sites:
                  old = bytes(orig(a + k) for k in range(n))
                  new = bytes(image.get(a + k, orig(a + k)) for k in range(n))
                  total += n
                  f.write('    {0x%08x, "%s", "%s"},\n' % (a, old.hex(), new.hex()))
              f.write('// %d sites, %d bytes\n' % (len(sites), total))
          print('%s: %d sites, %d bytes' % (path, len(sites), total))
      
      
      def rip_target(image, orig, at, size, disp_at):
          """The address a RIP-relative operand reads: the instruction at `at`, `size` bytes, its rel32 at disp_at."""
          rel = struct.unpack('<i', bytes(image.get(disp_at + k, orig(disp_at + k)) for k in range(4)))[0]
          return at + size + rel
      
      
      def main():
          if len(sys.argv) != 3:
              sys.exit(__doc__)
          root = ET.parse(sys.argv[1]).getroot()
          orig = load_eboot(sys.argv[2])
          ours = table_bytes()
          sixty = list_image(root, '60 FPS++')
          ninety = list_image(root, '90 FPS++')
      
          sites60 = changed_runs(sixty, orig, ours)
          write_inc(os.path.join(ROOT, 'src/engine/sixty_fps_sites.inc'),
                    ['Generated by tools/fps_sites.py from Kyo\'s "60 FPS++" list for 1.09 (shadPS4\'s patch list,',
                     'user/patches/shadPS4/Bloodborne.xml) and the 1.09 eboot: address (Binary Ninja), old bytes, new bytes.'],
                    sites60, sixty, orig)
      
          # What the 60 sites leave, byte for byte. A 90 site is a run of the bytes
          # the 90 list or a 60 site changes, kept when any byte of it is not what
          # the 60 sites leave there - also a byte the 60 list changes and the 90
          # list leaves as the eboot has it (0xb6fbd4's first: 0x70 at 90, 0x04 at
          # 60), which the 90 site writes back.
          after60 = {}
          for a, n in sites60:
              for k in range(n):
                  after60[a + k] = sixty.get(a + k, orig(a + k))
          sites90 = [s for s in changed_runs(ninety, orig, ours, also=[a for a, b in after60.items() if b != orig(a)])
                     if any(ninety.get(s[0] + k, orig(s[0] + k)) != after60.get(s[0] + k, orig(s[0] + k)) for k in range(s[1]))]
      
          sites90 = [x for x in sites90 if not any(lo <= x[0] < hi for lo, hi, _ in EXCLUDE_90)]
      
          # The cloth caves: each vmulps reads the stiffness scalars.
          caves = [a for a, n in sites90 if n == 25 and ninety.get(a) == 0xeb and ninety.get(a + 2) == 0xc5]
          for a in caves:
              if ninety.get(a + 3) != 0xf8:
                  raise SystemExit('cave 0x%x is not a vmulps' % a)
              t = rip_target(ninety, orig, a + 2, 8, a + 6)
              if t != CLOTH_SCALARS:
                  raise SystemExit('cave 0x%x reads 0x%x, not the stiffness scalars' % (a, t))
          if len(caves) != 6 or len(sites90) != 12:
              raise SystemExit('%d cloth caves (%d sites) in the 90 list, not 6 (12)' % (len(caves), len(sites90)))
          write_inc(os.path.join(ROOT, 'src/engine/ninety_fps_sites.inc'),
                    ['Generated by tools/fps_sites.py from Kyo\'s "90 FPS++" list for 1.09 (shadPS4\'s patch list,',
                     'user/patches/shadPS4/Bloodborne.xml, PatchVer 1.0) and the 1.09 eboot: the cloth\'s six stiffness',
                     'caves, written over the 60 sites above 60. Address (Binary Ninja), old bytes (the eboot\'s), new bytes.'],
                    sites90, ninety, orig)
      
      
      if __name__ == '__main__':
          main()

      #pragma once
      
      #include <cstdint>
      
      // Bloodborne 1.09 address spaces. Ghidra uses the
      // 0x800000000 image base; bbhost maps the ELF at GuestMemory::slide
      // (preferred 0x400000). ELF file VA = Ghidra VA - kGhidraBase.
      
      constexpr std::uint64_t kGhidraBase = 0x800000000ull;
      constexpr std::uint64_t kPreferredGuestSlide = 0x400000ull;
      
      // SHA-256 of eboot-109-decrypted.bin. Address-based patches and named
      // layouts apply only to this build.
      constexpr const char kEboot109Sha256[] =
          "941f887a562aae054fac35af8cc8f27cf075f3d4cc2e029fb5ae2a663aaa5ae7";
      
      inline constexpr std::uint64_t elf_from_ghidra(std::uint64_t ghidra_va) {
          return ghidra_va - kGhidraBase;
      }
      
      inline constexpr std::uint64_t guest_from_elf(std::uint64_t elf_va, std::uint64_t slide) {
          return slide + elf_va;
      }
      
      inline constexpr std::uint64_t guest_from_ghidra(std::uint64_t ghidra_va, std::uint64_t slide) {
          return guest_from_elf(elf_from_ghidra(ghidra_va), slide);
      }
```

```
      +def prepare_key(game, sku):
      +    digest = hashlib.sha256()
      +    modules = sorted((game / 'sce_module').iterdir()) if (game / 'sce_module').is_dir() else []
      +    # patches/redzone.json: the stores link_modules.py moves below the red zone (Intel 12th gen+).
      +    for path in [game / 'eboot.bin', game / 'sce_sys/param.sfo', *modules, *(SCRIPTS / s for s in PREPARE_SCRIPTS),
      +                 ROOT / 'patches' / 'redzone.json']:
      +        digest.update(path.name.encode('utf-8') + b'\0')
      +        if path.is_file():
      +            with path.open('rb') as f:
      +                while chunk := f.read(1 << 20):
      +                    digest.update(chunk)
      +        digest.update(b'\0')
      +    digest.update(f'sku={sku};check={os.environ.get("BB_SKIP_GAME_CHECK", "")}'.encode('utf-8'))
      +    return digest.hexdigest()
```

> **Fix 3 (heap expansion)**: The engine's `BB_DMEM_MB` (direct memory pool size) defaults to 5056 MiB, and is set to 9152 MiB only for scenes above 1080p (or when a patch enlarges the game's heaps). The phrase "expanded the game's internal heaps to 9152 MiB for resolutions above 1080p" — this is about the *direct memory pool* the engine maps for the guest (the game's memory). In bbhost, this corresponds to how much guest memory bbhost provides. Let me find bbhost's guest memory size. It's likely in `core/memory.cpp` or `hle/kernel.cpp` (the ~5 GB imported memory). The bbhost README says "the game's GPU-visible memory (about 5 GB)". So bbhost also gives ~5 GB. Porting: enlarge the guest memory for scenes >1080p. Hmm, but bbhost's memory model is different (memfd, imported). This may not map.

> Actually, the fix's essence: the game's internal heap (dmem) must be larger for a scene above 1080p, else the pool overflows and the game crashes at start. bbhost: does it size guest memory dynamically? Let me look at core/memory.cpp.
> 
> **Fix 1 (hang guard)**: In the texture cache GC, images accessed within the last BB_GC_RECENT_FRAMES (default 48) frames are never freed/downloaded, and DeleteImage'd images' Vulkan objects are kept in a graveyard for BB_IMAGE_FREE_DELAY_FRAMES (default 32) before reclaiming. This prevents freeing a texture still in use → GPU hang/device lost.
> 
> In bbhost, texture lifetime: `textures_retire` defers freeing until the command processor has retired submitted work. bbhost uses submission serials, so in-use textures aren't freed. So the hang guard may be largely present. BUT the specific bug (a texture bound but not referenced by the retired serial yet) — bbhost's scheme is arguably stronger.
> 
> **Fix 2 (VRAM cleanup)**: Above 85% of the VRAM budget, copies unused for 30s leave VRAM (10s above 90%); GPU-written data stays; a returning block brings its 2 MiB group. bbhost has `evict_cold_surfaces_locked` (evicts textures not bound for a while when video memory is low).       bool guest_alloc(GuestMemory* mem, std::uint64_t slide, std::size_t size) {
```
          mem->slide = slide;
          mem->size = size;
      #if defined(_WIN32)
          // The preferred slide when it is free (it is not under wine, whose
          // process heap sits there before main runs), else anywhere below 4 GiB:
          // every address-based patch converts through the real slide.
          const std::size_t round = (size + 0xffff) & ~std::size_t(0xffff);
          mem->base = VirtualAlloc(reinterpret_cast<void*>(slide), round, MEM_RESERVE | MEM_COMMIT, PAGE_READWRITE);
          if (!mem->base) {
              // The fixed fallback window kernel.cpp reserved (0x300000000), else anywhere below 4 GiB.
              mem->base = win_vm_commit(reinterpret_cast<void*>(0x300000000ull), round, PAGE_READWRITE, 0xffffffffull);
              if (!mem->base) mem->base = win_vm_commit(nullptr, round, PAGE_READWRITE, 0xffffffffull);
              if (mem->base) {
                  mem->slide = reinterpret_cast<std::uint64_t>(mem->base);
                  host_log("guest slide is 0x%llx (preferred 0x%llx was taken)", static_cast<unsigned long long>(mem->slide),
                           static_cast<unsigned long long>(slide));
              }
          }
          if (!mem->base) {
              host_log("VirtualAlloc(0x%llx, %zu) failed: %lu",
                       static_cast<unsigned long long>(slide), size, GetLastError());
              return false;
          }
      #else
          mem->base = mmap(reinterpret_cast<void*>(slide), size,
                           PROT_READ | PROT_WRITE, MAP_PRIVATE | MAP_ANONYMOUS, -1, 0);
          if (mem->base == MAP_FAILED) {
              host_log("mmap(%zu) failed", size);
              mem->base = nullptr;
              return false;
          }
          if (mem->base != reinterpret_cast<void*>(slide)) {
              mem->slide = reinterpret_cast<std::uint64_t>(mem->base);
              host_log("guest slide is 0x%llx (preferred 0x%llx was a hint)",
                       static_cast<unsigned long long>(mem->slide),
                       static_cast<unsigned long long>(slide));
          }
      #endif
          std::memset(mem->base, 0, size);
          return true;
      }
      
      void guest_free(GuestMemory* mem) {
          if (!mem->base) {
              return;
          }
      #if defined(_WIN32)
          VirtualFree(mem->base, 0, MEM_RELEASE);
      #else
          munmap(mem->base, mem->size);
      #endif
          mem->base = nullptr;
      }
      
      #if defined(_WIN32)
      static bool win_protect(void* p, std::size_t size, DWORD prot) {
          DWORD old = 0;
          return VirtualProtect(p, size, prot, &old) != 0;
      }
      #endif
      
      // The pages guest_keep_writable keeps writable (host addresses), and their
      // protection given back after a change that covered one.
      static std::mutex g_kept_mu;
      static std::vector<std::uintptr_t> g_kept;
      
      static void protect_page_rwx(std::uintptr_t page) {
      #if defined(_WIN32)
          win_protect(reinterpret_cast<void*>(page), 0x1000, PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE);
      #else
          mprotect(reinterpret_cast<void*>(page), 0x1000, PROT_READ | PROT_WRITE | PROT_EXEC);
      #endif
      }
      
      static void keep_kept_writable(const void* p, std::size_t size) {
          std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(g_kept_mu);
          const auto lo = reinterpret_cast<std::uintptr_t>(p), hi = lo + size;
          for (const std::uintptr_t page : g_kept) {
              if (page < hi && page + 0x1000 > lo) protect_page_rwx(page);
          }
      }
      
      void guest_keep_writable(GuestMemory* mem, std::uint64_t va) {
          const auto page = reinterpret_cast<std::uintptr_t>(guest_ptr(*mem, va & ~0xfffull));
          {
              std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(g_kept_mu);
              bool have = false;
              for (const std::uintptr_t k : g_kept) have = have || k == page;
              if (!have) g_kept.push_back(page);
          }
          protect_page_rwx(page);
      }
      
      bool guest_protect_rx(GuestMemory* mem, std::uint64_t va, std::size_t size) {
          void* p = guest_ptr(*mem, va);
      #if defined(_WIN32)
          if (!win_protect(p, size, PAGE_EXECUTE_READ)) {
              host_log("PAGE_EXECUTE_READ failed at 0x%llx", static_cast<unsigned long long>(va));
              return false;
          }
      #else
          if (mprotect(p, size, PROT_READ | PROT_EXEC) != 0) {
              host_log("mprotect RX failed at 0x%llx", static_cast<unsigned long long>(va));
              return false;
          }
      #endif
          keep_kept_writable(p, size);
          return true;
      }
      
      bool guest_protect_rw(GuestMemory* mem, std::uint64_t va, std::size_t size) {
          void* p = guest_ptr(*mem, va);
      #if defined(_WIN32)
          const bool ok = win_protect(p, size, PAGE_READWRITE);
      #else
          const bool ok = mprotect(p, size, PROT_READ | PROT_WRITE) == 0;
      #endif
          keep_kept_writable(p, size);
          return ok;
      }
      
      bool guest_protect_rwx(GuestMemory* mem, std::uint64_t va, std::size_t size) {
          void* p = guest_ptr(*mem, va);
      #if defined(_WIN32)
          return win_protect(p, size, PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE);
      #else
          return mprotect(p, size, PROT_READ | PROT_WRITE | PROT_EXEC) == 0;
      #endif
      }
```

```
      // Render targets come from SprjMemory's GFX_GraphicsPrivate heap (size
      // table 0x4b36d40, row 1 - the mode the game runs in - entry 3: 0x8ef00000,
      // 2287 MiB; CSGraphicsPrivateAllocator sends 1 MiB and up there and the rest
      // to GFX_GraphicsPrivateB, entry 4, 886 MiB, each falling back to the
      // other). That is the stock 1920x1080's budget, and streaming fills it as an
      // area loads - so targets made larger later have nowhere to come from; the
      // allocator returns null and a pass writes through it (a null read in the
      // light pass, a heap overrun, a jump into data) or keeps a freed pointer
      // (unfit_scene_ctx). Measured with the allocator's own counters (vtable
      // 0x57aec90; +0x30 free, +0x38 largest block) in Central Yharnam: each size
      // costs about 270 MiB per million pixels past 1080p (1680 for 3840x2160), and
      // the stock game leaves ~750 MiB free at 1080p. So the heap grows by that
      // cost and a margin for the largest size the run can reach.
      //
      // The heaps are carved from the 6 GiB of direct memory in table order, with
      // little to spare: +1 GiB fits, but +2 GiB left no room for
      // GFX_GraphicsPrivateB (it was not made, and its allocations went to the
      // grown heap - nothing gained) and +3 GiB failed at the start. So past 1 GiB
      // the direct memory grows by the same amount (hle_kernel_set_dmem_size). The
      // memory is the PC's but pinned for the GPU, so a
      // run is not grown for sizes it will not reach: a run with live changes
      // covers 3440x1440's pixels (+1088 MiB, about v0.2.5's +1 GiB) or its
      // starting size's when larger, and a change to more pixels than that applies
      // when the game next starts (live_resolution_can). A GPU with little memory
      // (host_gpu_memory_tight: a Steam Deck) covers 1080p's, the stock heap: the
      // heap is imported for the GPU whole, and the gigabyte more did not fit.
      constexpr std::uint64_t kPx1080 = 1920ull * 1080ull, kPxLiveDefault = 3440ull * 1440ull;
      constexpr std::uint64_t kFitsInDmemMiB = 1024;  // growth the stock 6 GiB of direct memory holds
      std::uint64_t g_live_max_px = ~0ull;  // the most pixels a live change may have
      
      std::uint64_t gfx_heap_more_mib(std::uint64_t px) {
          if (px <= kPx1080) return 0;
          const double mp = static_cast<double>(px - kPx1080) / 1e6;
          const auto mib = static_cast<std::uint64_t>(std::ceil((270.0 * mp + 256.0) / 64.0)) * 64;
          return std::max(mib, kFitsInDmemMiB);
      }

          const char* e = std::getenv("BBHOST_GFX_HEAP_MORE_MIB");

          std::uint64_t more = given ? std::strtoull(e, nullptr, 10) : gfx_heap_more_mib(px);

          host_log("resolution: GFX_GraphicsPrivate %llu -> %llu MiB, direct memory %llu MiB - live changes up to %.1f million pixels",
```

```
      // The video memory budget, followed as it changes (vram_headroom): the

      std::mutex g_budget_mu;
      std::int64_t g_budget_read_ms = -(1ll << 40);
      std::int64_t g_budget_room = 0;            // heapBudget - heapUsage when read
      std::uint64_t g_budget_local_at_read = 0;  // bb_memory_local_bytes() then

      std::uint64_t image_heap_vram_free_locked() {
          std::uint64_t free = 0;
          for (const HeapBlock& b : g_heap) {
              if (b.memory != VK_NULL_HANDLE && g.mem_props.memoryTypes[b.type].heapIndex == g.local_heap) free += kHeapBlock - b.used;
          }
          return free;
      }
      
      bool image_memory_in_vram(const ImageMemory& m) {
          return m.type >= g.mem_props.memoryTypeCount || g.mem_props.memoryTypes[m.type].heapIndex == g.local_heap;

      std::int64_t vram_headroom() {
          std::uint64_t limit = 0, used = 0;
          if (bb_memory_test_limited(&limit, &used)) return static_cast<std::int64_t>(limit) - static_cast<std::int64_t>(used);
          const std::uint64_t local = bb_memory_local_bytes();
          if (!g.has_memory_budget || !g.phys) return static_cast<std::int64_t>(g.local_budget) - static_cast<std::int64_t>(local);
          std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lk(g_budget_mu);
          const std::int64_t now = steady_ms();
          if (now - g_budget_read_ms >= 100) {
              VkPhysicalDeviceMemoryBudgetPropertiesEXT mb{VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_PHYSICAL_DEVICE_MEMORY_BUDGET_PROPERTIES_EXT};
              VkPhysicalDeviceMemoryProperties2 mp{VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_PHYSICAL_DEVICE_MEMORY_PROPERTIES_2};
              mp.pNext = &mb;
              vkGetPhysicalDeviceMemoryProperties2(g.phys, &mp);
              g_budget_room = static_cast<std::int64_t>(mb.heapBudget[g.local_heap]) - static_cast<std::int64_t>(mb.heapUsage[g.local_heap]);
              g_budget_local_at_read = bb_memory_local_bytes();
              g_budget_read_ms = now;
              return g_budget_room;
          }
          return g_budget_room - (static_cast<std::int64_t>(local) - static_cast<std::int64_t>(g_budget_local_at_read));
      }

      // fails, as before.
      void vram_reserve_init() {
          const char* e = std::getenv("BBHOST_VRAM_RESERVE_MB");
          const bool given = e && *e;
          const std::uint64_t mib = given ? std::strtoull(e, nullptr, 10) : (g.integrated || g.tight ? 0 : 512);

          if (g_vram_reserve)
```

```
      // it, else the driver's budget for the heap less its usage
      // (VK_EXT_memory_budget, read at most every 100 ms), else the budget at the
      // start less what our allocations hold there. Any thread.
      std::int64_t vram_headroom();
```

```
      // 10 s - a card past 90% fills faster than a 30 s sweep keeps up with, while
      // one merely past 85% can give a texture another half minute. The reserve

      // deletion) it may be freed in. A draw may still read a texture the frame that
      // used it recorded, and a deleted image's Vulkan objects outlive its
      // unregistration; with either count unmet the sweep leaves it. Frames are the
      // GPU's own timeline, so a long frame (a hitch, a load) cannot age a texture
      // out from under a submission still reading it.
```

```json
  "content": "# FIXES-LOG\n\nStability and crash fixes adapted from **BloodBorneButPc** (a Windows fork of the\nshadPS4/bbport engine) into **bbhost** (this native translation layer).\n\nThe two projects do not share source, so each fix is re-expressed in bbhost's own\narchitecture under the same switch name that gates it in BloodBorneButPc. Where\nbbhost already solved the same problem another way, that is noted rather than\nduplicated. Long-session VRAM accumulation and the launch-time heap overflow are\nthe crashes these target.\n\n## GPU hang guard - textures freed while still in use\n\n- **Source:** `BB_GC_RECENT_FRAMES` (default 48), `BB_IMAGE_FREE_DELAY_FRAMES`\n  (default 32) in BloodBorneButPc's texture cache.\n- **Files:** `src/host/textures.cpp`.\n- **Change:** each surface records the video flip of its last use\n  (`Surface::used_flip`, stamped wherever `used_ms` is). The cold-texture sweep\n  (`evict_cold_surfaces_locked`) and the reused-memory retire\n  (`textures_retire_reused_locked`) now skip any surface used or deleted within\n  `max(BB_GC_RECENT_FRAMES, BB_IMAGE_FREE_DELAY_FRAMES)` flips. Frames are the\n  GPU's own timeline, so a long frame (a hitch, a load) can no longer age a\n  texture out from under a submission still reading it - the\n  stalled-then-device-lost class of crash.\n- **Rationale:** bbhost already defers a deleted image's Vulkan objects to\n  submission retirement (`defer_destroy_image`), so the \"outlive unregistration\"\n  half is already covered; the frame floor adds the part it lacked - a texture\n  the just-recorded frame used is never a candidate for freeing.\n\n## VRAM cleanup - accumulation over a long session\n\n- **Source:** `BB_VRAM_PRESSURE_PERCENT` (default 85), `BB_VRAM_IDLE_SECONDS`\n  (default 30; 10 s above 90% of the driver's budget) in BloodBorneButPc.\n- **Files:** `src/host/textures.cpp`, `src/host/gpu.cpp`,\n  `src/host/gpu_internal.h`.\n- **Change:** `evict_cold_surfaces_locked` now measures pressure as a share of\n  the driver's budget (new accessor `vram_budget_bytes()`) and:\n  - triggers once usage reaches `BB_VRAM_PRESSURE_PERCENT` of that budget, in\n    addition to bbhost's existing reserve-and-full-heap trigger;\n  - frees only textures idle for `BB_VRAM_IDLE_SECONDS`, dropping that to 10 s\n    once the budget is 90% used.\n  - surfaces a shader or copy wrote are still never evicted (bbhost holds state\n    the guest memory underneath does not), matching BloodBorneButPc keeping\n    GPU-written blocks resident.\n- **Rationale:** the original default idle of 20 s (via `BBHOST_VRAM_EVICT_S`,\n  still honored, `=0` off) is kept as a fallback; the percentage line lets the\n  sweep start before the reserve is hit and sweep harder as the card fills.\n\n## Direct memory pool - launch crash on a large scene\n\n- **Source:** `BB_DMEM_MB` (BloodBorneButPc gives a scene above 1080p the\n  9152 MiB pool instead of 5056 MiB).\n- **Files:** `src/hle/kernel.cpp`.\n- **Change:** `BB_DMEM_MB` names the direct memory the game is told it has (the\n  stock 6 GiB otherwise), clamped to the window reserved for it (7.75 GiB).\n- **Rationale:** bbhost already grows the game's GFX heap and its direct memory\n  for a scene above 1080p (`grow_gfx_heap` / `hle_kernel_set_dmem_size`,\n  `engine/live_resolution.cpp`), so the >1080p policy is present; the switch\n  exposes the pool size itself, and its 7.75 GiB window is the ceiling that\n  BloodBorneButPc's 9152 MiB meets only as far as the window allows.\n\n## Already present in bbhost (not re-ported)\n\n- Crash reports for host faults on a game thread (Linux `SIGSEGV` handler,\n  `main.cpp`; `host/win_crash.cpp` on Windows).\n- Write faults at the end of a GPU mapping handled, unclaimed faults on guest\n  pages handed access back (`core/write_watch.cpp`).\n- Unknown texture formats read as `VK_FORMAT_UNDEFINED` and are skipped instead\n  of aborting; a lost/out-of-date swapchain is recreated\n  (`host/window.cpp`).\n- Audio output follows the device's real rate (`host/audio.cpp`).\n- Patch write sites are checked against the expected bytes before any is\n  written (`engine/patch_manifest.cpp`).\n- VM/launcher-only items (Windows error 1450 memory check, 10 GB pool, region\n  patch prompt) do not apply to bbhost's Linux path.\n"
}
```

Done. Here's what I found and did.

## Reconnaissance

The two repos are independent Bloodborne-on-PC projects with **no shared source**: `BloodBorneButPc`'s engine is a Windows fork of the shadPS4/bbport codebase (its work lives in `engine/bbhost-changes.patch`), while `bbhost-nocrash` is droogie's native translation layer. So a literal patch doesn't apply — each fix has to be re-expressed in bbhost's architecture. I confirmed the BloodBorneButPc README stability list is gated per-fix by named switches, so I used those as the map.

I verified the two projects share the same address space by matching a site both fix (the 12-second respawn `je`): `0x1938b59` in BloodBorneButPc = `0x1d38b59` in bbhost (a `+0x400000` offset). That confirmed how to read any BloodBorneButPc site.

Crucially, most of the 16 listed fixes **already exist in bbhost** (crash reports + Linux SIGSEGV handler, write-fault handling, unknown-format fallback, swapchain recreation, audio rate following the device, patch-site byte checks, and its own `evict_cold_surfaces_locked`). The three you prioritized exist only partly, so I ported the missing parts.

## Ported (3 commits on `awakechan-fixes`, no attribution)

1. **GPU hang guard** (`e405ffd`) — `src/host/textures.cpp`: surfaces now record the video flip of their last use; the cold-texture sweep and the reused-memory retire never free a surface used within `BB_GC_RECENT_FRAMES` (48) flips or deleted within `BB_IMAGE_FREE_DELAY_FRAMES` (32). Frames are the GPU's timeline, so a long frame can't free a texture still being read. (bbhost already defers deletions to submission retirement, so only the frame floor was missing.)
2. **VRAM cleanup** (`e405ffd`) — added `vram_budget_bytes()` and made the sweep trigger at `BB_VRAM_PRESSURE_PERCENT` (85) of the driver's budget, freeing textures idle for `BB_VRAM_IDLE_SECONDS` (30 s, dropping to 10 s above 90%), alongside bbhost's reserve trigger. GPU-written surfaces are still never evicted (matches keeping GPU-written blocks resident).
3. **Direct memory pool** (`5773be0`) — `src/hle/kernel.cpp` honors `BB_DMEM_MB` for the game's direct memory pool. Note bbhost already grows the GFX heap and direct memory for scenes >1080p, and its reserved window caps at 7.75 GiB, so BloodBorneButPc's 9152 MiB is honored only up to that window.

Plus `FIXES-LOG.md` (`0cd4e97`) recording each change (files + rationale) and the items already present.

## Limitations

- Per your constraint, **nothing was built or tested**. The edits use only existing bbhost helpers, but they are unverified against a compiler — build before relying on them.
- `BB_IMAGE_FREE_DELAY_FRAMES` is implemented as a shared frame floor with `BB_GC_RECENT_FRAMES` (bbhost's deferral already covers the "objects outlive unregistration" half); it is not a separate graveyard.

````
  content: |
      # bbhost
      
      bbhost is a translation layer that runs Bloodborne on Windows and Linux. The
      game's own 1.09 executable runs unmodified on the PC's x86-64 CPU; bbhost
      answers its calls into the PS4's system libraries with PC implementations, and
      recompiles its GPU work, GCN shaders and the engine's draw calls, for Vulkan.
      The aim is a definitive PC version of the game - the original, intact, with
      what a PC release would add: any resolution and aspect ratio, 60 fps and
      beyond, keyboard and mouse, proper settings, mods and online play.
      
      ![Cainhurst Castle](docs/images/cainhurst.jpg)
      
      bbhost contains no game code or data. You need your own copy of the game: a
      dump with the 1.09 update and its decrypted executable.
      
      ## Why not emulation
      
      The PS4 has an x86-64 CPU, so the game's code does not need to be translated
      to run on a PC - it needs a place to live. bbhost provides that place:
      
      - **The CPU side runs natively.** bbhost loads the game's ELF executable,
        relocates it, links its imports to its own implementations and starts it.
        The game's code runs at full speed on the host CPU, with no interpreter or
        recompiler involved.
      - **The PS4's system libraries are reimplemented** for the PC: files and
        saves, threads and memory, input, audio, movies, networking and the
        PlayStation Network calls the online features use - every one of the 660
        named functions the game imports.
      - **Graphics are being moved from emulation to native code.** The game's
        renderer was written for the PS4's GPU: it builds command buffers for an AMD
        GCN GPU and ships GCN shader programs. bbhost hooks FromSoftware's own
        graphics layer instead, so draws are built directly from the engine's objects,
        and decompiles the shaders to typed, structured SPIR-V. The
        status table below shows what is native today and what still goes through
        the emulated GPU command processor.
      - **Game functions are being rewritten as source**, one at a time, each checked
        against the original, so the game can be fixed and extended where a patch
        would not reach.
      
      ## Features
      
      | | |
      |---|---|
      | ![Yharnam in 21:9](docs/images/yharnam-ultrawide.jpg) | **Any resolution, ultrawide included.** 21:9 and 32:9 with a wider field of view and the HUD where it belongs, and the resolution can be changed while playing. FSR 1 upscaling for slower GPUs. |
      | ![PC Graphics settings](docs/images/pc-graphics.jpg) | **Settings in the game's own menus.** The System menu gains PC Settings, PC Graphics, PC Effects, PC Controls, PC Camera and Key Bindings, drawn in the game's style: anti-aliasing, ambient occlusion, shadow distance, fog, motion blur, field of view, frame cap and more. |
      
      - **60 fps**, with the game's timing corrected so physics, animation and
        cutscenes run at the right speed. Higher frame caps keep the game's logic at
        60.
      - **Keyboard and mouse**: mouse camera, a pointer in every menu, rebindable
        keys, and button prompts that show the keys.
      - **PC enhancements** that can be switched off for the game as it shipped: the
        Hunter's Dream mirror opens the character appearance editor (a feature cut
        from the release), "Rebirth in the Nightmare" at the Altar of
        Despair lets you redistribute your levels, and the late areas allow two
        invaders, as the chalice dungeons do.
      - **Online play** through a private server: co-op, invasions, messages,
        bloodstains and summon signs between bbhost players.
      - **Mods** without touching the game files: replacement files, param tables
        edited by field name, byte patches as data, and native plugins - a
        randomizer (items, shops and enemies), a boss rush, gameplay mutators and
        the developers' own debug menu ship with it.
      - **A setup window** that finds and checks your game files, and the Steam Deck
        as a supported device.
      
      ![The setup window](docs/images/setup-window.png)
      
      ## Status
      
      The game is playable on Windows and Linux: the world, its bosses and online
      sessions. What runs on native code and what is still emulated:
      
      | Part | State |
      |---|---|
      | Game logic (CPU) | the game's own code, running natively |
      | System libraries | reimplemented by bbhost: all 660 named imports the game binds |
      | Window, input, audio, movies, saves | native (SDL3, Vulkan, FFmpeg, LibAtrac9) |
      | Online | native sockets and HTTP against a private server; peer-to-peer UDP with NAT traversal |
      | Draws | native: each draw is built from the engine's graphics objects; the command buffer only marks its place in the stream |
      | Post-processing (YEBIS) | native: every stage's resources built by bbhost |
      | Tessellation | native: the host GPU's own tessellation stages, all three stages lifted; the game's mesh hulls draw as one native pipeline, without the PS4's on-chip ring |
      | Shaders | decompiled ("lifted") from GCN to typed, structured SPIR-V when the game creates them: every shader the game ships except compute (3,206 of 3,209 pixel shader programs, all vertex and tessellation programs; 100% of draws at the 12 measured places, see [docs/rendering.md](docs/rendering.md#shader-lifting)). Compute shaders and the few programs the lifter refuses are still translated by bbhost's GCN compiler |
      | Frame pacing | native: the game's frame-time manager runs as bbhost source; 30, 60, 90, 120 or uncapped, with the game's per-frame steps following real time |
      | Compute dispatches, labels, fences | still emulated: run through bbhost's command processor, which walks the game's PM4 command buffers; GPU particle counters are kept natively, as per-buffer counters |
      | Texture memory | the game's tiled textures are detiled on the GPU; changes are tracked by watching the game's writes |
      
      Known issues:
      
      - Compute work still goes through the emulated command processor, and the
        game's GPU-visible memory (about 5 GB) stays imported into Vulkan, because
        some shaders still read it through page-table walks.
      - A new GPU particle system's counter can start uninitialized; bbhost clamps
        such a dispatch to nothing rather than hang.
      - Slow poison runs twice as fast at 60 fps.
      - A new area compiles its pipelines on first sight, which can cause short
        hitches the first time it is visited.
      - About one in four first summons fail and have to be repeated.
      - The cause of a GPU hang reported on an AMD RX 580 (Polaris) under Windows is
        not yet known.
      
      See [docs/rendering.md](docs/rendering.md) for the graphics in detail and
      [docs/decomp.md](docs/decomp.md) for which game functions have been rewritten.
      
      ## Getting started
      
      1. Get the game files: a dump of Bloodborne with the 1.09 update copied over
         it (or kept beside it as `CUSA00900-UPDATE`, the way shadPS4 keeps it), and
         the 1.09 `eboot.bin` decrypted to an ELF (SHA-256
         `941f887a562aae054fac35af8cc8f27cf075f3d4cc2e029fb5ae2a663aaa5ae7`).
      2. Download a release for Windows or Linux, or build bbhost yourself.
      3. Start `bbhost`. The setup window asks for the two paths, checks them and
         saves them; press Play.
      
      [docs/running.md](docs/running.md) covers the configuration, the controls,
      saves, logs and troubleshooting.
      
      ## Building
      
      ```sh
      cmake -S . -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo
      cmake --build build -j
      ./build/bbhost
      ```
      
      Linux builds natively with GCC or Clang; the Windows executable is
      cross-compiled from Linux with Clang and mingw-w64 (MSVC cannot express the
      calling conventions involved). Dependencies, the Windows build, tests and
      packaging are in [docs/building.md](docs/building.md).
      
      ## Documentation
      
      - [Running](docs/running.md) - configuration, controls, saves, troubleshooting, the debug menu
      - [Building](docs/building.md) - Linux, Windows, tests, packages
      - [Rendering](docs/rendering.md) - how the graphics work, and what is native
      - [Decompilation](docs/decomp.md) - game functions rewritten as source
      - [Modding](docs/modding.md) - replacement files, params, patches
      - [Plugins](docs/plugins.md) - the plugin API and the official plugins
      - [Online](docs/online.md) - the private server and peer-to-peer play
      
      ## Project layout
      
      ```
      src/
        main.cpp       start-up and the main loop
        core/          ELF loading, relocation and import binding, TLS, configuration
        hle/           the PS4 system libraries: kernel, files, threads, audio, video,
                       network, NP, Gnm and the GPU command processor
        host/          the PC side: window, input, audio, Vulkan renderer, textures,
                       menus, overlay, plugins, update check
        gcn/           GCN shader decoding, translation and lifting to SPIR-V
        engine/        named engine structures and the features built on them:
                       frame rate, live resolution, menus, params, event flags,
                       PC enhancements
        decomp/        game functions rewritten as source
        net/           the private server's session service, accounts, STUN
        replay/        draw capture comparison
      include/         the plugin API and the engine SDK (layouts, params, symbols)
      plugins/         the official plugins (randomizer, boss rush, mutators) and an example
      patches/         byte patches as data
      res/             the Windows exe's icon and version details
      tests/           unit tests (ctest)
      tools/           shader tools, format tools, test drivers and packaging scripts
      third_party/     LibAtrac9, Dear ImGui, Monocypher
      ```
      
      ## Roadmap
      
      - **Graphics, native throughout**: compute dispatches, clears and copies built
        from the engine's objects like the draws, so the PM4 command processor can be
        retired; resources identified by the engine's own objects rather than guest
        addresses; compute shaders lifted too; the lifted SPIR-V emitted as HLSL and
        compiled with DXC.
      - **Decompilation**: more of the engine rewritten as source, starting with the
        systems mods and fixes need most.
      - **Performance**: a steady 60 fps everywhere on mid-range hardware, and
        headroom above it.
      - **PC features**: more settings, better keyboard and mouse handling in every
        screen, and more restored content.
      
      ## License
      
      bbhost is free software, licensed under the GNU General Public License,
      version 3 or later (see [LICENSE](LICENSE)). The third-party code in
      `third_party/` and `src/host/shaders/fsr1/` keeps its own licenses. The debug

      and 7x14, which are in the public domain.
      
      Bloodborne is a trademark of Sony Interactive Entertainment. bbhost is not
      affiliated with or endorsed by Sony or FromSoftware, and contains none of the

      ## Acknowledgements
      
      - Community work bbhost builds on: illusion's Skip Intro, Lance McDonald's

        files), and Kyo's 60 FPS++ timing list (built into the frame-rate code).
      - [shadPS4](https://github.com/shadps4-emu/shadPS4), a reference for the PS4's

      - SDL3, Vulkan, FFmpeg, SPIRV-Tools, LibAtrac9, Dear ImGui, Monocypher and
````

````
  content: |
      # Building
      
      bbhost builds with CMake on x86-64 Linux. The Windows executable is
      cross-compiled from Linux with Clang and the mingw-w64 runtime; MSVC is not
      supported, because the host needs `__attribute__((sysv_abi))` to call into
      the game's code.
      
      ## Linux
      
      Requirements:
      
      - Clang or GCC with C++20, CMake 3.20+, Ninja or Make
      - libstdc++ 14 or newer
      - recent Vulkan headers (Ubuntu 24.04's 1.3.275 are too old; CI uses 1.4.350)
        and the Vulkan loader
      - zlib (required); libcurl, SDL3, ffmpeg (libavcodec, libavformat, libavutil,
        libswscale, libswresample) and SPIRV-Tools are optional but needed for a
        usable build: networking, windowing, audio, movies and shader optimisation
        are compiled out without them
      
      On Arch Linux the packages are `vulkan-headers vulkan-icd-loader sdl3 ffmpeg
      curl zlib spirv-tools`. On Ubuntu 24.04 the distribution's Vulkan headers and
      SDL are too old; `tools/ci_build.sh` builds them into a prefix and is the
      reference for a from-scratch build there.
      
      ```sh
      cmake -S . -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo
      cmake --build build -j
      ```
      
      The result is `build/bbhost`, plus the official plugins in `build/plugins/`
      and the developer tools (`gcn2spv`, `gcndis`, `drawreplay`, ...).
      
      `-DBBHOST_RELEASE=ON` makes a release build, which by default checks at start
      whether a newer release is out and offers to open its page in the browser.
      
      ## Windows (cross-compiled)
      
      Requirements on the Linux machine: Clang, lld and llvm tools, the mingw-w64
      sysroot (`x86_64-w64-mingw32`), and wine for running the tests and the smoke
      run.
      
      ```sh
      tools/win_deps.sh       # once: zlib, SDL3, libcurl (schannel) and ffmpeg for the target
      cmake -S . -B build-win -G Ninja -DCMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE=cmake/mingw-toolchain.cmake \
            -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=$PWD/build/win-deps/prefix -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo
      cmake --build build-win
      ```
      
      The result is `build-win/bbhost.exe`, a single static executable that needs
      only the system DLLs and the GPU driver's `vulkan-1.dll`. It is linked at a
      fixed base (`0x600000000`) because the game's memory windows are reserved at
      fixed addresses before anything else runs.
      
      `tools/win_syntax_check.sh <file>` checks one source file for the Windows
      target while editing; `tools/win_tests.sh` builds and runs the low-level host
      tests (calling-convention thunks, TLS, `setjmp`/`longjmp`, `va_list`) under
      wine.
      
      ## Tests
      
      ```sh
      cd build && ctest --output-on-failure
      ```
      
      Tests that read game files skip unless `BBHOST_APP0` names the game folder
      (the one that contains `dvdroot_ps4`). No game file is ever part of the
      repository.
      
      `cmake --build build --target smoke` boots the game to the title screen and
      checks the log for crashes and unimplemented system calls; it needs a
      configured `bbhost.toml` with the game paths (see [running.md](running.md)).
      The Windows build has the same target under wine (`build-win`, target
      `smoke`).
      
      `build/gcn2spv --check <dvdroot_ps4>/shader/*.dcx` translates and validates
      every shader in the game's shader bundles.
      
      ## Packages
      
      | Target or script | Produces |
      |---|---|
      | `cmake --build build-win --target package-win` | `build/win/bbhost-win-<rev>.zip`, and the unstripped `.debug.exe` for symbolising crash reports |
      | `tools/package_linux.sh <bbhost> <outdir>` | a Linux tarball (built with `tools/linux_portable_build.sh` for a portable binary) |
      | `tools/package_steamdeck.sh` | the Linux package with the Steam Deck's settings |
      | `tools/package_plugins.sh` | the official plugins with their signatures |
      | `tools/package_playtest.sh` | tester kits for a playtest on a dev server, built by hand |
      
      The release workflow (`.github/workflows/release.yml`) builds the Windows,
      Linux and Steam Deck packages from a `v*` tag, signs `SHA256SUMS` and the
      official plugins with the release key, and publishes the release that bbhost's
      update check looks for. The bare executables it attaches are named the same in
      every release (`bbhost.exe`, and `bbhost` for Linux), so a shortcut or a Steam
      entry pointing at one keeps working when it is replaced. The packages pick no
      server, so they play on the live server (`https://thehuntersdream.com`),
      bbhost's default; `tools/check_release_bundle.sh` fails a release whose
      packages would go anywhere else, or that carries a playtest kit.
      
      ## Continuous integration
      
      `.github/workflows/build.yml` runs `tools/ci_build.sh` (a Linux build from
      scratch on Ubuntu 24.04, with the tests) and the Windows cross build on every
      push and pull request.
````

````
- path: README.md
  content: |
      # Bloodborne PC
      
      Bloodborne on Windows in one package: my launcher and my own engine. You only need your own game dump.
      
      **Community:** [join the Discord](https://discord.gg/d3Uv3Cfr5x) for help, news, co-op partners and beta feedback.
      
      **No game files are included.** Bring a decrypted Bloodborne dump (CUSA03173 or another
      region) with update 1.09.
      
      ## Install
      
      1. Download `BloodbornePC-<version>-win64.zip` from
         [Releases](https://github.com/Awakenchan/BloodBorneButPc/releases) and extract it anywhere.
      2. Run `Bloodborne Launcher.exe` and choose your game folder (the one with `eboot.bin`).
      3. Press **Play**.
      
      The launcher updates itself from the Releases page.
      
      ## Features
      
      - **Play**: game folder check, player profiles (each with its own saves and trophies), automatic save backups with restore, save import from shadPS4 or another port, DLC folder (The Old Hunters on base-game dumps), session summary. `Bloodborne.exe` starts the game straight away with your settings (for a shortcut or Steam).
      - **Display**: resolution (or your display's own, any shape), fullscreen, widescreen (21:9, 32:9), native HDR, 30 to 144 FPS or uncapped, in-game menu in 9 languages.
      - **Graphics**: FSR 4, FSR 3, DLSS and DLAA, TAA, sharpening, occlusion culling, picture and camera tuning, FPS counter (frame rate, frame time, upscaler), best settings for your PC.
      - **Controls**: keyboard and mouse for every action, the game's button prompts shown as your keys or as Xbox buttons, controller remapping, stick options, live controller detection, shareable profiles.
      - **Cheats**: Blood Vials and Quicksilver Bullets (infinite or a set amount), infinite consumables and stamina, stealth, no weapon wear, firearm range, keep echoes on death, echo multiplier. Each can be turned off.
      - **Trophies**: all 40, completion rate, in-game notification, reset.
      - **More**: mods and patches, online (The Hunter's Dream for messages and bloodstains; co-op with bbhost players on The Hunter's Dream through [bbbridge](https://github.com/MaskZeus/bbbridge-bbport-online-tool) by MaskZeus, signed in with Discord, or on a shadNet server), game log, crash helper with safe mode, memory check before starting, stable or beta updates with a version selector.
      
      ### Control profile format
      
      ```json
      {
        "format": "bbport-controls",
        "version": 2,
        "name": "Mouse focus",
        "author": "you",
        "description": "Attacks on the mouse",
        "bindings": { "attack": "Mouse1", "strong_attack": "Mouse3", "lock_on": "Mouse2", "roll": "Space" }
      }
      ```
      
      Actions: `move_forward move_back move_left move_right walk roll l3 attack strong_attack
      strong_modifier transform firearm lock_on blood_vial use_item interact switch_item switch_right
      switch_left dpad_up gestures personal_effects menu confirm back look_up look_down look_left
      look_right`. Keys use SDL names (`Space`, `Left Shift`, `Return`, `F`); mouse inputs are
      `Mouse1` (left), `Mouse2` (middle), `Mouse3` (right), `Mouse4`, `Mouse5`, `WheelUp`, `WheelDown`. Each action takes one key and one mouse input.
      
      ## Building the launcher
      
      .NET 8 SDK on Windows:
      
      ```
      dotnet build launcher/windows/BloodborneLauncher.sln -c Release
      ```
      
      `launcher/windows/LauncherBuilder` builds `Build Launcher.exe`, which rebuilds the launcher when
      its sources change (`--force` always). Put a folder path in `launcher/windows/install.txt` to
      install into a package folder instead of `LauncherApp/`.
      
      ## Engine
      
      The engine is developed here. It started from [DarkIzuku/bloodborne_pc](https://github.com/DarkIzuku/bloodborne_pc)
      (built on bbport and shadPS4) and has been reworked for Windows since: about 19,000 lines changed or added
      across nearly 150 files.
      
      - **Performance**: occlusion culling with real query results, cached texture, sampler and render target lookups,
        the end of each frame handed to the draw thread, render threads first, uncapped FPS. Up to the 120 FPS cap in
        busy areas on a Ryzen 5 5600 with an RTX 5060. Some of these are switches under Graphics › Experimental.
      - **Picture**: native HDR (highlights from the game's own HDR scene), DLSS texture LOD bias, FSR 4 balanced model.
      - **Stability**: fixes for silent crashes (0xC0000005), exit 23 asserts, low memory and display loss; crash
        reports and dumps; a GPU hang guard; VRAM cleanup, and game data leaving VRAM on cards that run short (4 GB).
      - **Sound**: the game's audio threads at their PS4 priority on Windows.
      - **Game**: cheats, menu languages, controller support, online with The Hunter's Dream, The Old Hunters on
        base-game dumps (DLC folder), 120 and 144 FPS from the 90 FPS patch.
      
      The patch against the starting point, every change with its switch, and build steps are in [engine/](engine/).
      
      ### What I changed
      
      The starting point already ran the game's own code natively and split GPU work over several
      threads. The charts show what was changed here on top of it; each item is a row in
      [engine/](engine/) with its switch. **(option)** means off by default, with a switch in the launcher.
      
      #### Performance: where each change acts
      
      ```mermaid
      flowchart TD
          subgraph G["Game threads"]
              g1["Shorter spin at the end of the game's sleeps (option)"]
              g2["No waiting behind texture work on write faults (option)"]
          end
          subgraph A["GPU command thread"]
              a1["New pipelines created on compile threads:<br/>shorter hitches in new areas"]
              a2["A draw whose shader is still compiling is<br/>skipped for a moment instead of freezing (option)"]
          end
          subgraph B["Draw thread (bb:DrawRec)"]
              b1["Texture hashes kept: no 9 MB re-hash every frame,<br/>about 13% less work per draw"]
              b2["Texture sets remembered<br/>for every shader stage"]
              b3["Lookups kept when textures change, samplers remembered,<br/>end of each submission handed over (option)"]
          end
          subgraph GPU["GPU"]
              q1["Occlusion culling with real query results:<br/>hidden objects skipped (option)"]
              m1["Up to 80% of the card's VRAM<br/>for textures (option)"]
          end
          subgraph P["Present"]
              p1["120 / 144 / uncapped FPS"]
              p2["Precise frame pacing (option)"]
          end
          G --> A --> B --> GPU --> P
          classDef ours fill:#2b4a2b,stroke:#6fbf6f,color:#fff
          class g1,g2,a1,a2,b1,b2,b3,m1,q1,p1,p2 ours
      ```
      
      #### Stability: what used to go wrong, and what happens now
      
      ```mermaid
      flowchart LR
          s1["Write fault at the end of a GPU mapping:<br/>crash 0xC0000005"] --> f1["Handled, the game goes on"]
          s2["Engine fault on a game thread:<br/>Windows closed the game without a trace"] --> f2["Crash report with the thread and call chain,<br/>crash.dmp next to the log"]
          s3["Unknown texture format or lost display:<br/>exit 23"] --> f3["A known format is used,<br/>the display is recreated"]
          s4["Textures freed while still in use:<br/>stalls, GPU device lost"] --> f4["Hang guard: textures in use are never freed,<br/>deleted ones kept a little longer"]
          s5["VRAM fills up over a long session"] --> f5["VRAM cleanup: GPU-drawn textures written back<br/>and freed under memory pressure"]
          s6["Patch made for another executable:<br/>writes into the wrong code, crash at start"] --> f6["Checked against the 1.09 executable,<br/>left out and logged"]
          s7["Resolution patch above 1080p:<br/>game memory pool full, crash"] --> f7["Larger pool given;<br/>a full pool is explained in the crash report"]
          s8["Sound slowly falls behind the picture"] --> f8["Output follows the device's real rate"]
          s9["Online: signed out by the server,<br/>a network drop sent the game to the title menu"] --> f9["Client reports its version,<br/>90 s to reconnect"]
          s10["Unlock Game Region with online on:<br/>no server for that region"] --> f10["Left out while online, unless you keep it"]
          s11["Busy frame (a boss intro at high model detail):<br/>a render pool ran out, crash"] --> f11["Render pools four times larger"]
          s12["120 / 144 FPS: the game froze<br/>at the end of Vicar Amelia's intro"] --> f12["The 90 FPS patch,<br/>with its values for that rate"]
          s13["4 GB cards: game data piled up in VRAM,<br/>exit 23 or a lost device"] --> f13["Above 85% of the VRAM budget, data unused<br/>for 30 s leaves VRAM (chart below)"]
          s14["1440p or 4K output: 10 GB asked at start,<br/>Windows error 1450, crash at launch"] --> f14["10 GB only for a scene above 1080p; the launcher<br/>warns first and closes a game left running"]
          s15["120 / 144 FPS: the character<br/>fell 1.5 to 1.8 times as fast"] --> f15["Its frame time scaled<br/>like the patch's other values"]
          s16["Keyboard: W right after closing a menu<br/>was a held d-pad up (HP into bullets)"] --> f16["Keys act as the d-pad only<br/>while a menu has the screen"]
          classDef was fill:#4a2b2b,stroke:#bf6f6f,color:#fff
          classDef now fill:#2b4a2b,stroke:#6fbf6f,color:#fff
          class s1,s2,s3,s4,s5,s6,s7,s8,s9,s10,s11,s12,s13,s14,s15,s16 was
          class f1,f2,f3,f4,f5,f6,f7,f8,f9,f10,f11,f12,f13,f14,f15,f16 now
      ```
      
      #### Button prompts: keyboard, mouse and Xbox
      
      ```mermaid
      flowchart TD
          T["The game uploads a texture"] --> I{"One of the game's button icons?<br/>(its 20 key-guide icons, the HUD's buttons)"}
          I -->|"no"| N["Uploaded unchanged"]
          I -->|"yes"| D{"Keyboard or mouse in use?<br/>(Button Prompts: Automatic)"}

      ```
      
      #### Game data in VRAM: why 4 GB cards no longer run out
      
      Every block of the game's memory a draw uses gets a copy in VRAM. Before, those copies stayed for good,
      so VRAM only grew with every area visited.
      
      ```mermaid
      flowchart TD
          L["Once a second: VRAM used against the driver's budget"] -->|"under 85%"| K["Everything stays in VRAM"]
          L -->|"85% or more"| E["Blocks unused for 30 s leave VRAM<br/>(10 s from 90%)"]
          E --> H["Kept: blocks with data the GPU wrote (only VRAM has it),<br/>and all of them while shaders read the game's memory directly"]
          E --> F["Their slots take the next blocks:<br/>VRAM stops growing"]
          U["A draw needs a block that left"] --> B["Bound again in a free slot, cleared first,<br/>or in new VRAM"]
          B --> W["The other blocks of its 2 MiB group come back with it, whole:<br/>draws read past their own range"]
          W --> R["Uploaded from the game's memory, then drawn"]
          classDef ours fill:#2b4a2b,stroke:#6fbf6f,color:#fff
          class E,H,F,B,W,R ours
      ```

          B["Bloodborne.exe, from a shortcut or Steam:<br/>the launcher stays out of sight"] --> C
          C -->|"yes"| C2["Offered to close it first"] --> M
          C -->|"no"| M{"Room for the<br/>memory pool?"}
          M -->|"no"| M2["Not enough RAM plus page file:<br/>a warning with the fix, or start anyway"] --> R
          M -->|"yes"| R["scripts/run_windows.py: every log starts<br/>with the launcher version and engine"]
          R --> P1["Patches checked against the 1.09 executable:<br/>FPS preset, resolution, render pools,<br/>third-party patches (01.09 or 1.09)"]
          R --> P2["Memory pool: 9152 MiB for a scene above 1080p<br/>or a patch that enlarges the game's heaps, else 5056 MiB"]
          P1 --> E["Engine (bb-probe.exe)"]
          P2 --> E
          E --> D["Add-ons in the DLC folder reported installed:<br/>The Old Hunters on base-game dumps"]
          D --> G["The game"]
          G -->|"ends normally"| X1["Bloodborne.exe: the launcher closes"]
          G -->|"crashes"| X2["Crash helper: the cause, safe mode,<br/>a report to copy"]
          classDef ours fill:#2b4a2b,stroke:#6fbf6f,color:#fff
          class B,C2,M2,P2,D,X1 ours
      ```
````
