      # Engine
      
      The engine as developed here. My work is `bbhost-changes.patch` (engine and scripts), applied to its starting point, [DarkIzuku/bloodborne_pc](https://github.com/DarkIzuku/bloodborne_pc)
      at tag `v0.4.0-darkizuku-preview.1`.
      
      ## Changes
      
      | Change | Switch |
      |---|---|
      | 120 / 144 / uncapped FPS on Windows | `BB_FPS_LIMIT`, `BB_VBLANK_HZ` |
      | VRAM cleanup: GPU-drawn textures written back and freed under memory pressure | `BB_IMAGE_WRITEBACK_GC=0` off |
      | GPU hang guard: textures in use are never freed, deleted ones kept a little longer | `BB_GC_RECENT_FRAMES=0`, `BB_IMAGE_FREE_DELAY_FRAMES=0` off |
      | Texture memory sized to the GPU (80% of its budget on discrete cards) | `BB_GC_PRESSURE_PERCENT=0` off |
      | Precise frame pacing | `BB_PRECISE_PACING=0` off |
      | Render threads at above-normal priority | `BB_GPU_THREAD_PRIORITY=0` off |
      | Shorter spin at the end of the game's sleeps | `BB_SLEEP_SPIN_US=600` off |
      | Audio threads (FMOD, PS4 priority 256-300) above the game's other threads on Windows | `BB_AUDIO_THREAD_PRIORITY=0` off |
      | Audio output follows the device's real rate (proportional correction, queue capped), so sound can't drift behind | |
      | Audio device thread watched (writes, rate, longest gap in the audio statistics) and raised when Windows leaves it at normal priority; DirectSound output with a larger buffer as an option | `BB_AUDIO_STATS`, `SDL_AUDIO_DRIVER=directsound`, `SDL_AUDIO_DEVICE_SAMPLE_FRAMES` |
      | Pipelines created on compile threads (shorter hitches in new areas) | `BB_ASYNC_PIPELINES=0` off |
      | Occlusion culling: real occlusion query results, so the game skips hidden objects; a block reads hidden only after three empty results (no flicker) | `BB_OCCLUSION=0` off |
      | Cached texture, sampler and render target lookups kept across image (un)registration | `BB_MEMO_REVALIDATE=0`, `BB_SAMPLER_MEMO=0` off |
      | End of each submission handed to the draw recording thread instead of draining it | `BB_SUBMIT_END_TASKS=0` off |
      | Draws whose shader is still compiling are skipped for a moment instead of freezing the game; pipelines bound once compiled | `BB_SKIP_UNCOMPILED=0`, `BB_LATE_PIPELINE_BIND=0`, `BB_PIPELINE_TAKE=0` off |
      | Game threads no longer wait behind texture work on write faults | `BB_FAULT_SKIP_TEXTURES=0`, `BB_DRAIN_SLEEP=0` off |
      | Write protection after uploads applied by a thread of its own (bb:Protect) and by the copy that reads the pages, instead of on the draw recording thread; off by default since 0.9.24 (a write in its window could leave a texture half-written) | `BB_DEFER_PROTECT=1` on |
      | WriteData and DMA wait only for the fences the command processor would have written before them, not for every pending one | `BB_FENCE_ORDER=all` off |
      | DMA waits only when the DMA really writes guest memory on the CPU; spin waits for host copies instead of yield loops | `BB_DMA_WAITS=all`, `BB_HOST_WAIT_SPIN_US=0` off |
      | Lookahead thread (bb:DrawAhead) that prefetches the cache lines of the next draws for the draw recording thread; on with 8 or more hardware threads | `BB_DRAWREC_WORKERS=0` off, `=1` on, `BB_DRAWREC_LOOKAHEAD` packets ahead |
      | An unbound descriptor table (a null pointer, seen while maps load) reads as an empty descriptor instead of crashing | |
      | Texture and sampler cleanup stops at its limits instead of walking every old entry on each submission | |
      | The previous display buffer is released before the game learns of the flip, so its next frame's label is no longer cleared (no 20 ms wait at the flip) | |
      | Every retail serial (CUSA03179 included) accepted by the save sound fix, third-party patch files and mod folders | |
      | Working profile-guided builds with clang (`BB_PGO=generate`, then `use`) | |
      | In-game menu in Spanish, Portuguese (Brazil), French, German, Italian, Polish, Turkish | `menu_language` |
      | Controller: the pad in use takes over; swap sticks, invert camera, dead zone | `pad_swap_sticks`, `pad_invert_look_x/y`, `pad_deadzone` |
      | Controller: Cross/Circle in the name entry, held buttons ignored after menus | |
      | No 12-second minimum loading time after death | `BB_RESPAWN_DELAY_FIX=0` off |
      | Crash fixes: oversized command data, empty recording chunk, out-of-order flip IRQ, SnormNz packed formats, failed allocations in audio decoding and the save list; swapchain recreation | |
      | Crash reports for host faults on game threads (Windows ended those without a trace); RAM in the log once a minute | |
      | Write faults at the end of a GPU mapping handled (they ended the game, 0xC0000005); unclaimed faults on guest pages get access back; crash dump next to the log; display loss and unknown formats no longer exit | |
      | Picture tuning live: the picture hooks are always installed and the switch gates them per call; wider ranges, typed values | `graphics_controls` |
      | HDR native mode: the game's UI at its own brightness and colours (sRGB to DCI-P3) | `hdr_ui_brightness`, `hdr_ui_color` |
      | Trophies a save already earned: the 19 boss trophies whose defeat flags are set count once a character is in the world ("earned in this save") | |
      | Chromatic aberration, depth of field, motion blur and the game's own anti-aliasing off by default | `effect_*` |
      | Online: characters given no id (0x8000000000000000) ask again; summon sign timeout (droogie bbhost 566184a) | `BB_SIGN_TIMEOUT` (`online_sign_timeout`) |
      | The mouse cursor hidden 2 s after the mouse last moved (it was always shown on Windows unless the mouse camera was on) | `hide_cursor` |
      | Online: the client reports what it is after signing in (shadNet 0.0.34 signs out clients that report nothing); a rejection is logged and signs out at once | `BB_CLIENT_VERSION` |
      | Launch: the boot image (prepare, link_libc, link_modules, content profile) is reused while its inputs are unchanged, about 10 s a launch | `out/prepared.json` |
      | Loading profile: the game's main loop, render and resource-loading threads and the engine's GPU command and recording threads sampled every 2 ms, their hottest game and engine code in the log every 5 s | `BB_SAMPLE_THREADS=load` |
      | Patches check the executable first: a built-in patch whose write sites differ from the standard 1.09 (CRC-32s in `patches/Bloodborne-1.09-sites.json`) is left out and logged instead of writing into other code | |
      | A scene above 1080p (output resolution and upscaler preset, without Live resolution) or a patch that enlarges the game's heaps (resolution patches above 1080p from the patches folder) gets the 9152 MiB pool; the output alone does not (it exists only on the host side), so a 1440p output with a scene up to 1080p keeps 5056 MiB; a full pool is logged and explained in the crash report | `BB_DMEM_MB` |
      | Online: a network drop of the shadNet connection keeps the game signed in for 90 s while it reconnects (it returned to the title menu) | |
      | Online co-op on The Hunter's Dream with bbhost players: the launcher starts bbbridge (MaskZeus, GPL-3.0-or-later, built unmodified, in `bbbridge\`) with the game and points the game's shadNet and server traffic at it; Discord sign-in on the Online page, account in `network\bbbridge\` | `online_pool=huntersdream` |
      | Intel 12th gen and later: the game's stores that keep values just below the stack pointer run 128 bytes lower, so Windows' exception frames no longer overwrite them (the crash when hit); 607 sites, skipped where the bytes differ (d4rksp4rt4n, Supermedo/bloodborne_pc #2, `patches/redzone.json`) | |
      | Built-in patches (Bloodborne.xml) can be switched on in the launcher's Mods page again, off by default; the ones the port sets from its own settings are not offered | `patches.json` |
      | eboot.bin as a plain decrypted ELF is accepted as well as the PS4 SELF | |
      | Quit game button in the in-game menu (Insert or L3+R3), pressed twice: the same clean exit as closing the window | |
      | Online co-op: shadNet server framing for signaling, UPnP port mapping (Supermedo 004d2c37), P2P port 3658 by default, play logs to the game server | `SHADPS4_P2P_PORT` |
      | In-game PC Colour page (brightness, contrast, saturation, hue from the game's own tone map) and a fog slider on PC Graphics, live; the same in the launcher's Picture tuning | `graphics_brightness`, `graphics_contrast`, `graphics_hue`, `graphics_fog` |
      | HDR output: HDR10 or scRGB swapchain with paper white, peak and highlight boost; native mode takes highlight brightness from the game's scene (a gain map), expand mode from the SDR picture | `hdr`, `hdr_mode`, `hdr_paper_white`, `hdr_peak`, `hdr_boost` |
      | DLSS texture LOD bias | `BB_DLSS_MIP_BIAS=0` off |
      | Optional FSR 4 balanced model | `BB_FSR4_BALANCED=1` |
      | Cheats: Blood Vials and Quicksilver Bullets (infinite or a set amount), consumables, stamina, stealth, no weapon wear, firearm range, keep echoes, echo multiplier, add echoes/insight; live and revertible (in-game menu) | `cheat_*` |
      | Texture refresh: an image the GPU rewrites every frame (the game's copy of the depth buffer) keeps the hashes of its guest memory while nothing wrote that memory, instead of hashing 9 MB a frame on the draw recording thread; large images are hashed on the copy threads | `BB_KEEP_MIP_HASHES=0`, `BB_PARALLEL_IMAGE_HASH=0` off |
      | Texture set memo for shader stages without prepared draw data as well | `BB_LOCAL_TEXTURE_SETS=0` off |
      | Effects at reduced presets: passes at the output size that read a reduced-resolution image through a point sampler read the full-size image instead, which is upscaled with linear filtering (blocky effects and moon edge with DLSS/FSR) | `BB_PROXY_POINT_NATIVE=0`, `BB_SCENE_LINEAR_RESOLVE=0` off |
      | Keyboard and mouse button prompts: the game's 20 key-guide icons and the HUD's buttons drawn as the bound keys when they are uploaded, the game's own icons again with a controller | `button_prompts` (`auto`, `keyboard`, `controller`) |
      | Xbox controller icons: with a controller other than a PlayStation one in use (or chosen), the same icons drawn as the Xbox button bound to each PS4 button (A, B, X, Y, LB, RB, LT, RT, LS, RS, View, Menu); the d-pad and stick icons stay the game's. The in-game PC Controls page has no Defaults row (8 rows fill it) | `pad_icons` (`auto`, `playstation`, `xbox`) |
      | A patch that changes the game's region (Unlock Game Region) is left out while online is on, unless kept: the game has no server for that region | `BB_REGION_PATCH_ONLINE=keep` |
      | Output resolution 7680x2160 (32:9), and `auto`: the display's own size (read from Windows at start), the camera and UI widened to fill it | `output_res`, `BB_DISPLAY_SIZE` |
      | A third-party resolution patch (any patch writing the game's resolution and UI layout sites) is left out while the output resolution isn't 1920x1080, unless kept: applied after the engine's own, it kept its shape on screen (black bars) and stopped the widescreen hooks | `BB_RESOLUTION_PATCH=keep` |
      | 120 and 144 FPS: the 90 FPS++ patch with its frame-rate values for that rate (frame times, frame counts, timings, a thread's sleep, the limiter's longest sleep, two speed scales, and the character update's frame time: left at 90's, the character fell 1.5 times as fast at 120). The uncapped patch they used before froze the game at the end of Vicar Amelia's intro | `fps_mode` (`120`, `144`) |
      | The game's two per-frame render pools are 1 MiB each instead of 256 KiB: a busy frame ran one out and the game wrote through the null pointer it got (GXWorker crash in a boss intro with Model LOD -2 at 2560x1440) | `BB_RENDER_POOLS=0` off |
      | VRAM budget for the game's data: without the PC memory model (it needs an AMD GPU) every block of the game's memory the GPU used kept its VRAM copy, so 4 GB cards ran out (exit 23, or a lost device). Above 85% of the driver's VRAM budget, copies unused for 30 s leave VRAM (10 s above 90%) and are uploaded again from the game's memory when used; blocks with data the GPU wrote stay; one that comes back brings the other blocks of its 2 MiB group back whole, since a draw reads past its own range. Slots they leave take new blocks before new VRAM is allocated, cleared first (vertex buffers are bound without a size, so a draw reading past its range must find zeros there, as in new VRAM). Where the driver offers system memory for the game's data (not NVIDIA's), new blocks go there instead while VRAM is tight. With the PC memory model, unused copies go back after 15 s instead of 60 (3 s above 90%) | `BB_VRAM_PRESSURE_PERCENT` (`0` off), `BB_VRAM_IDLE_SECONDS` |
      | Third-party patches for version `1.09` are taken as well as `01.09` | |
      | Add-ons (The Old Hunters on base-game dumps): the dumped add-ons in the launcher's DLC folder and in `<user>/addcont/<title id>/` are reported to the game as installed; the label is the end of each add-on's CONTENT_ID (`sce_sys/param.sfo`, category `ac`), else its folder's name. Their data ships with update 1.09 | `BB_DLC_DIR` |

      | Keys navigate menus as the d-pad only while a menu has the screen: in the 0.4 s after a menu closed, W was a held d-pad up in the world (HP into Quicksilver Bullets) | |
      
      Parts are adapted from [IFreemz/shadPS4-Bloodborne-DLSS-FSR](https://github.com/IFreemz/shadPS4-Bloodborne-DLSS-FSR),
      [AwesomeObserver/bloodborne_pc](https://github.com/AwesomeObserver/bloodborne_pc),
      [Supermedo's Windows port](https://github.com/Supermedo/bloodborne_pc) and
      [deadinside28/bloodborne_pc](https://github.com/deadinside28/bloodborne_pc) (all GPL-2.0-or-later) and [droogie/bbhost](https://github.com/droogie/bbhost) (GPL-3.0); the authors are
      credited in the code.
      
      ## Build
      
      In the MSYS2 **CLANG64** shell (packages as in the engine's README):
      
      ```bash
      git clone --branch v0.4.0-darkizuku-preview.1 --recurse-submodules https://github.com/DarkIzuku/bloodborne_pc
      cd bloodborne_pc
      git apply /path/to/engine/bbhost-changes.patch
      cp /path/to/engine/win_compat.h gpu/
      CFLAGS="-Wno-error=unused-but-set-global" CXXFLAGS="-include $PWD/gpu/win_compat.h" bash build.sh
      ```
      
      `win_compat.h` supplies headers the bundled FSR 3 SDK expects transitively, which newer libc++
      no longer includes. The result is `out/bb-probe.exe`; the package's `out/` holds it with the
      CLANG64 DLLs it loads.
      
      GPL-3.0-or-later, like the engine.

- path: /tmp/pp/docs__pipeline_compiles.md.diff
  content: |
      diff --git a/docs/pipeline_compiles.md b/docs/pipeline_compiles.md
      new file mode 100644
      index 0000000..dfb8088
      --- /dev/null
      +++ b/docs/pipeline_compiles.md
      @@ -0,0 +1,115 @@
      +# Pipeline compiles and the waits behind them
      +
      +A pipeline first seen during play is compiled on the compile threads (`BB_ASYNC_PIPELINES`,
      +default on). With a cold NVIDIA cache a compile takes 100-300 ms; entering an area brings
      +20-90 at once. Pipelines known from the shader database are created at start (preload) and
      +come out of the driver cache (`<serial>.vkcache`) quickly.
      +
      +## What a draw does with a pipeline still compiling
      +
      +Before (0.9.10 beta 1) the draw recording thread (stage B of the draw pipe) waited for it when
      +it recorded the bind: every new pipeline stalled the frame by its compile time (user logs, RTX
      +5060: `2 compiles 594 ms` -> a 607 ms frame, `18 compiles 1110 ms` -> 1665 ms), and the GPU
      +command thread and the guest threads that waited for stage B (drains, see below) stalled with
      +it. Now (`Rasterizer::DrawRecord`, `HandleIfReady`):
      +
      +- **Scene geometry is left out** while its pipeline compiles (`SkipUncompiledDraw`): draws with
      +  the scene depth (the G-buffer pass's, which was also the scene depth the frame before) that
      +  are not full-screen passes (more than 6 indices or instanced) - the draws the upscaler
      +  jitters. G-buffer, light volumes, forward/transparent draws and effects drawn with the scene
      +  depth. The frame draws these targets again from a clear, so the object is missing for the
      +  frames the compile takes (pop-in), nothing more. Everything else of the draw runs as before
      +  (targets, barriers, render pass, resources): only `vkCmdDraw` is not recorded. Never left
      +  out: draws the game measures (occlusion queries: zero samples would hide their predicated
      +  draws), indirect draws, compute dispatches, shadow maps, half-resolution effects,
      +  post-processing and UI (what they draw may be kept over frames or read as a whole), and
      +  draws during a frame capture. A pipeline's draws are left out for at most
      +  `BB_SKIP_UNCOMPILED_MS` (1000) from its first left-out draw; then they wait for it. "A few
      +  frames" at 120 FPS is 25-40 ms, below every compile measured, so the bound is in time.
      +  `BB_SKIP_UNCOMPILED=0`: never left out.
      +- **Everything else binds the pipeline on a recording thread** (`BindWhenCompiled`): the bind
      +  becomes a command of its own, and the recording thread that records it into the command
      +  buffer waits for the compile there. Stage B goes on with the next draws, so drains of the
      +  GPU command thread (and the guest threads behind them) do not wait for the compile. The
      +  frame itself still waits for it (its submission needs the command). `BB_LATE_PIPELINE_BIND=0`
      +  (or commands recorded on the calling thread: `BB_VK_RECORD_THREAD=0`, direct segments):
      +  stage B waits, as before.
      +- **A thread that must wait compiles the pipeline itself** when no compile thread has started
      +  it (`Pipeline::WaitReady`, `TakePipelineJob`): in a burst it was queued behind the other
      +  pipelines first. `BB_PIPELINE_TAKE=0`: waits for the compile threads.
      +
      +An already compiled pipeline costs what it did: `HandleIfReady` is the load and branch
      +`Handle()` was. The draw command gained a branch on the recording thread (bind or not).
      +
      +## Why not VK_EXT_graphics_pipeline_library
      +
      +DXVK links pipelines from libraries compiled when the game creates its shaders, long before the
      +draws. Here (measured on the user's shader database, 855 graphics pipelines):
      +
      +- Shaders reach the port at the draw that needs them: the guest binary is translated there.
      +  Libraries would be compiled at that draw too; only linking is fast.
      +- All stages of a pipeline share descriptor set 0 (one push descriptor set; the vertex stage's
      +  bindings follow the fragment stage's, and the vertex module is specialized on that offset).
      +  Libraries need identically defined layouts, so they are shared only between pipelines with
      +  the same stage modules: 780 distinct stage sets among the 855 pipelines (75, 9%, would reuse
      +  libraries). Separate sets per stage would end push descriptors for one of them: a descriptor
      +  set write per draw on the thread that limits the frame rate.
      +- NVIDIA compiles each library stage about as fully as in a pipeline: a draw would wait for
      +  the slower of the vertex and fragment libraries instead of both (perhaps 30-40% less), at
      +  about twice the compile work (libraries and the optimized pipeline after them).
      +
      +The start line reports whether the device offers it (`graphics pipeline library offered (fast
      +linking)`) for later work, e.g. if shader translation could run ahead of the draws.
      +
      +## Waits behind the draw recording thread (write faults, drains)
      +
      +`Stall: 335.8 ms frame; ... write faults 324.6 ms; GPU thread on CPU 328.1 ms (kernel 203.1
      +ms)`, and from a boss fight `image create 575 ms`, `image refresh 608.6 ms` with `write faults
      +605.1 ms`. Two different waits:
      +
      +- **Guest threads** handle their write faults with locks (`OnWriteFault`, `assume_locks`
      +  false); they never drain. `TextureCache::InvalidateMemory` takes the texture cache's lock,
      +  which stage B holds through `FindImage` (image creation, page protection) and `UpdateImage`
      +  (`RefreshImage`: the upload): 0.5-0.6 s with memory short. Most faults are on buffer pages
      +  (the game rewriting constants and vertices) that no image watches. The texture cache now
      +  counts, per 4 KiB page, the tracked images that protect it (`WatchedPages`, kept with the
      +  page manager's watchers, readable without the lock); a fault on a page no image watches
      +  updates the buffer tracking only. Images learn of CPU writes through their own page
      +  protection alone, so this is what the lock gave them: an untracked image is already dirty,
      +  or new (dirty), or hash-checked (MaybeCpuDirty). `BB_FAULT_SKIP_TEXTURES=0`: the lock for
      +  every fault. A fault on a page an image watches still waits for the lock (unchanged), and
      +  a guest thread's fault on GPU-written data still needs the GPU thread for the readback.
      +- **The GPU command thread** (stage A) drains before it handles its own faults (stream order:
      +  the queued draws read the old bytes first; a readback records commands) and at many other
      +  points. It waited with `SwitchToThread` in a loop for as long as stage B took: a core burnt
      +  in the kernel while stage B (or a compile thread) needed it. Its waits (`Drain`,
      +  `WaitForPacket`, a full ring) now spin, yield for `BB_DRAIN_SPIN_US` (500), then sleep until
      +  stage B has run the packet they need (stage B checks after each packet whether stage A
      +  sleeps for it: a load and a branch). `BB_DRAIN_SLEEP=0`: spin and yield as before. The wait
      +  itself is as long as stage B's work: with compiles off stage B that is now mostly image
      +  creation and uploads (memory pressure).
      +
      +## Statistics and log lines
      +
      +At start:
      +
      +    Pipelines: new ones compiled on 4 threads; draws of one still compiling: scene geometry left out for up to 1000 ms, other draws bind it on the recording threads (they wait for it) (BB_SKIP_UNCOMPILED, BB_LATE_PIPELINE_BIND); graphics pipeline library offered (fast linking), not used
      +    Waits: GPU command thread drains sleep after a spin (stage B wakes them); write faults on pages no image watches leave the texture cache alone (BB_DRAIN_SLEEP, BB_FAULT_SKIP_TEXTURES)
      +
      +`BB_FRAME_STATS`, every 5 s when anything happened:
      +
      +    Pipelines: 18 compiled in the background (2 by the thread that needed them); 340 draws of 12 pipelines left out while compiling; 6 draws/dispatches bound on the recording threads; 3 waits, 210.4 ms, longest 120.3 ms
      +
      +and `(N/s slept)` in the `Draw pipe:` line. The `shader/pipeline compiles, ms` figure of
      +`Frame stats` still adds the waits (now on recording threads too) to the translation time.
      +
      +## Risks
      +
      +- Left-out scene draws: an object (or light volume, decal, particle) appears a few frames
      +  late the first time its pipeline is needed. A transparent layer whose pipeline is ready
      +  over an opaque one still compiling shows over the background for those frames.
      +- A recording thread waiting for a compile delays its segment, the submission and the guest's
      +  fences after it, as stage B's wait did; ordered tasks (guest copies, fence signals) queue
      +  behind it.
      +- `ReplaceShader` (shader patching from the debug UI) destroys pipelines at once; a late bind
      +  still queued for one would use it after that.

      diff --git a/docs/parallel-stageb.md b/docs/parallel-stageb.md
      new file mode 100644
      index 0000000..9f33d28
      --- /dev/null
      +++ b/docs/parallel-stageb.md
      @@ -0,0 +1,299 @@
      +# Stage B across more than one thread: design notes
      +
      +Stage B is the draw recording thread `bb:DrawRec` (`vk_draw_pipe.h`, `Rasterizer::RunDrawPacket`).
      +In heavy fights on the Ryzen 5 5600 / RTX 5060 it is the frame rate limit: 62-94 FPS,
      +1300-1900 draws per frame, stage B busy 89-94%, ~5.3 us per packet, ~2500 packets per frame
      +(13.3 ms of a 14.4 ms frame in the 69.6 FPS window of `route\p10.log`). The game's main thread
      +would allow ~130 FPS. This note records what stage B does per packet, which parts are order
      +dependent, the approaches considered for running it on more than one thread, the one implemented
      +(`BB_DRAWREC_WORKERS=1`, a lookahead thread that prefetches for stage B), and why the approach
      +that would really scale (an ownership split of stage B into two pipelined stages) is not
      +something I could make safe in this change.
      +
      +Evidence: `route\p9.log` and `route\p10.log` (played heavy-fight sessions with `BB_SECTIONS=1`,
      +`BB_SAMPLE_THREADS=load`), `symprofile.py` on `bb-probe-p10.exe`, `docs/parallel_gpu.md` (the
      +earlier measurements of the texture binding helper and the two-stage pipeline), and the code.
      +
      +## 1. What stage B does per packet today
      +
      +Stage A (`shadPS4:GpuCommandProcessor`) decodes PM4, keeps the register file, runs the constant
      +engine, selects the pipeline (with the prepared draws of the `bb:DrawPrep` workers) and copies
      +small read-only constants into the constant ring. It writes a packet into the draw pipe ring: the
      +32-word register blocks written since the previous packet, each stage's user data and flattened
      +user data, the ring bindings, the vertex stream V#s, the draw parameters. Ordered tasks (EOP/EOS
      +fences, WriteData, DmaData, the flip) are packets too.
      +
      +Stage B, per draw packet (`RunDrawPacket` -> `DrawRecord`), with the `stage B us per packet`
      +numbers of the 69.6 FPS window (5.29 us per packet; a packet is a draw, a dispatch or a task):
      +
      +| step | what it touches | us/packet |
      +|---|---|---|
      +| apply register blocks, install user data snapshots | its own register copy (`pipe_regs`), thread-local snapshots | ~0.2 |
      +| `PrepareRenderState` | render/depth target descriptions (memoized per slot) | 0.17 |
      +| `BindBuffers` (per stage) | ring bindings (no lookup), else `ObtainBuffer`: arena table, residency, the memory tracker's page words (CPU/GPU dirty bits), uploads, `gpu_modified_ranges`, barrier tracker | 0.41 (ObtainBuffer in total 0.89, `VRAM track` 0.45) |
      +| `BindTextures` (per stage) | texture set memo slot (97% hits in fights: 219k hits, 5.7k misses per 5 s); per image: flags, backing, up-to-date check, layout transition; else the full lookup (image description cache, `FindImage`, views, refresh) | 0.99 (set 0.59: check 0.22, apply 0.22; full 0.27; samplers 0.07) |
      +| `BeginRendering` | render state memo (84% hits), else target views, barriers, scene proxies | 0.28 |
      +| `ResolveVertexBuffers`, `ResolveIndexBuffer` | `ObtainBuffer` for the merged stream ranges and the index range | 0.52 + 0.11 |
      +| `EmitVertexBuffers`, `FlushBarriers` | record chunk | 0.13 |
      +| object motion | bone palette hashes, index range cache (reads guest memory) | 0.26 |
      +| descriptors, `UpdateDynamicState`, `MarkPass`, `scheduler.BeginRendering`, the draw command | record chunk, dynamic state | ~0.3 |
      +| `ResetBindings`, `KickRecording` | image binding flags, buffer access tracker, hand-over to `bb:VkRecorder` | 0.14 |
      +| dispatches (`DispatchRecord`, the copy shader HLE) | `ObtainBuffer` for sources and destinations, copies | 0.61 per packet averaged |
      +| ordered tasks (fences, WriteData, DMA, flip) | waits for host copies and deferred fences, guest memory stores | 0.46 |
      +
      +Already parallel: Vulkan command recording (`bb:VkRecorder` threads record the closures stage B
      +pushes into record chunks; `HandOver`/`KickRecording`), host copies (copy threads and the
      +ordered copies on the recorders), draw preparation (`bb:DrawScan`, `bb:DrawPrep`: pipeline keys,
      +sharps, texture description hashes, vertex inputs, all validated by stage A), and since the plan
      +in `perf-plan.md`, page re-protection (`bb:Protect`, `BB_DEFER_PROTECT`). The CPU profile of
      +stage B is flat (`symprofile.py`: `BindTextures` 4.8%, the spin in `DrawPipe::Run` 2.5%,
      +`RunDrawPacket` 2.4%, `DrawRecord` 2.2%, `Image::GetBarriers` 1.7%, `BindBuffers` 1.7%, nothing
      +else above 1.5%; ~21% in ntdll, mostly the sleeps, protects and waits the applied plan removes).
      +The earlier `perf` profile with call graphs (`parallel_gpu.md`, "Second pass") said the same:
      +no function above ~5% self time, the cost is cache misses spread over the texture, buffer and
      +barrier structures.
      +
      +## 2. What is order dependent
      +
      +Everything a draw does on stage B reads or writes state that the previous packets left:
      +
      +- The register copy: a draw reads the registers at its position; only the changed blocks travel.
      +- The barrier tracker (`Runtime::IsBufferAccessed`/`AccessBuffer`, `Transit`, image layouts):
      +  the barrier a draw needs depends on what the previous draws and copies did to the same buffer
      +  or image, and the transitions it records change what the next draw needs.
      +- The buffer cache: `ObtainBuffer` turns CPU-dirty pages into uploads recorded before this draw
      +  and marks pages GPU-modified for written bindings; a later binding of the same range must see
      +  those marks, and a GPU-modified range must not be re-uploaded from stale guest data. The
      +  stream path copies guest memory into the stream buffer at this point of the stream: a later
      +  WriteData/DMA to the same memory waits for that copy (`WaitHostCopiesFor`).
      +- The texture cache: images are registered, refreshed, invalidated by storage writes, tracked
      +  and untracked (page watchers) in stream order; the texture set memo and the render state memo
      +  are valid exactly because nothing ran between the memoized draw and this one that the checks
      +  do not cover.
      +- The scheduler's producer side: one thread fills the current record chunk and the ordered
      +  chunk (`ProducerScope` reports a second one); draws, uploads, barriers, copies and fences
      +  must land in it in stream order, since `OrderedReady` and the deferred fences assume it.
      +- CPU side effects of tasks: WriteData and CPU DMA store into guest memory in order with the
      +  host copies of earlier draws (`WaitHostCopiesFor`) and the deferred fences (`WaitDeferredSignals`);
      +  later draws read what they wrote (constants, index data).
      +- The deferred-protect invariant (`page_manager.cpp` ~430): pages an upload copied may stay
      +  writable until `bb:Protect` or the copy itself applies the protection; every reader of guest
      +  memory on the GPU side goes through `CopySparseMemory`, which flushes pending protects first.
      +
      +So a draw's result (what it uploads, which barriers it emits, which memo entries it finds valid)
      +is a function of the whole prefix of the stream. The only parts without side effects are
      +computations from the packet's own data: hashes, keys, the addresses of what will be consulted.
      +
      +## 3. Approaches considered
      +
      +### A. N workers each running a whole draw from a register snapshot (fork/join)
      +
      +Each worker would need the caches, the barrier tracker and the scheduler's producer side; none
      +of them is thread-safe, and the barrier and upload decisions of draw N+1 depend on draw N. The
      +closest experiment that exists is the texture binding helper (`BB_TEXTURE_HELPER=1`,
      +`parallel_gpu.md`, "Texture binding on a helper thread"): the helper binds textures on the
      +memoized path while stage B binds buffers, with a join before any image state changes. 68% of
      +draws were bound in parallel and the frame rate did not move (85.9 vs 85.8 FPS): the helper's
      +task took ~6200 cycles where the same work cost ~4600 on the GPU thread and the join waited
      +~2500 cycles per fork, because the descriptor infos, image states and binding flags it writes
      +are read by stage B right after and move between cores. Moving ~7 us of cache-bound work to
      +another core per draw costs about what it saves. Gain ~0, risk high. Rejected.
      +
      +### B. Pipelining stage B into two owners (B1: decode, buffers, uploads, tasks; B2: textures, targets, barriers, recording)
      +
      +This is the design `parallel_gpu.md` ("What would scale", item 1) identifies as the one that
      +scales: each thread owns its data for long stretches instead of handing per-draw results across.
      +From the table above B2 would take textures (0.99), render state and begin rendering (0.45),
      +dynamic state, descriptors, the draw command and the kick (~0.45): ~1.9 of 5.3 us; stage B1
      +would keep ~3.4 us, so stage B's critical path would fall by ~35% (plus whatever the dispatch
      +path splits), i.e. ~+50% FPS where stage B limits, bounded by the main thread at ~130 FPS.
      +
      +What it needs, and why I did not do it here:
      +
      +- Two producers into the scheduler's command stream in stream order while B2 lags B1 by several
      +  draws: the scheduler would need a second ordered lane (B1's upload copies and barriers must be
      +  recorded before B2 reaches the draw, after B2's previous draws), or B1 must stop recording
      +  anything and hand its upload commands to B2 as data. Every `runtime.CopyBuffer`,
      +  `IsBufferAccessed`, `AccessBuffer` call in the buffer cache moves to B2 or becomes a message.
      +- The buffer and texture caches call each other: `ObtainBuffer` invalidates images for storage
      +  writes (`InvalidateMemoryFromGPU`), texel buffers sync from images (`SynchronizeMemoryFromImage`),
      +  image refresh obtains buffers (`ObtainBufferForImage`, `RefreshObtain`), the copy shader HLE and
      +  the DMA GPU paths use both and record copies. Each of these becomes a cross-stage drain or a
      +  protocol.
      +- `ResetBindings` (buffer access marks of the draw's buffers) and `needs_barrier` are shared
      +  between the halves.
      +- The memo validity arguments (texture sets, render state) assume the one-thread order; B2's
      +  memos would have to be reasoned about against B1's uploads landing in between.
      +- Ordered tasks: WriteData/DMA stores (B1) are ordered against host copies and deferred fences
      +  that the recorders run after B2's commands; the fence barrier logic of `perf-plan.md` C2-3
      +  assumes a single stage B position.
      +
      +That is a multi-week refactor across `vk_scheduler`, `buffer_cache`, `texture_cache`,
      +`vk_rasterizer` and `vk_shader_hle`, with failure modes that only show in play (stale uploads,
      +missing barriers, heap corruption through fence order). I cannot run the game here, and a
      +change of that size cannot be validated by compiling it. It is the right next step if the
      +remaining single-thread wins are exhausted; it is not safe within this scope.
      +
      +### C. Splitting the command stream at frame or submission boundaries
      +
      +Two stage B instances on alternate frames or submissions would need two copies of every cache
      +and of the image layout state, or locks around all of it; the stream of one frame depends on
      +the layouts, uploads and GPU-modified marks the previous frame left. Not viable.
      +
      +### D. Speculative cache lookups on the draw-preparation workers
      +
      +The `bb:DrawPrep` workers already compute everything that depends only on the packet (sharps,
      +hashes, vertex inputs). What remains on stage B is the part that reads mutable cache state and
      +must be validated against it, and the validation is the same read as the lookup (the texture set
      +check is 0.22 us of the 0.59 us set path; the lock-free dirty-page check is a bitset scan). A
      +"candidate" from a worker saves nothing stage B does not redo, and a stale candidate costs a
      +second pass. Rejected for the texture and buffer lookups; the remaining pure parts (bone
      +palette hash, the texture set key) are ~0.1 us.
      +
      +### E. A lookahead thread that prefetches for stage B (implemented)
      +
      +Stage B is a pointer-chasing consumer whose per-frame working set does not fit its core's
      +caches: the texture set memo alone is 32768 slots of ~1.1 KiB (~35 MiB, more than the 5600's
      +32 MiB L3), plus thousands of `Image` slots, the page tracking words of the touched 4 MiB
      +regions, the arena table, the record chunks and the packets themselves. The first touches of a
      +draw form short dependent chains (set slot -> entry id -> image slot; region pointer -> page
      +words) that nothing can overlap because the addresses come from the previous load. A thread that
      +walks the committed packets a few ahead of stage B can resolve those chains early and prefetch
      +the lines, so stage B finds them in the shared L3 or in the lookahead core's cache (an on-die
      +transfer, ~40-100 cycles) instead of memory (~250-300 cycles at DDR4-3200).
      +
      +It changes no state: the only loads are from the packet ring (committed packets stage A cannot
      +overwrite), the prepared draws (kept alive until stage B passes the packet), the shader infos and
      +the memo slot's key and ids; everything else is an address that is prefetched and never read, and
      +prefetch instructions do not fault. Risk is therefore low and the whole thing sits behind one
      +toggle, default off. The gain is bounded by the DRAM-miss share of stage B's time, which the
      +profiles cannot show directly (a flat profile is consistent with it but does not prove it); the
      +estimate is in section 5. It is honestly the only one of the five that I could make safe without
      +running the game, and it is the one with the best gain-to-risk ratio for a single toggle. It
      +does not reach the stated target of stage B well under the main thread's time; B does.
      +
      +## 4. The lookahead thread (`BB_DRAWREC_WORKERS=1`)
      +
      +Thread `bb:DrawAhead`, `Rasterizer::LookaheadLoop` (`vk_rasterizer.cpp`), started with the draw
      +pipe when `BB_DRAWREC_WORKERS` is set to anything but 0. Normal priority (`BB_DRAWREC_IDLE=1`:
      +idle priority, only spare cores, starved on a busy CPU). It keeps a cursor into the draw pipe
      +ring:
      +
      +1. If stage B passed the cursor (it fell behind), it jumps to stage B's position (counted:
      +   `behind stage B`).
      +2. If it is more than `BB_DRAWREC_LOOKAHEAD` packets (default 8) ahead of stage B's count, it
      +   waits (pause spin, yields after 100 us; counted: `waited for it`): lines fetched too early
      +   would be evicted before use and only pollute the cache.
      +3. If no packet is committed past the cursor it spins 20 us and then sleeps; `DrawPipe::Commit`
      +   wakes it with the same announce-then-check protocol as stage B's own sleep
      +   (`DrawPipe::WaitForCommit`; one extra atomic load on stage A per commit).
      +4. Otherwise it reads the packet (`DrawPipe::PacketAt`) and runs `PrefetchPacket`.
      +
      +`PrefetchPacket` handles direct draws with a prepared draw (`PacketKind::Draw` with
      +`packet.prepared`; 82-98% of draws in the logs): tasks, dispatches, indirect and special draws
      +bind without prepared sharps and are skipped. It parses the packet exactly as `RunDrawPacket`
      +does and, per stage with a matching `PreparedStage` (`FindPreparedStage`, now also usable from
      +another thread):
      +
      +- Textures (the `BindTexturesFromSet` path): the same key as stage B
      +  (`XXH3(image_hashes) ^ stage ^ point_native`), the slot's header and hashes; if the slot's key
      +  matches (one relaxed load), its entries and the first 192 bytes of each image slot
      +  (`TextureCache::ImageSlotAddress` -> `SlotVector::SlotAddress`: an address computed from the
      +  storage pointer, never dereferenced); otherwise the two ways of the image description cache
      +  for each texture (the start of the full lookup).
      +- Buffers (`BindBuffers` -> `ObtainBuffer`): for each non-special buffer that is not a ring
      +  binding of this packet, `BufferCache::PrefetchBinding`: the arena table entry and, through
      +  `MemoryTracker::Prefetch`, the CPU and GPU page bit words of every 4 MiB region of the range
      +  (what `IsRegionModified` and `ForEachUploadRange` read first; regions are not created).
      +- The vertex streams (`ResolveVertexBuffers`): the same for each V# in the packet.
      +
      +Not prefetched: the index buffer and the render targets (they come from the register file, which
      +the lookahead thread does not replay), the memory tracker's region locks (taken only for written
      +bindings, and a shared prefetch of a line stage B will write only costs an extra invalidation),
      +anything behind a pointer read from a memo slot (an image's backing state), guest memory (reads
      +there could trigger the page tracker's read-fault path).
      +
      +Safety:
      +
      +- Ring: `Begin` waits for room below `consumed + Capacity`, so a packet at or past `consumed` is
      +  never overwritten; the lookahead reads only packets between `Consumed()` and `Published()`
      +  (acquire loads; `Commit` publishes after the bytes are written).
      +- Prepared draws: kept alive by `pipe_keepalive` until stage B reached the packet's position and
      +  stage A ran `RetireSubmission`. If the lookahead falls behind and reads a packet stage B has
      +  passed, the prepared pointer may be stale; the read is wrapped in `BB_RECOVER_SET` (the
      +  loader's vectored handler resumes at the recovery point on any thread) and counted
      +  (`faults recovered`). The ring bytes themselves stay valid for 16 MiB of further packets.
      +- Memo slots and image ids: read with relaxed atomic loads of the key and the ids only; a torn
      +  or reused id produces a wrong address to prefetch, which is harmless.
      +- No locks, no page protection, no guest memory, no scheduler calls, no cache mutation: the
      +  deferred-protect invariant, the fence ordering and the DMA/WriteData side effects are untouched
      +  because the thread never participates in them. Stage B's order and results are the same with
      +  the thread on or off.
      +- Stop: the thread is a `std::jthread` member declared after `draw_pipe`, so it is joined before
      +  the ring goes; `WaitForCommit` registers a stop callback on its sleep.
      +- Live A/B: experiment bit 16 of `BB_TOGGLE_FILE` pauses it (it sleeps in 1 ms steps and
      +  re-syncs on resume), so `-AbBits 16` compares on/off within one run.
      +
      +What can still go wrong (not ruled out without running it):
      +
      +- It takes a hardware thread. On 12 threads with the game's own pools, stage A, stage B, two
      +  recorders, copy threads and `bb:Protect`, a spinning thread can slow a game thread or stage B
      +  itself; the spin is short (20 us) and it sleeps between frames, but heavy fights keep it busy.
      +  If the FPS drops with it on, `BB_DRAWREC_IDLE=1` is the first thing to try, then a smaller
      +  window.
      +- Bandwidth and pollution: ~20-60 lines per draw at ~5 us per draw is ~1 GB/s of extra traffic
      +  if every line missed; prefetches past the L2's outstanding-miss capacity are dropped, which
      +  only loses the benefit.
      +- Lines stage B writes right after reading (binding flags, `tick_accessed_last`, set
      +  generation) are in the lookahead core's cache in shared state: stage B's write costs an
      +  invalidation. The texture helper measurements show the cost of moving written lines between
      +  cores; here only reads are shared, which is cheaper, but it is not free.
      +- The stale-packet recovery relies on the vectored handler being installed and on nothing
      +  holding a lock across the faulting read (nothing does); a fault in the middle of a prefetch
      +  loop leaves no state behind.
      +
      +## 5. Expected gain, from the numbers
      +
      +Per draw, stage B's first touches that the lookahead covers: 1 texture set slot (3 lines header
      +and hashes, then 12 lines of entries for a full set) and 2-8 image slots (2-3 lines each) for
      +each of 2-3 stages with textures; 2-3 lines per buffer range for ~6-10 ranges (the arena entry is
      +hot). That is 20-60 lines per draw. How many of them miss to DRAM is what the logs cannot show.
      +If 4-8 of them do (the set slot in a 35 MiB table that exceeds the L3, images not bound since
      +the last frame, regions not touched for a while), each costs 80-100 ns on this CPU: 0.3-0.8 us
      +of the 5.3 us per packet, 6-15%. A lookahead that resolves them a few packets ahead removes
      +most of that latency from stage B's path but adds the shared-line invalidations and the thread's
      +own footprint, so I expect 0-8% less stage B time per frame, with a real chance of 0 and a small
      +chance of a loss on a core-starved run. The same window and `-AbBits 16` will tell. If it gives
      +nothing, the honest reading is that stage B is not DRAM-latency bound in the parts the lookahead
      +can reach, which is itself useful before investing in approach B.
      +
      +Measure: `Draw pipe` lines (`BB_FRAME_STATS=1`): `stage B busy`, and the new line
      +
      +```
      +  lookahead: N packets/s walked, D draws/s prefetched, L lines/draw, A packets ahead,
      +             behind stage B B/s, waited for it W/s, busy X%, F faults recovered
      +```
      +
      +`A` should sit near the window (a lookahead that keeps up); `behind` near 0; `busy` well under
      +stage B's. With `BB_SECTIONS=1`, `stage B us per packet`: `tex set`, `tex set check`, `buffers`,
      +`VRAM track`, `vertex` are the sections that should fall. FPS and `GPU thread us/draw` are the
      +result. Correctness: screenshots identical on/off (nothing changes what stage B does), no new
      +`Draw pipe:` reports, `faults recovered` ~0 (a steady count means the thread keeps falling
      +behind; raise nothing, it only loses the benefit).
      +
      +## 6. Files changed
      +
      +- `gpu/shim/bbport_toggles.h`: `BbStats::lookahead_*` counters (CRLF).
      +- `gpu/shadps4/video_core/renderer_vulkan/vk_draw_pipe.h`: `Published`, `ConsumedPackets`,
      +  `PacketAt`, `WaitForCommit`; the lookahead's wake flag checked in `Commit` (CRLF).
      +- `gpu/shadps4/common/slot_vector.h`: `SlotAddress` (CRLF).
      +- `gpu/shadps4/video_core/texture_cache/texture_cache.h`: `ImageSlotAddress` (LF).
      +- `gpu/shadps4/video_core/buffer_cache/memory_tracker.h`: `Prefetch` (CRLF).
      +- `gpu/shadps4/video_core/buffer_cache/buffer_cache.h/.cpp`: `PrefetchBinding` (CRLF).
      +- `gpu/shadps4/video_core/renderer_vulkan/vk_rasterizer.h/.cpp`: `LookaheadWanted`,
      +  `LookaheadWindow`, `LookaheadLoop`, `PrefetchPacket`, `PrefetchDraw`, the static
      +  `FindPreparedStage`, the thread member, the startup line and the statistics line (CRLF).
      +
      +Environment: `BB_DRAWREC_WORKERS=1` (on; default off, 0 = today's behaviour; the value is a
      +switch, there is one lookahead thread), `BB_DRAWREC_LOOKAHEAD=<packets>` (default 8, 1..256),
      +`BB_DRAWREC_IDLE=1` (idle priority), experiment bit 16 of `BB_TOGGLE_FILE` (pause, for A/B).

      diff --git a/docs/hdr.md b/docs/hdr.md
      new file mode 100644
      index 0000000..8db00a1
      --- /dev/null
      +++ b/docs/hdr.md
      @@ -0,0 +1,127 @@
      +# HDR output
      +
      +`hdr=1` in `bbport.ini` (`BB_HDR=1`, the menu's "HDR output", applied on restart) presents the
      +game in an HDR swapchain when the display offers one (Windows HDR on): HDR10 (BT.2020, PQ,
      +`A2B10G10R10`) or scRGB (linear BT.709 in FP16). The game itself only makes an 8-bit SDR frame;
      +`hdr_output.frag` encodes it. SDR white is shown at `hdr_paper_white` nits (80-500, default 200),
      +nothing goes above `hdr_peak` (400-10000, default 1000). The settings menu is drawn into its own
      +layer and composed at paper white. SDR is decoded with a 2.2 power curve (the piecewise sRGB curve
      +lifts Bloodborne's shadows into grey).
      +
      +How the highlights get above paper white is `hdr_mode` (`BB_HDR_MODE`, the menu's "HDR mode",
      +live):
      +
      +| mode | highlights from | midtones | UI |
      +|---|---|---|---|
      +| `native` (default) | the game's own linear HDR scene, before its tonemap | exactly the SDR picture | paper white |
      +| `expand` | the clipped SDR picture (a guess) | exactly the SDR picture | expanded like the rest |
      +
      +## Expand
      +
      +Above a knee (linear 0.8) the brightest channel of the SDR frame is stretched so that SDR white
      +reaches `1 + (peak / paper - 1) * hdr_boost` times paper white (boost 0..1, default 0.25: 400
      +nits with the defaults). Hue and saturation stay. Anything near SDR white is expanded, a lamp and
      +a white menu text alike.
      +
      +## Native
      +
      +The game's tonemap compresses its HDR scene into SDR: midtones roughly by an exposure, highlights
      +by a shoulder that ends at SDR white. Native mode keeps the game's SDR frame (its grading,
      +contrast, saturation, vignette, fog colour, bloom and UI) and multiplies its highlights by how
      +much brighter the scene really is there, measured every frame on the GPU:
      +
      +1. **Scene luma** (`hdr_native.comp` LUMA): before the post-processing combine (compute shader
      +   `9a9cf8a9`, the upscaler's hook; after FSR/DLSS/TAA wrote its output into the scene color,
      +   so output-sized at 1080p output). The RGBA16F scene color's brightest channel at half size:
      +   the 2x2 maximum (highlights) and the brightest channel of the 2x2 average (exposure). A
      +   reduced scene (scaled presets) is resolved into the guest image first, as the game's own
      +   compute passes reading it do.
      +2. **UI-free copy and exposure** (SNAPSHOT, EXPOSURE): at the first UI pass (at 1080p output
      +   the first Scaleform draw: vertex shader `34e8a281` or another of
      +   `UiComposition::MovieShader`, into the game's RGBA8 UI target; with scaled presets the
      +   output-size UI image right after the upscaler or background copy wrote it) the tonemapped
      +   frame is copied bit for bit, and
      +   `log2(SDR / scene)` is averaged over the SDR midtones (linear brightest channel 0.02-0.45, at
      +   least 1/200 of the pixels): what the game's curve does to the scene there. Bloom lights up
      +   SDR midtones around lamps where the scene is dark; samples far from the last exposure count
      +   less (Gaussian weight, one stop), so a uniform change still goes through. Smoothed over
      +   frames (10% a frame); after frames without a scene it starts over.
      +3. **Gain map** (GAIN): at the display pass that copies the finished frame (UI included) into a
      +   display buffer, the first pass of the next frame. Per pixel of the finished frame:
      +   - UI: where the frame differs from the UI-free copy (HUD, menus, subtitles, their translucent
      +     backgrounds), gain 1;
      +   - below the knee (linear brightest channel 0.5) gain 1: the SDR picture exactly; above it the
      +     gain fades in (smoothstep to SDR white);
      +   - the scene's brightness on the SDR scale is `exposure * scene`, with the brightest scene
      +     pixel of the 2x2 luma texels around (4x4 scene pixels: the footprint does not shimmer with
      +     the upscalers' sub-pixel jitter). Where the SDR frame is brighter than that (bloom, glare:
      +     they are added after the scene color) the gain stays 1; else the SDR pixel goes towards it:
      +     `gain = (scene / sdr) ^ (sqrt(boost) * fade)`;
      +   - the result goes smoothly into the peak (unchanged up to halfway between SDR white and the
      +     peak, then towards the peak with the same slope), so very bright sources keep some
      +     gradation.
      +
      +   The map (R16F, the finished frame's size, negative where UI was found) belongs to that
      +   display buffer. The flip of a display buffer comes a frame later in the command stream; the
      +   presenter takes the buffer's map when it prepares the flip (`Presenter::PrepareFrame`,
      +   exchanged with the frame's previous map, no copy), so a frame and its map always match.
      +4. **Encode** (`hdr_output.frag`): the letterboxed SDR frame times the map (filtered, mapped
      +   over the frame's rectangle in the window), capped at the peak.
      +
      +A frame without a scene (title, menus, loading screens, pre-rendered movies), or whose display
      +pass reads another image than the UI-free copy came from (or whose UI target was not found),
      +has no map: it is shown as plain SDR at paper white. A frame with a scene but no UI pass (in-engine
      +cutscenes without subtitles) is its own UI-free copy.
      +
      +`hdr_boost` in native mode is the share of the scene's highlight range shown, in log2:
      +`sqrt(boost)`. The default 0.25 shows half of it (a lamp the scene has 10x brighter than SDR
      +white comes out about 3.2x), 1 all of it (up to the peak), 0 none (the SDR picture).
      +
      +HDR metadata (`VK_EXT_hdr_metadata`): max mastering luminance is the peak, MaxFALL paper white;
      +MaxCLL is the peak in native mode and expand's SDR white level in expand mode. It changes with
      +the settings, not per frame.
      +
      +### Cost
      +
      +Per frame, a handful of commands recorded on the recording threads (`Scheduler::Record`), none
      +per draw, no readback, no wait: one dispatch at each of the three points (and a one-group sum),
      +the encode samples one more image. GPU: the scene read once (RGBA16F), the frame read twice and
      +copied once (RGBA8), a half-size RG16F and a full-size R16F written, about 55 MB at 1080p.
      +Measured (`hdr-native-shader-test --bench <w> <h>`, all passes with their barriers, RTX 5060):
      +0.18 ms at 1920x1080, 0.37 ms at 2560x1440, 0.79 ms at 3840x2160 (in the game the scene luma
      +stays at the guest's 1920x1080 for larger outputs, so a little less). Native mode off (or HDR
      +off): nothing.
      +
      +### Debug view
      +
      +`BB_HDR_DEBUG=1` shows the gain instead of the picture: the frame in grey at a third of paper
      +white, the gain over it from blue (a little) through green and yellow to red (the peak), UI that
      +native mode keeps at paper white in magenta. The square in the top left corner is green while
      +native mode has the frame's gain map and orange while the frame has none and is shown as SDR (in
      +expand mode the heat map shows expand's gain).
      +
      +The log says which mode runs (`HDR output: HDR10 (PQ, BT.2020), mode native (...)`, again when
      +it is changed in the menu) and, in native mode, when frames stop or start having a gain map
      +(`HDR native: ...`, at most every 5 s, with the number of switches in between).
      +
      +### Tests
      +
      +`ninja -C out/gpu hdr-native-shader-test` runs the passes on a synthetic frame (plain Vulkan,
      +any 1.3 device; `BB_TEST_GPU=<index>` picks one): the luma's 2x2 max/average with NaN and inf
      +texels, the bit-exact copy, the exposure of a known tonemap (exact to 0.03 stops) and its
      +resistance to bloom (0.27 stops off on the first frame, 0.001 after 60), empty frames, and the
      +gain map: exactly 1 in the midtones and on UI, the scene's ratio to the power of the strength
      +into the peak on an 8x highlight, 1 on bloom brighter than the scene. `settings-test` covers
      +`hdr_mode`.
      +
      +### Limits
      +
      +- The scene color is the pre-post scene: bloom, depth of field and motion blur are only in the
      +  SDR frame. Bloom halos stay at SDR brightness; a blurred highlight gets the gain where its
      +  sharp source is (the 4x4 footprint softens that).
      +- One exposure for the whole frame: the vignette darkens the SDR corners but not the scene, so
      +  bright highlights in the corners lose a little of the vignette.
      +- Scaled presets (output other than 1080p): the scene luma is at the guest resolution, jittered
      +  when an upscaler runs; the map is interpolated to the output.
      +- `BB_UPSCALER=none` disables the frame analysis the passes rely on: native mode shows every frame
      +  as SDR (use expand mode instead).

      # FIXES-LOG
      
      Stability and crash fixes adapted from **BloodBorneButPc** (a Windows fork of the
      shadPS4/bbport engine) into **bbhost** (this native translation layer).
      
      The two projects do not share source, so each fix is re-expressed in bbhost's own
      architecture under the same switch name that gates it in BloodBorneButPc. Where
      bbhost already solved the same problem another way, that is noted rather than
      duplicated. Long-session VRAM accumulation and the launch-time heap overflow are
      the crashes these target.
      
      ## GPU hang guard - textures freed while still in use
      
      - **Source:** `BB_GC_RECENT_FRAMES` (default 48), `BB_IMAGE_FREE_DELAY_FRAMES`
        (default 32) in BloodBorneButPc's texture cache.
      - **Files:** `src/host/textures.cpp`.
      - **Change:** each surface records the video flip of its last use
        (`Surface::used_flip`, stamped wherever `used_ms` is). The cold-texture sweep
        (`evict_cold_surfaces_locked`) and the reused-memory retire
        (`textures_retire_reused_locked`) now skip any surface used or deleted within
        `max(BB_GC_RECENT_FRAMES, BB_IMAGE_FREE_DELAY_FRAMES)` flips. Frames are the
        GPU's own timeline, so a long frame (a hitch, a load) can no longer age a
        texture out from under a submission still reading it - the
        stalled-then-device-lost class of crash.
      - **Rationale:** bbhost already defers a deleted image's Vulkan objects to
        submission retirement (`defer_destroy_image`), so the "outlive unregistration"
        half is already covered; the frame floor adds the part it lacked - a texture
        the just-recorded frame used is never a candidate for freeing.
      
      ## VRAM cleanup - accumulation over a long session
      
      - **Source:** `BB_VRAM_PRESSURE_PERCENT` (default 85), `BB_VRAM_IDLE_SECONDS`
        (default 30; 10 s above 90% of the driver's budget) in BloodBorneButPc.
      - **Files:** `src/host/textures.cpp`, `src/host/gpu.cpp`,
        `src/host/gpu_internal.h`.
      - **Change:** `evict_cold_surfaces_locked` now measures pressure as a share of
        the driver's budget (new accessor `vram_budget_bytes()`) and:
        - triggers once usage reaches `BB_VRAM_PRESSURE_PERCENT` of that budget, in
          addition to bbhost's existing reserve-and-full-heap trigger;
        - frees only textures idle for `BB_VRAM_IDLE_SECONDS`, dropping that to 10 s
          once the budget is 90% used.
        - surfaces a shader or copy wrote are still never evicted (bbhost holds state
          the guest memory underneath does not), matching BloodBorneButPc keeping
          GPU-written blocks resident.
      - **Rationale:** the original default idle of 20 s (via `BBHOST_VRAM_EVICT_S`,
        still honored, `=0` off) is kept as a fallback; the percentage line lets the
        sweep start before the reserve is hit and sweep harder as the card fills.
      
      ## Direct memory pool - launch crash on a large scene
      
      - **Source:** `BB_DMEM_MB` (BloodBorneButPc gives a scene above 1080p the
        9152 MiB pool instead of 5056 MiB).
      - **Files:** `src/hle/kernel.cpp`.
      - **Change:** `BB_DMEM_MB` names the direct memory the game is told it has (the
        stock 6 GiB otherwise), clamped to the window reserved for it (7.75 GiB).
      - **Rationale:** bbhost already grows the game's GFX heap and its direct memory
        for a scene above 1080p (`grow_gfx_heap` / `hle_kernel_set_dmem_size`,
        `engine/live_resolution.cpp`), so the >1080p policy is present; the switch
        exposes the pool size itself, and its 7.75 GiB window is the ceiling that
        BloodBorneButPc's 9152 MiB meets only as far as the window allows.
      
      ## Already present in bbhost (not re-ported)
      
      - Crash reports for host faults on a game thread (Linux `SIGSEGV` handler,
        `main.cpp`; `host/win_crash.cpp` on Windows).
      - Write faults at the end of a GPU mapping handled, unclaimed faults on guest
        pages handed access back (`core/write_watch.cpp`).
      - Unknown texture formats read as `VK_FORMAT_UNDEFINED` and are skipped instead
        of aborting; a lost/out-of-date swapchain is recreated
        (`host/window.cpp`).
      - Audio output follows the device's real rate (`host/audio.cpp`).
      - Patch write sites are checked against the expected bytes before any is
        written (`engine/patch_manifest.cpp`).
      - VM/launcher-only items (Windows error 1450 memory check, 10 GB pool, region
        patch prompt) do not apply to bbhost's Linux path.
