```
      #!/bin/bash
      # Starts bbhost and keeps its log in logs/ (the newest ten are kept).
      #   ./run-bbhost.sh                       the per-user config (~/.config/bbhost/bbhost.toml)
      #   BBHOST_CONFIG=other.toml ./run-bbhost.sh   that file on top of it
      cd "$(dirname "$0")" || exit 1
      cfg=${BBHOST_CONFIG:-bbhost.toml}
      mkdir -p logs
      log=logs/bbhost-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S).log
      ls -1t logs/bbhost-*.log 2>/dev/null | tail -n +10 | xargs -r rm -f
      args=()
      [ -f "$cfg" ] && args=(--config "$cfg")
      echo "bbhost: config ${args[1]:-per-user}, log $(pwd)/$log"
      # tee -i: Ctrl-C stops the game, not the log, so its last lines are kept.
      ./bbhost "${args[@]}" "$@" 2>&1 | tee -i "$log"
      exit "${PIPESTATUS[0]}"
      EOF
      chmod +x "$dir/run-bbhost.sh"
      
      cat > "$dir/README-linux.txt" <<EOF
      bbhost for Linux, build $name
      ==================================
      
      bbhost runs Bloodborne on PC: the game's own 1.09 executable, its calls into
      the PS4's system libraries answered by bbhost and its graphics recompiled for
      Vulkan. Free software under the GNU GPL, version 3 or later (LICENSE); the
      source is at https://github.com/droogie/bbhost.
      
      You need
        - x86-64 Linux with glibc ${glibc#GLIBC_} or newer (Ubuntu 24.04, Linux Mint 22, Debian 13,
          Fedora 39 or anything newer; Arch; a current SteamOS). Check with: ldd --version
        - A Vulkan 1.3 GPU driver and the Vulkan loader. Check with: vulkaninfo --summary
        - These system libraries (every desktop has most of them already):
              $needed
          Packages that provide them:
              Ubuntu / Debian / Mint : libvulkan1 mesa-vulkan-drivers libcurl4t64 zlib1g
              Fedora                 : vulkan-loader mesa-vulkan-drivers libcurl zlib
              Arch / SteamOS         : vulkan-icd-loader vulkan-radeon|vulkan-intel|nvidia-utils curl zlib
          NVIDIA: the proprietary driver brings its own Vulkan driver.
        - X11 or Wayland, and PulseAudio, PipeWire or ALSA for sound (SDL3 is built
          in and uses what it finds).
        - The eboot.bin of the game's 1.09 update, decrypted to an ELF (SHA-256
          941f887a562aae054fac35af8cc8f27cf075f3d4cc2e029fb5ae2a663aaa5ae7; bbhost
          stops at start and says why when it is another version), and the game
          dump with the 1.09 update's files copied over it: the CUSA00900 folder
          that contains dvdroot_ps4, whose sce_sys/param.sfo says APP_VER 01.09
          (or the update kept beside it in CUSA00900-UPDATE, the way shadPS4 keeps
          a game library). Neither is in this package.
      
      Built static: libstdc++ ($glibcxx), SDL3, ffmpeg (movie decoders only),
      SPIRV-Tools.
      
      Setup
        Untar this folder somewhere of its own, for example ~/Games/bbhost, and run
        ./run-bbhost.sh from a terminal there. The first time, the setup window
        opens: pick the game folder and the decrypted eboot with the Browse buttons
        (each turns green when it is right), then Play. ./run-bbhost.sh --setup
        opens it again.
      
        The settings are kept in ~/.config/bbhost/bbhost.toml, which every copy of
        bbhost reads, so a new download or an update needs nothing set again. The
        F10 settings and your account sign-in are kept beside it, saves and caches
        in ~/.local/share/bbhost/data.
        bbhost.example.toml lists every setting.
      
      Run
        ./run-bbhost.sh          (the log goes to logs/ and the terminal)
        The first visit to an area stutters for a moment while its graphics are
        prepared for your GPU; later visits do not. F10 in the game window opens
        the PC settings: resolution, window mode, V-Sync, frame cap, mouse, key
        bindings and your account.
      
      Online
        bbhost plays online on the community server, https://thehuntersdream.com,
        with other bbhost players (not with PS4s). The game stays offline until this
        PC is linked to an account, and the account's name is your name online.
        Link it once, in the setup window's Account section or with F10 > ACCOUNT
        at the title screen:
          - Log in with Discord (Link with Discord in F10): a code appears and your
            browser opens https://thehuntersdream.com/link. Sign in there with
            Discord, check that the page names this PC, and approve.
          - Create account on this PC: type a name (3 to 16 letters, digits, _ or
            -). A recovery code appears once. Write it down: it is the only way to
            get the account back on another PC or after reinstalling (Recover
            account takes the name and that code).
        Then choose Play Online at the title.
      
        Co-op: the host rings the Beckoning Bell and the helper the Small Resonant
        Bell, in the same area. Invasions: the Sinister Resonant Bell. The website
        has the live map of deaths and messages, the leaderboards and your account
        page (Public profile puts your name on them).
      
        Other players reach you on UDP port 9307: a firewall on this PC must let it
        in. If summons keep failing with one person, forwarding that port to this
        PC on your router often fixes it. Two PCs in one house: set p2p_addr under
        [online] in ~/.config/bbhost/bbhost.toml to each PC's local address.
      
      Steam Deck
        The release's bbhost-steamdeck tarball is this package with the Deck's
        settings (its screen's 1280x800, full screen, 30 fps) and STEAMDECK.md,
        the steps for adding it to Steam and playing in Game Mode.
      
      Plugins
        plugins/ holds the official ones, signed by the bbhost release key
        (the .sig beside each). Turn them on and set them up in the setup
        window's Plugins tab (bbhost --setup), which can also fetch the latest
        official plugins; in the game, F9 opens the plugin menu (start the boss
        rush there). Or in the per-user bbhost.toml:
            [plugins]
            randomizer = true    # every pickup and shop shuffled from a seed
            boss_rush = true     # the game's bosses back to back, timed
            mutators = true      # speed, bullet time, one-hit, chaos and more
            debug_menu = true    # the developers' debug menu: \` opens it
        Each one's settings go in a section of its own name ([randomizer],
        [boss_rush], [mutators]); docs/plugins.md in the repository lists them.
        Use the boss rush on a save of its own. Cheating against other players
        with the debug menu gets an account banned; trying it out online with
        friends is fine.
      
      Reporting a problem
        Send the log of that session from logs/ (privately: it contains your
        internet address), with what happened, when, your account name and your
        GPU. If the game crashed, the log ends with a block starting "SIGSEGV pc="
        with the registers and the frames; the release's $name.debug symbolizes
        it.
      
        A wrong picture (wrong colours, a green or black screen, missing parts):
        press F12 in the game while it shows. bbhost writes that frame, the images
        the game drew it from and its list of draws into a folder of its own in
        logs/ (logs/f12-<date>-<time>; the log names it). Pack that folder
        (tar czf f12.tar.gz logs/f12-<date>-<time>) and send it with the log.
        BBHOST_F12_PNG=1 ./run-bbhost.sh writes PNG files instead of PPM (any
        image viewer opens them, a fifth of the size); BBHOST_F12_TEXTURES=1 adds
        every texture the frame used (the game pauses while it writes them).
      EOF
      
      # Packed from a local copy with plain modes: on a filesystem without them
      # (NFS here) every file would go out executable.
      stage=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$stage"' EXIT
      cp -r "$dir" "$stage/"
      find "$stage" -type d -exec chmod 755 {} + && find "$stage" -type f -exec chmod 644 {} +
      chmod 755 "$stage/$name/bbhost" "$stage/$name/run-bbhost.sh"
      rm -f "$out/$name.tar.gz"
      tar czf "$out/$name.tar.gz" -C "$stage" --owner=0 --group=0 "$name"
      echo "package: $out/$name.tar.gz ($(( $(stat -c %s "$out/$name.tar.gz") / 1048576 )) MB); symbols: $out/$name.debug"
      
  referencedBy: {}
```

```
=== linux_portable_build.sh ===
#!/bin/bash
# Builds a bbhost that runs on other Linux machines, not just this one.
#
# A plain `cmake --build build` here links against this machine's glibc
# (2.43 on Arch today: acosf@GLIBC_2.43, __isoc23_strtol@GLIBC_2.38), its
# libstdc++ (GLIBCXX_3.4.35) and its ffmpeg 8 / SDL3 shared libraries, so the
# binary starts on an up-to-date Arch box and nowhere else. This builds inside
# an Ubuntu 24.04 root filesystem instead (glibc 2.39: Ubuntu 24.04+, Mint 22+,
# Debian 13, Fedora 40+, SteamOS, Arch), rootless (a user + mount namespace and
# chroot; no docker, no sudo), with:
#   - libstdc++ 14 and libgcc linked in (-static-libstdc++ -static-libgcc);
#   - SDL3 static (it opens X11/Wayland/PulseAudio/PipeWire itself at run time);
#   - ffmpeg static, only the movie decoders (the same cut as tools/win_deps.sh);
#   - SPIRV-Tools static (Ubuntu's .a);
#   - the Vulkan headers of this machine (headers only; the loader is the
#     player's libvulkan.so.1);
# leaving libvulkan.so.1, libcurl.so.4 and libz.so.1 (plus glibc) as the only
# shared libraries it needs, which every desktop distribution ships.
#
#   tools/linux_portable_build.sh            -> build-linux-portable/build/bbhost
#                                               (and plugins/, the official ones
#                                               tools/package_linux.sh packs)
#
# LINUX_ROOTFS is where the Ubuntu tree goes (default
# build-linux-portable/rootfs). It must be on a local filesystem that keeps
# ownership (ext4, xfs, btrfs; not NFS, where dpkg's chown fails).
set -eu
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
SRC=$PWD
W=$SRC/build-linux-portable
ROOTFS=${LINUX_ROOTFS:-$W/rootfs}
UBUNTU_BASE=${UBUNTU_BASE:-https://cdimage.ubuntu.com/ubuntu-base/releases/24.04/release/ubuntu-base-24.04.5-base-amd64.tar.gz}
SDL_TAG=${SDL_TAG:-release-3.4.16}
FFMPEG_VER=${FFMPEG_VER:-7.1.1}

if [ "${1:-}" != --inside ]; then
    mkdir -p "$W/src" "$W/prefix/include"
    # The root filesystem, once.
    if [ ! -x "$ROOTFS/usr/bin/apt-get" ]; then
        mkdir -p "$ROOTFS"
        curl -sL -m 600 -o "$W/ubuntu-base.tar.gz" "$UBUNTU_BASE"
        # A few files belong to groups the one-uid namespace cannot map; they do not matter.
        unshare -rm tar xzf "$W/ubuntu-base.tar.gz" -C "$ROOTFS" --exclude='dev/*' 2>/dev/null || true
        rm -f "$W/ubuntu-base.tar.gz"
        cp /etc/resolv.conf "$ROOTFS/etc/resolv.conf"
        echo 'APT::Sandbox::User "root";' > "$ROOTFS/etc/apt/apt.conf.d/99sandbox"
    fi
    # Sources, fetched here (the chroot has no copy of this tree's network setup).
    fetch() {  # fetch NAME URL DIR-GLOB
        if ! ls -d "$W/src"/$3 > /dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo "fetching $1"
            curl -sL -m 600 -o "$W/src/$1.tar" "$2"
            tar xf "$W/src/$1.tar" -C "$W/src"
            rm -f "$W/src/$1.tar"
        fi
    }
    fetch sdl3 "https://github.com/libsdl-org/SDL/archive/refs/tags/$SDL_TAG.tar.gz" 'SDL-*'
    fetch ffmpeg "https://ffmpeg.org/releases/ffmpeg-$FFMPEG_VER.tar.xz" 'ffmpeg-*'
    # The Vulkan headers of this machine (Ubuntu 24.04's are 1.3.275, older than
    # the renderer's), copied: the chroot cannot follow a symlink out of itself.
    rm -rf "$W/prefix/include/vulkan" "$W/prefix/include/vk_video"
    cp -r /usr/include/vulkan /usr/include/vk_video "$W/prefix/include/"
    # The revision the binary logs on its first line (cmake/version.cmake):
    # the chroot has the tree but not its git directory.
    rev=$(git -c core.excludesFile=/dev/null rev-parse --short HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)
    if [ -n "$(git -c core.excludesFile=/dev/null status --porcelain --untracked-files=no 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
        rev="$rev+"
    fi
    export BBHOST_GIT_REV=$rev
    exec unshare -rm --fork sh -c '
        R=$1; SRC=$2; shift 2
        mount --rbind /dev "$R/dev"
        mount -t proc proc "$R/proc" 2>/dev/null || mount --rbind /proc "$R/proc"
        mount --rbind /sys "$R/sys"
        mkdir -p "$R/src" && mount --bind "$SRC" "$R/src"
        exec chroot "$R" /usr/bin/env -i PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin \
            HOME=/root DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive LANG=C.UTF-8 BBHOST_GIT_REV="$BBHOST_GIT_REV" \
            bash /src/tools/linux_portable_build.sh --inside
    ' sh "$ROOTFS" "$SRC"
fi

# --- inside the Ubuntu 24.04 root ---------------------------------------------
W=/src/build-linux-portable
P=$W/prefix
# libstdc++ 14, not 24.04's default 13: the HLE libc calls std::acosf and friends,
# which libstdc++ has only had since 14. Clang takes the newest GCC it finds.
if [ ! -x /usr/bin/clang ] || [ ! -f /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libSPIRV-Tools-opt.a ] || [ ! -d /usr/include/c++/14 ]; then
    apt-get update -q > /tmp/apt-update.log 2>&1
    apt-get install -y -q --no-install-recommends clang lld llvm cmake ninja-build pkg-config make nasm \
        libstdc++-14-dev libcurl4-openssl-dev libvulkan-dev zlib1g-dev spirv-tools \
        libx11-dev libxext-dev libxrandr-dev libxcursor-dev libxi-dev libxfixes-dev libxss-dev libxtst-dev \
        libxkbcommon-dev libwayland-dev wayland-protocols libegl-dev libdecor-0-dev libpulse-dev \
        libasound2-dev libpipewire-0.3-dev libdbus-1-dev libudev-dev libdrm-dev libgbm-dev \
        ca-certificates file python3 xz-utils > /tmp/apt-install.log 2>&1 || { tail -20 /tmp/apt-install.log; exit 1; }
fi
export CC=clang CXX=clang++

# SDL3, static. Its video/audio backends are opened with dlopen at run time,
# so the player's X11 or Wayland and PulseAudio or PipeWire are used as found.
if [ ! -f "$P/lib/libSDL3.a" ]; then
    s=$(ls -d $W/src/SDL-* | head -1)
    cmake -S "$s" -B "$W/sdl3" -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX="$P" \
        -DCMAKE_INSTALL_LIBDIR=lib -DSDL_SHARED=OFF -DSDL_STATIC=ON -DSDL_TEST_LIBRARY=OFF -DSDL_TESTS=OFF \
        -DSDL_EXAMPLES=OFF -DCMAKE_POSITION_INDEPENDENT_CODE=ON > "$W/sdl3-configure.log"
    cmake --build "$W/sdl3" > "$W/sdl3-build.log"
    cmake --install "$W/sdl3" > /dev/null
fi

# ffmpeg, only what the movies need (tools/win_deps.sh has the reasons), static.
if [ ! -f "$P/lib/libavcodec.a" ]; then
    f=$(ls -d $W/src/ffmpeg-* | head -1)
    mkdir -p "$W/ffmpeg"
    (cd "$W/ffmpeg" && "$f/configure" --prefix="$P" --cc=clang --cxx=clang++ --enable-static --disable-shared \
        --enable-pic --disable-programs --disable-doc --disable-network --disable-everything \
        --enable-decoder=h264,hevc,aac,mp3 --enable-demuxer=mov,mp3,aac --enable-parser=h264,hevc,aac \
        --enable-protocol=file --enable-swscale --enable-swresample --disable-avdevice --disable-avfilter \
        --disable-postproc --disable-debug --disable-vaapi --disable-vdpau --disable-xlib --disable-libdrm \
        --disable-iconv --disable-zlib --disable-bzlib --disable-lzma --extra-cflags=-O2 \
        > "$W/ffmpeg-configure.log" 2>&1 \
        && make -j"$(nproc)" > "$W/ffmpeg-build.log" 2>&1 && make install > "$W/ffmpeg-install.log" 2>&1) \
        || { tail -20 "$W/ffmpeg-configure.log" "$W/ffmpeg-build.log"; exit 1; }
fi

# ffmpeg's .pc files ask for -latomic, a shared library that is not on every
# machine (Fedora keeps it in its own package): the static archive instead.
sed -i 's/ -latomic/ -l:libatomic.a/' "$P"/lib/pkgconfig/*.pc

# bbhost. pkg-config sees only the prefix's ffmpeg; the static archives'
# private libraries (-lm, -lpthread) come with libstdc++'s.
export PKG_CONFIG_PATH=$P/lib/pkgconfig
cmake -S /src -B "$W/build" -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo \
    -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="$P" -DVulkan_INCLUDE_DIR="$P/include" \
    -DCMAKE_EXE_LINKER_FLAGS="-static-libstdc++ -static-libgcc -fuse-ld=lld" \
    -DCMAKE_MODULE_LINKER_FLAGS="-static-libgcc -fuse-ld=lld" > "$W/bbhost-configure.log"
grep -E "^-- bbhost" "$W/bbhost-configure.log" || true
cmake --build "$W/build" --target bbhost bb_plugin_hello bb_plugin_randomizer bb_plugin_boss_rush bb_plugin_mutators -j"$(nproc)" > "$W/bbhost-build.log" 2>&1 \
    || { grep -E "error|undefined" "$W/bbhost-build.log" | head -30; exit 1; }
echo "portable build: $W/build/bbhost"
=== package_steamdeck.sh head ===
#!/bin/bash
# The Steam Deck kit: the Linux package (tools/package_linux.sh's) with the
# Deck's settings - tools/steamdeck/bbhost-steamdeck.toml: its screen's
# 1280x800, full screen, 30 fps - STEAMDECK.md, and the launcher pointed at
# them. The game's paths stay in the per-user config, as for every package.
#   tools/package_steamdeck.sh LINUX_TARBALL OUTDIR
set -eu
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
lin_tgz=$(realpath "$1"); out=$(realpath -m "$2")
sd=$PWD/tools/steamdeck
mkdir -p "$out"
work=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
(cd "$work" && tar xzf "$lin_tgz")
ldir=$(ls -d "$work"/bbhost-linux-* | head -1)
name=$(basename "$ldir" | sed 's/^bbhost-linux-/bbhost-steamdeck-/')
cp "$sd/bbhost-steamdeck.toml" "$sd/STEAMDECK.md" "$ldir/"
sed -i 's/^cfg=\${BBHOST_CONFIG:-bbhost.toml}/cfg=${BBHOST_CONFIG:-bbhost-steamdeck.toml}/' "$ldir/run-bbhost.sh"
grep -q 'bbhost-steamdeck.toml' "$ldir/run-bbhost.sh" || { echo "run-bbhost.sh: config line not found"; exit 1; }
sed -i 's/^  bbhost.example.toml lists every setting./  bbhost.example.toml lists every setting; STEAMDECK.md has the Steam Deck steps./' "$ldir/README-linux.txt"
grep -q 'STEAMDECK.md' "$ldir/README-linux.txt" || { echo "README-linux.txt: settings line not found"; exit 1; }
find "$ldir" -type d -exec chmod 755 {} + && find "$ldir" -type f -exec chmod 644 {} +
chmod 755 "$ldir/bbhost" "$ldir/run-bbhost.sh"
mv "$ldir" "$work/$name"
(cd "$work" && rm -f "$out/$name.tar.gz" && tar czf "$out/$name.tar.gz" --owner=0 --group=0 "$name")
ls -la "$out/$name.tar.gz"

```
```
#!/bin/bash
# Copies the official plugins of a build into a package's plugins/ folder,
# without their DWARF, and signs each one (docs/plugins.md, "Official
# plugins"): <file>.sig is the release key's Ed25519 signature over the file
# as shipped, which the host checks before it loads the plugin.
#   tools/package_plugins.sh BUILD_PLUGIN_DIR PACKAGE_PLUGIN_DIR
# The key comes from RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY (the PEM text: the release workflow's
# secret) or RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY_FILE; without either the plugins ship unsigned.
set -eu
from=$1; to=$2
plugins="randomizer boss_rush mutators debug_menu"
mkdir -p "$to"
key=""
if [ -n "${RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY:-}" ]; then
    key=$(mktemp); chmod 600 "$key"
    printf '%s\n' "$RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY" > "$key"
elif [ -n "${RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY_FILE:-}" ]; then
    key=$RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY_FILE
fi
n=0
for p in $plugins; do
    for f in "$from/$p.so" "$from/$p.dll"; do
        [ -f "$f" ] || continue
        out="$to/$(basename "$f")"
        objcopy --strip-debug "$f" "$out" 2>/dev/null || llvm-objcopy --strip-debug "$f" "$out" 2>/dev/null || cp "$f" "$out"
        if [ -n "$key" ]; then
            openssl pkeyutl -sign -inkey "$key" -rawin -in "$out" -out "$out.sig"
        fi
        n=$((n + 1))
    done
done
[ -n "${RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY:-}" ] && rm -f "$key"
echo "plugins: $n packed into $to$( [ -n "$key" ] && echo ', signed' || echo ', unsigned')"
# Every package carries every official plugin: a missing one is a build that
# did not make it, not something to ship around.
want=$(echo $plugins | wc -w)
if [ "$n" -lt "$want" ]; then
    echo "package_plugins: $n of $want official plugins found in $from - build their targets first" >&2
    exit 1
fi
```

## What the scripts give you instead

Your `build-ci/build/bbhost` is **not redistributable** — without `CI_PORTABLE=1`, `ci_build.sh` leaves `static=""` (`:99`) and links the server's libstdc++ and glibc, so it runs on machines at least as new as that server and nowhere else. For something you can hand to another machine:

```sh
CI_PORTABLE=1 tools/ci_build.sh                                  # static libstdc++/libgcc
tools/package_linux.sh build-ci/build/bbhost build/linux
```

or the rootless-chroot route that needs no sudo, `tools/linux_portable_build.sh` (Ubuntu 24.04 rootfs, glibc 2.39 floor), then `tools/package_linux.sh` with no args.

Output: `build/linux/bbhost-linux-<rev>.tar.gz` (binary stripped, `patches/`, signed-`plugins/`, `bbhost.example.toml`, `run-bbhost.sh` that logs to `logs/`, and an empty `data/ logs/ build/`) plus `<rev>.debug` for symbolising.

- `package_linux.sh` calls `package_plugins.sh`, which **exits 1 unless all four** of `randomizer boss_rush mutators debug_menu` are in the build dir (`package_plugins.sh:35-38`). === package_steamdeck.sh (full) ===
```
#!/bin/bash
# The Steam Deck kit: the Linux package (tools/package_linux.sh's) with the
# Deck's settings - tools/steamdeck/bbhost-steamdeck.toml: its screen's
# 1280x800, full screen, 30 fps - STEAMDECK.md, and the launcher pointed at
# them. The game's paths stay in the per-user config, as for every package.
#   tools/package_steamdeck.sh LINUX_TARBALL OUTDIR
set -eu
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
lin_tgz=$(realpath "$1"); out=$(realpath -m "$2")
sd=$PWD/tools/steamdeck
mkdir -p "$out"
work=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
(cd "$work" && tar xzf "$lin_tgz")
ldir=$(ls -d "$work"/bbhost-linux-* | head -1)
name=$(basename "$ldir" | sed 's/^bbhost-linux-/bbhost-steamdeck-/')
cp "$sd/bbhost-steamdeck.toml" "$sd/STEAMDECK.md" "$ldir/"
sed -i 's/^cfg=\${BBHOST_CONFIG:-bbhost.toml}/cfg=${BBHOST_CONFIG:-bbhost-steamdeck.toml}/' "$ldir/run-bbhost.sh"
grep -q 'bbhost-steamdeck.toml' "$ldir/run-bbhost.sh" || { echo "run-bbhost.sh: config line not found"; exit 1; }
sed -i 's/^  bbhost.example.toml lists every setting./  bbhost.example.toml lists every setting; STEAMDECK.md has the Steam Deck steps./' "$ldir/README-linux.txt"
grep -q 'STEAMDECK.md' "$ldir/README-linux.txt" || { echo "README-linux.txt: settings line not found"; exit 1; }
find "$ldir" -type d -exec chmod 755 {} + && find "$ldir" -type f -exec chmod 644 {} +
chmod 755 "$ldir/bbhost" "$ldir/run-bbhost.sh"
mv "$ldir" "$work/$name"
(cd "$work" && rm -f "$out/$name.tar.gz" && tar czf "$out/$name.tar.gz" --owner=0 --group=0 "$name")
ls -la "$out/$name.tar.gz"
=== steamdeck toml ===
# bbhost - Steam Deck settings: the screen's own 1280x800, full screen, the
# game's own 30 fps.
#
# Leave this file as it is. The game's paths are not set here: they live in
# your per-user config (~/.config/bbhost/bbhost.toml), which the first start
# writes (the setup window asks for them) and every copy of bbhost reads - see
# STEAMDECK.md. This file only sets what suits the Deck. The F10 screen and
# the game's PC Graphics menu still change any of it; those changes (and the
# account sign-in) are kept for this kit alone, beside the per-user config.

[video]
# The window: the Deck's screen. In Game Mode it is shown full screen anyway.
width = 1280
height = 800
# What the game renders at: the screen's own size. At 16:10 the world fills
# the screen and the HUD and menus stay 16:9 in the middle.
resolution = "1280x800"
window_mode = "Fullscreen"
# The game's own pace. With the Deck's screen at 40 Hz (Steam's performance
# menu), 40 is worth a try.
fps_cap = 30

[startup]
# Skip the company logos at start.
skip_intro = true
=== STEAMDECK.md (head 60) ===
# bbhost on the Steam Deck

This is the Linux build of bbhost with settings for the Deck: it renders at
the screen's own 1280x800, full screen, at the game's 30 fps
(`bbhost-steamdeck.toml`). It runs natively on SteamOS; nothing needs
installing. You bring the game: the CUSA00900 dump with the 1.09 update's
files over it, and the 1.09 `eboot.bin` decrypted to an ELF (README-linux.txt
says how to check both).

## Set it up (Desktop Mode, once)

1. Switch to Desktop Mode (Steam button, Power, Switch to Desktop).
2. Copy the game dump and the decrypted eboot onto the Deck - the internal
   storage or the SD card (`/run/media/...`) both work.
3. Extract this archive into your home folder, for example `~/Games`
   (right-click it in Dolphin, Extract, Extract archive here).
4. Add it to Steam: open Steam, Games, "Add a Non-Steam Game to My
   Library...", Browse, set the file type to All Files, pick `run-bbhost.sh`
   in the extracted folder, Add Selected Programs. Its Properties can rename
   it (Bloodborne, say).
5. Start it from Steam (Library, Non-Steam) - here in Desktop Mode too. The
   first start opens the setup window (the touchscreen or the right trackpad
   work it): pick the game folder (the one with `dvdroot_ps4` in it) and the
   eboot, then Play. Check that the title screen comes up, then quit.

Always start it from Steam, not by double-clicking `run-bbhost.sh` or from
Konsole. Outside Steam, Steam's desktop controls stay on: A, B and Y also
send Return, Escape and Space, the d-pad the arrow keys, the triggers mouse
clicks - so every button does two things, and the menus open and close on
their own. bbhost says so on screen when it sees it.

## Play (Game Mode)

Switch back to Game Mode and start it from your Library (Non-Steam). The
Deck's controls are the game's pad. If the sticks or buttons act as a mouse
and keyboard instead, pick the Gamepad layout in its controller settings
(Steam button, Controller Settings).

- The game's System menu has a **Steam Deck** section, on a Deck only, and
  the PC sections (PC Graphics: resolution, PC Settings: frame cap and
  more). F10 opens the host's own options screen (account, updates, keys);
  without a keyboard, give F10 to one of the back buttons in the controller
  settings.
- These settings and the account sign-in are kept for this kit alone, so a
  copy of bbhost on a PC keeps its own; the game's paths are shared.
- The first minutes in a new area compile shaders and can stutter; they are
  kept, so the next start is smoother.
- **30 or 60 fps**: System, Steam Deck, Frame Rate. 30 fps renders at the
  screen's own 1280x800, the game's own pace and the Deck's default here.
  60 fps renders at 960x600 and bbhost scales the picture up to the screen
  with AMD's FSR 1, which keeps edges sharp, with Model Detail at Low (it
  draws distant buildings one step coarser, which is hard to see on this
  screen): the heaviest views found, like the first gate in Central
  Yharnam, hold 60. The resolution and the model detail change at once; the
  frame rate itself on the next start. The Deck's GPU cannot draw the game
  at its full 1280x800 sixty times a second (about 45). The same section's
  Model Detail can be set on its own (Normal at 60 fps holds 60 walking,
  about 58.5 at the heaviest views), and PC Graphics' Resolution offers
  1024x640, a little sharper and a little less steady. In Game Mode set the screen to 60 Hz in the performance
  overlay (... button, Performance, Refresh Rate), so every frame is shown
```

> _Reasoning_
> My ICO parsing had a bug (struct format). Entry format: width(1) height(1) colorcount(1) reserved(1) planes(2) bitcount(2) bytesInRes(4) imageOffset(4) = 16 bytes → '<BBBBHHII' is B B B B H H I I = 4+2+2+4+4 = 16. That's 8 fields, and I unpacked into 9 names (w,h,c,r,p,planes,bpp,size,offset) = 9. My mistake. Fix: w,h,c,r,planes,bpp,size,offset = 8.

> ```sh
> #!/bin/sh
> # AppRun: run bbhost from the mounted AppDir; the AppImage is read-only, so
> # the log and the frame dumps go under ~/.local/share/bbhost instead of
> # beside the binary.

````
    # appimagetool ![Downloads](https://img.shields.io/github/downloads/AppImage/appimagetool/total.svg) [![irc](https://img.shields.io/badge/IRC-%23AppImage%20on%20libera.chat-blue.svg)](https://web.libera.chat/#AppImage) [![Donate](https://img.shields.io/badge/Donate-PayPal-green.svg)](https://www.paypal.com/cgi-bin/webscr?cmd=_s-xclick&hosted_button_id=ZT9CL8M5TJU72)
    ## Usage
    `appimagetool` is used to generate an AppImage from an existing `AppDir`. Many community-provided higher-level [tools for deploying applications in AppImage format](https://github.com/AppImageCommunity/awesome-appimage/blob/main/README.md#appimage-developer-tools) use it internally. A precompiled version can be downloaded on [GitHub Releases](../..//releases), but in most cases you will be better off using one of the higher-level tools instead of using `appimagetool` directly.
    Usage in a nutshell, assuming that you already have an [AppDir](https://github.com/AppImage/AppImageSpec/blob/master/draft.md#appdir) in place:
    ```
    ARCH=x86_64 ./appimagetool-x86_64.AppImage some.AppDir
    ```
    Detailed usage:
    ```
    Usage:
    appimagetool [OPTION...] SOURCE [DESTINATION] - Generate AppImages from existing AppDirs
    Help Options:
    -h, --help Show help options
    Application Options:
    -l, --list List files in SOURCE AppImage
    -u, --updateinformation Embed update information STRING; if zsyncmake is installed, generate zsync file
    -g, --guess Guess update information based on environment variables set by common CI systems (GitHub actions, GitLab CI)
    --version Show version number
    -v, --verbose Produce verbose output
    -s, --sign Sign with gpg[2]
    --comp Squashfs compression
    -n, --no-appstream Do not check AppStream metadata
    --exclude-file Uses given file as exclude file for mksquashfs, in addition to .appimageignore.
    --runtime-file Runtime file to use
    --sign-key Key ID to use for gpg[2] signatures
    --sign-args Extra arguments to use when signing with gpg[2]
    ```
    ### Environment variables
    Some of the parameters above can alternatively be specified as environment variables. Also, some additional environment variables are available, too.
    - `ARCH`: Needs to be set whenever appimagetool cannot automatically determine the architecture of the binaries inside the AppDir to choose a suitable runtime (e.g., when binaries for multiple architectures or just shell scripts are contained in there).
    - `APPIMAGETOOL_APP_NAME`: If no destination is set by the user, appimagetool automatically generates a suitable output filename, using the root desktop entry's `Name` field. With this environment variable, this value can be set explicitly by the user.
    - `APPIMAGETOOL_SIGN_PASSPHRASE`: If the `--sign-key` is encrypted and requires a passphrase to be used for signing (and, for some reason, GnuPG cannot be used interactively, e.g., in a CI environment), this environment variable can be used to safely pass the key.
    - `APPIMAGETOOL_RUNTIME_FILE`: Path to a local AppImage runtime. If `--runtime-file` is specified, it takes precedence over this environment variable.
    - `VERSION`: This value will be inserted by appimagetool into the root desktop file and (if the destination parameter is not provided by the user) in the output filename.
    ## Building
    To build for various architectures on a local machine (or on GitHub Codespaces) using Docker:
    * For 64 bit Intel, run `ARCH=x86_64 bash ./ci/build-in-docker.sh`
    * For 32 bit Intel, run `ARCH=i686 bash ./ci/build-in-docker.sh`
    If you are on an Intel machine and would like to cross-compile for ARM:
    * Prepare the Docker system for cross-compiling with `docker run --rm --privileged multiarch/qemu-user-static --reset -p yes`, then run
    * For 64 bit ARM, run `ARCH=aarch64 bash ./ci/build-in-docker.sh`
    * For 32 bit ARM, run `ARCH=armhf bash ./ci/build-in-docker.sh`
    ## Changelog
    * Unlike previous versions of this tool provided in the [AppImageKit](https://github.com/AppImage/AppImageKit/) repository, this version downloads the latest AppImage runtime (which will become part of the AppImage) from https://github.com/AppImage/type2-runtime/releases. If you do not like this (or if your build system does not have Internet access), you can supply a locally downloaded AppImage runtime using the `APPIMAGETOOL_RUNTIME_FILE` environment variable or `--runtime-file` parameter instead.
````

```
    # AppImage Specification
    #### Working Draft
    The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in [RFC 2119](https://www.ietf.org/rfc/rfc2119.txt).

    [Introduction]: #introduction "Introduction"
    [Revision History]: #revision-history "Revision History"
    [Definitions]: #definitions "Definitions"
    [Specification]: #specification "Specification"
    [Image format]: #image-format "Specification - Image Format"
    [Type 0 image format]: #type-0-image-format "Specification - Image Format - Type 0 image format"
    [Type 1 image format]: #type-1-image-format "Specification - Image Format - Type 1 image format"
    [Type 2 image format]: #type-2-image-format "Specification - Image Format - Type 2 image format"
    [Contents of the image]: #contents-of-the-image "Specification - Contents of the image"
    [The filesystem image]: #the-filesystem-image "Specification - Contents of the image - The filesystem image"
    [The AppRun file]: #the-apprun-file "Specification - Contents of the image - The AppRun file"
    [The payload application]: #the-payload-application "Specification - Contents of the image - The payload application"
    [Metadata]: #metadata "Specification - Metadata"

    [Desktop Integration]: #desktop-integration "Specification - Desktop Integration"
    ## Introduction
    The AppImage Specification describes [AppImage], a format to deploy application software to Linux-based operating systems.
    ## Revision History
    Version | Date | Notes
    --- | --- | ---
    Draft | 2016-06-15 | Initial draft of the AppImage Specification started
    Draft | 2016-09-18 | Type 2 image format drafted
    ## Definitions
    ##### AppDir
    Application directories as used in the [ROX Desktop](http://rox.sourceforge.net/) - <http://rox.sourceforge.net/desktop/AppDirs.html>
    [AppDir]: #appdir "AppDir: Application Directory (as used in the ROX Desktop)"
    ##### AppImage
    The AppImage file format which can be used to deploy application software to Linux-based operating systems. Depending on the context, the term can also refer to an application packaged in this format
    [AppImage]: #appimage "AppImage: The packaging format defined in this Specification, or an application packaged in this format"
    ##### AppImageKit
    Reference implementation for building AppImages. <https://github.com/probonopd/AppImageKit>
    [AppImageKit]: #appimagekit "AppImageKit: A packaging tool for building AppImages"
    ##### .desktop file
    A Desktop Entry File following the [Desktop Entry Specification](https://specifications.freedesktop.org/desktop-entry-spec/latest/)
    [.desktop file]: #desktop-file ".desktop file: A Desktop Entry File following the Desktop Entry Specificiation"
    ##### MIME Types
    MIME type definitions are spread across several resources. The MIME type definitions should be in compliance with [RFC 6838](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6838)
    [MIME Type]: #mime-type "MIME Type: A media type or file format identifier"
    ##### Payload application
    The software application contained inside an AppImage
    [payload application]: #payload-application "Payload application: The software application contained within an AppImage"
    ##### Target system(s)
    The target system(s) the application software packaged as an [AppImage] is intended to run on. The person or group creating an [AppImage] can decide which target systems the [AppImage] needs to run on, and **SHOULD** communicate the system requirements clearly to users
    [target system]: #target-systems "Target System(s): The system(s) on which an AppImage is intended to run"
    ##### zsync
    A file transfer algorithm which implements efficient download of only the content of a file which is not already known to the receiver. <http://zsync.moria.org.uk/paper/>
    [zsync]: #zsync "zsync: A file transfer program that facilitates delta updates"
    ## Specification
    ### Image format
    The image format determines how an [AppImage] is represented on disk. Currently there are two defined image formats, however, there could be additional image formats in the future.
    #### Type 0 image format
    Reserved for not fully standards-compliant AppImages (e.g., portable binaries that look and behave like AppImages on a user level, but do not conform to a standard on a programming level).
    #### Type 1 image format
    An [AppImage] which conforms to the type 1 image format:
    * **MUST** be an [ISO 9660](https://www.ecma-international.org/publications/standards/Ecma-119.htm) file
    * **MUST** use [Rock Ridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_9660#Rock_Ridge) extensions
    * **MAY** use [Joliet](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/imapi/disc-formats#joliet) extensions
    * **SHOULD** use [zisofs](http://fileformats.archiveteam.org/wiki/Zisofs) compression
    * **MUST** be a valid [ELF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Executable_and_Linkable_Format) executable
    * **MUST**, when executed, mount the [AppImage] and execute the executable file `AppRun` contained in the root of the ISO 9660 filesystem
    * **MUST NOT** rely on any specific file name extension, although it is **RECOMMENDED** that the file name extension `.AppImage` is used whenever a file name extension is desired. Futher it is **RECOMMENDED** to follow the naming scheme `ApplicationName-$VERSION-$ARCH.AppImage` in cases in which it is desired to convey this information in the file name
    * **SHOULD NOT** be encapsulated in another archive/container format during download or when stored
    * **MUST** work when spaces are used in its own filesystem path, in its own file name and in paths and filenames it uses internally
    * **MAY** embed [update information] in the ISO 9660 Volume Descriptor field (offset 33651). If the information in this location is not in one of the known [update information] formats, then it **SHOULD** be empty and/or be ignored
    * **SHOULD** contain the magic hex `0x414901` at offset 8 ([why?](https://github.com/probonopd/AppImageKit/issues/144))
    #### Type 2 image format
    An [AppImage] which conforms to the type 2 image format:
    * **MUST** be a valid [ELF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Executable_and_Linkable_Format) executable
    * **MUST** have appended to it a filesystem that the ELF part can mount
    * **MUST**, when executed, mount the [AppImage] and execute the executable file `AppRun` contained in the root of the filesystem image
    * **MUST NOT** rely on any specific file name extension, although it is **RECOMMENDED** that the file name extension `.AppImage` is used whenever a file name extension is desired. Futher it is **RECOMMENDED** to follow the naming scheme `ApplicationName-$VERSION-$ARCH.AppImage` in cases in which it is desired to convey this information in the file name
    * **SHOULD NOT** be encapsulated in another archive/container format during download or when stored
    * **MUST** work when spaces are used in its own filesystem path, in its own file name and in paths and filenames it uses internally
    * **MAY** embed [update information] in the ELF section `.upd_info`. If the information in this location is not in one of the known [update information] formats, then it **SHOULD** be empty and/or be ignored
    * **MAY** embed a digital signature in the ELF section `.sha256_sig`. If this section exists then it **MUST** either be empty (filled with `0x00` padding) or contain a valid digital signature of the sha256 of the AppImage assuming the ELF section `.sha256_sig` being filled with `0x00` padding ([why?](https://github.com/probonopd/AppImageKit/issues/238#issuecomment-249412813))
    * **MUST** contain the magic hex `0x414902` at offset 8 ([why?](https://github.com/probonopd/AppImageKit/issues/144))
    ### Contents of the image
    #### The filesystem image:
    * Is an [AppDir]
    * **MUST** contain a file named `AppRun` in its root directory
    * **SHOULD** contain a [payload application] that is ultimately executed when the [AppImage] is executed
    * **SHOULD** contain exactly one `$APPNAME.desktop` file in its root directory with `$APPNAME` being the name of the [payload application]
    * **SHOULD** contain icon files below `usr/share/icons/hicolor` following the [Icon Theme Specification](https://standards.freedesktop.org/icon-theme-spec/icon-theme-spec-latest.html) for the icon identifier as set in the `Icon=` key of the `$APPNAME.desktop` file. If present, these icon files **SHOULD** be given preference as the icon being used to represent the [AppImage].
    * **MAY** contain an `$APPICON.svg`, `$APPICON.svgz` or `$APPICON.png` file in its root directory with `$APPICON` being the icon identifier as set in the `Icon=` key of the `$APPNAME.desktop` file. If present and no icon files matching the icon identifier present below `usr/share/icons/hicolor`, this icon **SHOULD** be given preference as the icon being used to represent the [AppImage]. If a PNG file, the icon **SHOULD** be of size 256x256, 512x512, or 1024x1024 pixels.
    * **MUST** contain a `.DirIcon` file as per the [AppDir] specification which **SHOULD** be a 256x256 PNG file.
    #### The `AppRun` file:
    * **MUST** be executable and, when executed, launch the [payload application] either directly or indirectly (i.e., by invoking other helper binaries or scripts which, in turn, launch the [payload application])
    * **MAY** be an ELF binary or an interpreted script
    * If it is an ELF binary, it **SHOULD** have as few runtime dependencies as possible
    * If it is an interpreted script, it **SHOULD** be written in a language in which an interpreter can be assumed to be available on every [target system]
    * **MUST** work even when stored in a filesystem path that contains blanks
    * **SHOULD** pass any arguments passed to it to the [payload application] either directly or indirectly (i.e., by invoking other helper binaries or scripts which, in turn, launch the [payload application]) if it is not explicitly deemed useful otherwise
    * **SHOULD** pass any environment variables passed to it to the [payload application] either directly or indirectly (i.e., by invoking other helper binaries or scripts which, in turn, launch the [payload application]) if it is not explicitly deemed useful otherwise
    * **MAY** `cd` to a directory inside the [AppImage] at runtime before executing the [payload application], commonly `./usr/`
    #### The [payload application]:
    * **MAY** be an ELF binary or an interpreted script
    * If it is an ELF binary, it **SHOULD** have as few dynamic library dependencies as possible and each dynamic library dependency **MUST** be included in the [AppImage] *IF* it cannot be assumed to be part of every [target system] in a recent enough version
    * If it is an interpreted script, it **SHOULD** be written in a language in which an interpreter can be assumed to be available on every [target system], otherwise the interpreter **MUST** be included in the [AppImage]
    * It is **RECOMMENDED** that the [payload application] and its dependencies are located in a `$PREFIX` directory tree inside the [AppDir] with `$PREFIX` commonly being `./usr/`; it is **RECOMMENDED** that the `$PREFIX` directory tree inside the [AppDir] follows the [File System Hierarchy conventions for `/usr`](https://refspecs.linuxfoundation.org/FHS_3.0/fhs/ch04.html)
    ### Metadata
    Section to be expanded; additional metadata is being discussed on <https://github.com/probonopd/AppImageKit/issues/59>
    #### AppStream
    An [AppImage] **SHOULD** ship AppStream metadata in `usr/share/metainfo/$ID.appdata.xml` wi
```

> ```bash
> #!/bin/bash
> # Packs bbhost into an AppImage: one file to run, no install, nothing to
> # unpack - add it to Steam as a non-Steam game or run it from a terminal. It
> # packs the Linux package (tools/package_linux.sh's tarball) rather than the
> # bare binary, so what the tarball carries comes with it: the patch manifests
> # (patches/), the official plugins, bbhost.example.toml and a README.
> #
> #   tools/package_appimage.sh [INPUT] [OUTDIR]
> #     INPUT   build/linux/bbhost-linux-*.tar.gz (tools/package_linux.sh), or a
> #             bbhost binary, which is packed into that tarball first. Default:
> #             the newest tarball in build/linux.
> #     OUTDIR  default build/appimage
> #
> #   BB_APPIMAGE_BUILD=1   build the tarball first, then pack it:
> #                         CI_PORTABLE=1 BB_MARCH=... tools/ci_build.sh and
> #                         tools/package_linux.sh build-ci/build/bbhost build/linux
> #   BB_MARCH=<flags>      compiler flags for that build (e.g. znver2, native).
> #                         Empty by default: the AppImage runs on other machines.
> #   BB_APPIMAGE_PROFILE=steamdeck   the Deck's settings; tools/package_appimage_steamdeck.sh sets it
> #   APPIMAGETOOL=<path>   use this appimagetool instead of downloading one
> #   APPIMAGETOOL_RUNTIME=<path>  the AppImage runtime to embed (appimagetool
> #                         downloads one otherwise, which needs network access)
> #   JOBS=<n>              parallel jobs for BB_APPIMAGE_BUILD (default nproc)
> #
> # An AppImage mounts read-only, so the log and the F12 frame dumps cannot go
> # beside the binary as they do in the tarball: AppRun puts them in
> # ${XDG_DATA_HOME:-~/.local/share}/bbhost/logs. The per-user config
> # (~/.config/bbhost/bbhost.toml), the saves and the shader caches are in the
> # same places as for every other bbhost.
> set -eu
> cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

> # An AppImage of bbhost: one file to run, nothing to install and nothing to

-e \"$input\" ]; then\n    echo \"nothing to pack: pass tools/package_linux.sh's tarball or a bbhost binary, or set\"\n    echo \"BB_APPIMAGE_BUILD=1 to build one (no tarball in build/linux)\"\n    exit 1\nfi\n\nmkdir -p \"$work/pkg\"\ncase \"$input\" in\n    *.tar.gz | *.tgz)\n        cp \"$input\" \"$work/pkg.tgz\"\n        ;;\n    *)\n        # A binary: the Linux package is what knows how to lay a bbhost out\n        # (the manifests, the plugins, the launcher), so build one from it.\n        [ -x \"$input\" ] || { echo \"$input is neither a .tar.gz nor an executable\"; exit 1; }\n        tools/package_linux.sh \"$input\" \"$work/linux\"\n        cp \"$work\"/linux/bbhost-linux-*.tar.gz \"$work/pkg.tgz\"\n        ;;\nesac\ntar xzf \"$work/pkg.tgz\" -C \"$work/pkg\"\npkg=$(ls -d \"$work\"/pkg/bbhost-linux-* 2>/dev/null | head -1)\n[ -n \"$pkg\" ] || { echo \"the package has no bbhost-linux-* folder\"; exit 1; }\n\nbase=$(basename \"$pkg\")\nname=$base\n[ \"$profile\" = steamdeck ] && name=$(echo \"$base\" | sed 's/^bbhost-linux-/bbhost-steamdeck-/')\nappdir=$work/$name.AppDir\nmkdir -p \"$appdir\"\ncp -r \"$pkg\"/. \"$appdir\"/\n# The tarball's write targets (the run fills them): a mounted AppImage cannot,\n# and AppRun sends those writes somewhere writable instead.\nrm -rf \"$appdir/data\" \"$appdir/logs\" \"$appdir/build\"\n\nif [ \"$profile\" = steamdeck ]; then\n    cp tools/steamdeck/bbhost-steamdeck.toml tools/steamdeck/STEAMDECK.md \"$appdir\"/\n    # The same edit tools/package_steamdeck.sh makes, so an extracted AppImage's\n    # launcher uses the Deck's settings too.\n    sed -i 's/^cfg=\\${BBHOST_CONFIG:-bbhost.toml}/cfg=${BBHOST_CONFIG:-bbhost-steamdeck.toml}/' \"$appdir/run-bbhost.sh\"\n    grep -q 'bbhost-steamdeck.toml' \"$appdir/run-bbhost.sh\" ||\n        { echo \"run-bbhost.sh: config line not found\"; exit 1; }\nfi\n\ncat > \"$appdir/AppRun\" <<'EOF'\n#!/bin/bash\n# AppRun: starts bbhost out of the mounted AppImage. The image is read-only, so\n# the session's log goes to ${XDG_DATA_HOME:-~/.local/share}/bbhost/logs (the\n# newest ten are kept) and an F12 frame dump to a folder of its own there.\n# Arguments are passed on, so --setup works.\nset -o pipefail\nhere=${APPDIR:-$(cd \"$(dirname \"$0\")\" && pwd)}\ndata=${XDG_DATA_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share}/bbhost\nmkdir -p \"$data/logs\"\nlog=$data/logs/bbhost-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S).log\nls -1t \"$data\"/logs/bbhost-*.log 2>/dev/null | tail -n +10 | xargs -r rm -f\ncfg=${BBHOST_CONFIG:-}\nif [ -z \"$cfg\" ] && [ -f \"$here/bbhost-steamdeck.toml\" ]; then\n    cfg=$here/bbhost-steamdeck.toml\nfi\nargs=()\nif [ -n \"$cfg\" ]; then args=(--config \"$cfg\"); fi\nexport BBHOST_CAPTURE_DIR=${BBHOST_CAPTURE_DIR:-$data/f12}\ncd \"$here\" || exit 1\necho \"bbhost: AppImage, config ${cfg:-the per-user one}, log $log\"\n# tee -i: Ctrl-C stops the game, not the log, so its last lines are kept.\n./bbhost \"${args[@]}\" \"$@\" 2>&1 | tee -i \"$log\"\nexit \"${PIPESTATUS[0]}\"\nEOF\n\nif [ \"$profile\" = steamdeck ]; then\n    title=\"bbhost (Steam Deck)\"\n    comment=\"Bloodborne on PC: bbhost with the Steam Deck's settings\"\nelse\n    title=\"bbhost\"\n    comment=\"Bloodborne on PC: the game's own execut..able, recompiled for Vulkan\"\nfi\ncat > \"$appdir/bbhost.desktop\" <<EOF\n[Desktop Entry]\nType=Application\nName=$title\nComment=$comment\nExec=bbhost\nIcon=bbhost\nTerminal=false\nCategories=Game;\nEOF\n\n# The icon: the 256x256 image inside res/bbhost.ico, taken out of it as it is\n# (the AppImage spec's .DirIcon is that same file, 256x256 PNG).\npython3 - \"$SRC/res/bbhost.ico\" \"$appdir/bbhost.png\" <<'PY'\nimport struct, sys\nd = open(sys.argv[1], 'rb').read()\nif d[:4] != b'\\x00\\x00\\x01\\x00':\n    sys.exit(f'{sys.argv[1]}: not an ICO')\nbest = None\nfor i in range(struct.unpack('<H', d[4:6])[0]):\n    w, h, c, r, planes, bpp, size, off = struct.unpack('<BBBBHHII', d[6 + 16 * i:22 + 16 * i])\n    if d[off:off + 8] == b'\\x89PNG\\r\\n\\x1a\\n' and (best is None or size > best[0]):\n        best = (size, off)\nif best is None:\n    sys.exit(f'{sys.argv[1]}: no PNG image in it to use as the AppImage icon')\nopen(sys.argv[2], 'wb').write(d[best[1]:best[1] + best[0]])\nPY\ncp \"$appdir/bbhost.png\" \"$appdir/.DirIcon\"\n\n# Plain modes (a filesystem without them would send every file out executable).\nfind \"$appdir\" -type d -exec chmod 755 {} +\nfind \"$appdir\" -type f -exec chmod 644 {} +\nchmod 755 \"$appdir/bbhost\" \"$appdir/AppRun\"\n[ -f \"$appdir/run-bbhost.sh\" ] && chmod 755 \"$appdir/run-bbhost.sh\"\n\ntool=${APPIMAGETOOL:-}\nif [ -z \"$tool\" ]; then\n    tool=$work/appimagetool-x86_64.AppImage\n    url=${APPIMAGETOOL_URL:-https://github.com/AppImage/appimagetool/releases/download/continuous/appimagetool-x86_64.AppImage}\n    echo \"appimage: fetching appimagetool\"\n    curl -sSL -m 600 -o \"$tool\" \"$url\"\n    chmod 755 \"$tool\"\n    sum=$(sha256sum \"$tool\" | cut -d' ' -f1)\n    if [ -n \"${APPIMAGETOOL_SHA256:-}\" ]; then\n        [ \"$sum\" = \"$APPIMAGETOOL_SHA256\" ] ||\n            { echo \"appimagetool: sha256 $sum is not APPIMAGETOOL_SHA256\"; exit 1; }\n        echo \"appimage: appimagetool sha256 ok\"\n    else\n        echo \"appimage: appimagetool sha256 $sum (set APPIMAGETOOL_SHA256 to pin it)\"\n    fi\nfi\n[ -x \"$tool\" ] || { echo \"appimagetool: $tool is not executable\"; exit 1; }\n\ndest=$out/$name.AppImage\nrm -f \"$dest\"\nargs=(-n)  # no AppStream metadata in here\nif [ -n \"${APPIMAGETOOL_RUNTIME:-}\" ]; then args+=(--runtime-file \"$APPIMAGETOOL_RUNTIME\"); fi\n# appimagetool is itself an AppImage: APPIMAGE_EXTRACT_AND_RUN runs it without\n# FUSE, which a server or a container usually does not have.\nARCH=x86_64 APPIMAGE_EXTRACT_AND_RUN=1 \"$tool\" \"${args[@]}\" \"$appdir\" \"$dest\"\necho \"appimage: $dest ($(( $(stat -c %s \"$dest\") / 1048576 )) MB)\"\n"
```json
}
```

> shim realpath:
> ```bash
> #!/bin/bash
> # realpath [-m] paths
> m=0; args=()
> for a in "$@"; do case "$a" in -m) m=1;; *) args+=("$a");; esac; done
> python3 -c 'import os,sys
> m=sys.argv[1]=="1"
> for p in sys.argv[2:]:
>     print(os.path.realpath(p) if not m else os.path.abspath(p))' "$m" "${args[@]}"

> Hmm, os.path.abspath doesn't resolve symlinks — `realpath -m` resolves symlinks but doesn't require existence. os.path.realpath does exactly that (resolves symlinks, tolerates nonexistent). So just use os.path.realpath for both cases. Good.
> 
> shim sha256sum:
> ```bash
> #!/bin/bash
> python3 -c 'import hashlib,sys
> for f in sys.argv[1:]:
>     h=hashlib.sha256(open(f,"rb").read()).hexdigest()
>     print(h+"  "+f)' "$@"
> ```
> 
> shim stat: support `-c %s FILE`:
> ```bash
> #!/bin/bash
> if [ "$1" = "-c" ] && [ "$2" = "%s" ]; then exec /usr/bin/stat -f %z "$3"; fi
> exec /usr/bin/stat "$@"
> ```
> 
> shim xargs: handle `-r` (drop it) and the empty-input case:
> ```bash
> #!/bin/bash
> drop_r=0; cmd=()
> for a in "$@"; do [ "$a" = "-r" ] && continue; cmd+=("$a"); done
> inp=$(cat)
> [ -z "${inp//[[:space:]]/}" ] && exit 0
> # shellcheck disable=SC2086
> printf '%s\n' "$inp" | xargs "${cmd[@]}"
> ```
> Careful about recursion: shim calling `xargs` would find itself in PATH → infinite. Use /usr/bin/xargs explicitly.

> ```bash
> #!/bin/bash
> if [ "$1" = "-i" ]; then
>     shift
>     # BSD sed wants the (possibly empty) backup suffix as its own argument
>     exec /usr/bin/sed -i '' "$@"

```
===== AppRun =====
#!/bin/bash
# AppRun: starts bbhost out of the mounted AppImage. The image is read-only, so
# the session's log goes to ${XDG_DATA_HOME:-~/.local/share}/bbhost/logs (the
# newest ten are kept) and an F12 frame dump to a folder of its own there.
# Arguments are passed on, so --setup works.
set -o pipefail
here=${APPDIR:-$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)}
data=${XDG_DATA_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share}/bbhost
mkdir -p "$data/logs"
log=$data/logs/bbhost-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S).log
ls -1t "$data"/logs/bbhost-*.log 2>/dev/null | tail -n +10 | xargs -r rm -f
cfg=${BBHOST_CONFIG:-}
if [ -z "$cfg" ] && [ -f "$here/bbhost-steamdeck.toml" ]; then
    cfg=$here/bbhost-steamdeck.toml
fi
args=()
if [ -n "$cfg" ]; then args=(--config "$cfg"); fi
export BBHOST_CAPTURE_DIR=${BBHOST_CAPTURE_DIR:-$data/f12}
cd "$here" || exit 1
echo "bbhost: AppImage, config ${cfg:-the per-user one}, log $log"
# tee -i: Ctrl-C stops the game, not the log, so its last lines are kept.
./bbhost "${args[@]}" "$@" 2>&1 | tee -i "$log"
exit "${PIPESTATUS[0]}"
```

```
#!/bin/bash
# The Steam Deck's AppImage: the Linux one (tools/package_appimage.sh) with the
# Deck's settings - tools/steamdeck/bbhost-steamdeck.toml, its screen's
# 1280x800 full screen at the game's own 30 fps, and STEAMDECK.md - and, when
# BB_APPIMAGE_BUILD=1 builds it, compiled for the Deck's CPU: -march=znver2,
# which is what both Deck revisions are (Van Gogh and Sephiroth are Zen 2).
# The game's paths are not in it, as in every package: the per-user config
# holds those, so the Deck and a PC can share them.
#
#   tools/package_appimage_steamdeck.sh [INPUT] [OUTDIR]
#
# INPUT, OUTDIR and the switches are tools/package_appimage.sh's, plus
# BB_MARCH, which defaults to znver2 here (an empty BB_MARCH builds for the
# compiler's own target, as the plain Linux AppImage does).
#
# On a Deck: run the .AppImage, or add that file to Steam as a non-Steam game
# (Desktop Mode, Games, Add a Non-Steam Game) and start it from Game Mode.
# Running an AppImage needs FUSE, and "Cannot mount the AppImage, please check
# your FUSE setup" (or a missing libfuse.so.2) is what it says where that is
# not there - the Deck and Steam's own runtime both being known for it. Then
# put --appimage-extract-and-run among the game's launch options in Steam: the
# runtime unpacks itself into /tmp and runs from there. STEAMDECK.md has the
# rest (the controller layout, 30 or 60 fps, the first area's shader compile).
set -eu
cd "$(dirname "$0")"

```

```
- path: /Users/sandvault-dn/bbwork/bbhost-nocrash/tools/package_appimage.sh
  content: |
      cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
      SRC=$PWD
      profile=${BB_APPIMAGE_PROFILE:-linux}
      case "$profile" in
          linux | steamdeck) ;;
          *) echo "unknown BB_APPIMAGE_PROFILE=$profile (linux, steamdeck)"; exit 1 ;;
      esac
      out=$(realpath -m "${2:-build/appimage}")
      mkdir -p "$out"
      work=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
      
      if [ "${BB_APPIMAGE_BUILD:-0}" = 1 ]; then
          extra=""
          if [ -n "${BB_MARCH:-}" ]; then
              extra="-DCMAKE_C_FLAGS=-march=$BB_MARCH -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS=-march=$BB_MARCH"
              echo "appimage: building (CI_PORTABLE, -march=$BB_MARCH)"
          else
              echo "appimage: building (CI_PORTABLE, the compiler's own target)"
          fi
          CI_PORTABLE=1 CI_CMAKE_ARGS="${CI_CMAKE_ARGS:-} $extra" tools/ci_build.sh
          tools/package_linux.sh "${CI_WORK:-$SRC/build-ci}/build/bbhost" build/linux
      fi
      
      input=${1:-}
      if [ -z "$input" ]; then
          input=$(ls -1t build/linux/bbhost-linux-*.tar.gz 2>/dev/null | head -1 || true)
      fi
      if [ -z "$input" ] || [ ! -e "$input" ]; then
          echo "nothing to pack: pass tools/package_linux.sh's tarball or a bbhost binary, or set"
          echo "BB_APPIMAGE_BUILD=1 to build one (no tarball in build/linux)"
          exit 1
      fi
      
      mkdir -p "$work/pkg"
      case "$input" in
          *.tar.gz | *.tgz)
              cp "$input" "$work/pkg.tgz"
              ;;
          *)
              # A binary: the Linux package is what knows how to lay a bbhost out
              # (the manifests, the plugins, the launcher), so build one from it.
              [ -x "$input" ] || { echo "$input is neither a .tar.gz nor an executable"; exit 1; }
              tools/package_linux.sh "$input" "$work/linux"
              cp "$work"/linux/bbhost-linux-*.tar.gz "$work/pkg.tgz"
              ;;
      esac
      tar xzf "$work/pkg.tgz" -C "$work/pkg"
      pkg=$(ls -d "$work"/pkg/bbhost-linux-* 2>/dev/null | head -1)
      [ -n "$pkg" ] || { echo "the package has no bbhost-linux-* folder"; exit 1; }
      
      base=$(basename "$pkg")
      name=$base
      if [ "$profile" = steamdeck ]; then
          name=${base/bbhost-linux-/bbhost-steamdeck-}
      fi
      appdir=$work/$name.AppDir
      mkdir -p "$appdir"
      cp -r "$pkg"/. "$appdir"/
      # The tarball's write targets (the run fills them): a mounted AppImage cannot,
      # and AppRun sends those writes somewhere writable instead.
      rm -rf "$appdir/data" "$appdir/logs" "$appdir/build"
      
      if [ "$profile" = steamdeck ]; then
          cp tools/steamdeck/bbhost-steamdeck.toml tools/steamdeck/STEAMDECK.md "$appdir"/
          # The same edit tools/package_steamdeck.sh makes, so an extracted AppImage's
          # launcher uses the Deck's settings too.
          sed -i 's/^cfg=\${BBHOST_CONFIG:-bbhost.toml}/cfg=${BBHOST_CONFIG:-bbhost-steamdeck.toml}/' "$appdir/run-bbhost.sh"
          grep -q 'bbhost-steamdeck.toml' "$appdir/run-bbhost.sh" ||
              { echo "run-bbhost.sh: config line not found"; exit 1; }
      fi
      
      cat > "$appdir/AppRun" <<'EOF'
      #!/bin/bash
      # AppRun: starts bbhost out of the mounted AppImage. The image is read-only, so
      # the session's log goes to ${XDG_DATA_HOME:-~/.local/share}/bbhost/logs (the
      # newest ten are kept) and an F12 frame dump to a folder of its own there.
      # Arguments are passed on, so --setup works.
      set -o pipefail
      here=${APPDIR:-$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)}
      data=${XDG_DATA_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share}/bbhost
```

Both scripts are in, and I tested them as far as a Darwin host allows.

## What I added

- **`tools/package_appimage.sh`** (208 lines) — packs a Linux bbhost into an AppImage. Accepts a `package_linux.sh` tarball **or a bare binary** (in which case it runs `package_linux.sh` itself first, so the manifests, plugins and README come along exactly as that script lays them out).
- **`tools/package_appimage_steamdeck.sh`** (26 lines) — a wrapper that sets the Deck profile and `BB_MARCH=znver2`.
- **`docs/building.md`** — two rows in the package table plus a short paragraph on what the scripts fetch and the FUSE caveat.

On the server, from the tree that already built:

```sh
tools/package_appimage.sh build-ci/build/bbhost build/appimage
tools/package_appimage_steamdeck.sh build-ci/build/bbhost build/appimage
# or build and pack in one go:  BB_APPIMAGE_BUILD=1 tools/package_appimage_steamdeck.sh
```

## Your two questions

**Makeflags.** Both build scripts already run one job per core (`ci_build.sh:26` `JOBS=$(nproc)`, `linux_portable_build.sh` `-j"$(nproc)"`), so there was nothing to tune there. The real platform difference is `-march`: the generic script leaves `BB_MARCH` empty, because an AppImage is meant to run on other machines and `-march=native` would pin it to the build host. The Deck script defaults to `BB_MARCH=znver2` — correct for both Deck revisions, Van Gogh and Sephiroth are Zen 2 — and `BB_MARCH=native` or an empty `BB_MARCH=` overrides either.

**The `.desktop`.** You said you don't need one, and you don't get one as a file — but `appimagetool` reads a root desktop entry to name the app, and the AppImage spec wants one in the AppDir, so the script writes `bbhost.desktop` *inside* the AppDir at pack time. Nothing for you to manage. It also extracts the 256×256 PNG already embedded in `res/bbhost.ico` for the icon and `.DirIcon`, so no new artwork.

## What AppRun does, and why it isn't just the launcher

A mounted AppImage is read-only, so the tarball's `run-bbhost.sh` would fail writing `logs/` beside the binary. AppRun instead logs to `${XDG_DATA_HOME:-~/.local/share}/bbhost/logs` (newest ten kept), points `BBHOST_CAPTURE_DIR` there so F12 dumps still work, passes `--config .../bbhost-steamdeck.toml` on the Deck build, passes your arguments through (`--setup` works) and preserves the game's exit status through the `tee`.

## Verified

`shellcheck` reports zero errors (three info/style notes, all matching existing repo idioms); `bash -n` clean. Then three dry runs on this host with GNU shims plus a stub `appimagetool`, which confirmed: the AppDir contents and modes (only `bbhost`, `AppRun` and `run-bbhost.sh` executable), the icon really is a 256×256 PNG, `data/logs/build` removed, and for the Deck profile the toml + `STEAMDECK.md` are in with the launcher's `cfg=` line rewritten to `bbhost-steamdeck.toml`. Running AppRun with a fake binary: log lands in `~/.local/share/bbhost/logs`, 12 old logs prune to 10, `--setup` reaches the binary, `BBHOST_CAPTURE_DIR` is exported, the Deck build passes its config, and **exit status 7 propagates**.

## Not verified — real limitations

- **No real AppImage was ever built.** `appimagetool` (mksquashfs + runtime) is Linux-only and there's no Docker on this machine; only the AppDir and its launcher were exercised. The `APPIMAGETOOL_RUNTIME` branch is likewise untested.
- The binary-input path ran through the *real* `package_linux.sh` and `package_plugins.sh`, but with shimmed `objcopy`/`readelf`/`objdump`, so the dependency list it writes into `README-linux.txt` in that run was fake.
- `BB_APPIMAGE_BUILD=1` was not executed — it needs the Linux build.
- One caveat worth repeating: the AppImage is only as portable as the binary inside it. Point it at `build-ci/build/bbhost` from a plain (non-`CI_PORTABLE`) build and you get a single file that still refuses to start on older distros.

````
  content: |
      # FIXES-LOG
      
      Stability and crash fixes adapted from **BloodBorneButPc** (a Windows fork of the
      shadPS4/bbport engine) into **bbhost** (this native translation layer).
      
      The two projects do not share source, so each fix is re-expressed in bbhost's own
      architecture under the same switch name that gates it in BloodBorneButPc. Where
      bbhost already solved the same problem another way, that is noted rather than
      duplicated. Long-session VRAM accumulation and the launch-time heap overflow are
      the crashes these target.
      
      ## GPU hang guard - textures freed while still in use
      
      - **Source:** `BB_GC_RECENT_FRAMES` (default 48), `BB_IMAGE_FREE_DELAY_FRAMES`
        (default 32) in BloodBorneButPc's texture cache.
      - **Files:** `src/host/textures.cpp`.
      - **Change:** each surface records the video flip of its last use
        (`Surface::used_flip`, stamped wherever `used_ms` is). The cold-texture sweep
        (`evict_cold_surfaces_locked`) and the reused-memory retire
        (`textures_retire_reused_locked`) now skip any surface used or deleted within
        `max(BB_GC_RECENT_FRAMES, BB_IMAGE_FREE_DELAY_FRAMES)` flips. Frames are the
        GPU's own timeline, so a long frame (a hitch, a load) can no longer age a
        texture out from under a submission still reading it - the
        stalled-then-device-lost class of crash. The two counts share one floor (the
        larger of the two), so setting either alone to 0 does not switch it off; set
        both to 0 for bbhost's original behavior.
      - **Rationale:** bbhost already defers a deleted image's Vulkan objects to
        submission retirement (`defer_destroy_image`), so the "outlive unregistration"
        half is already covered; the frame floor adds the part it lacked - a texture
        the just-recorded frame used is never a candidate for freeing.
      
      ## VRAM cleanup - accumulation over a long session
      
      - **Source:** `BB_VRAM_PRESSURE_PERCENT` (default 85), `BB_VRAM_IDLE_SECONDS`
        (default 30; 10 s above 90% of the driver's budget) in BloodBorneButPc.
      - **Files:** `src/host/textures.cpp`, `src/host/gpu.cpp`,
        `src/host/gpu_internal.h`.
      - **Change:** `evict_cold_surfaces_locked` now measures pressure as a share of
        the driver's budget (new accessor `vram_budget_bytes()`) and:
        - triggers once usage reaches `BB_VRAM_PRESSURE_PERCENT` of that budget, in
          addition to bbhost's existing reserve-and-full-heap trigger;
        - frees only textures idle for `BB_VRAM_IDLE_SECONDS`, dropping that to 10 s
          once the budget is 90% used.
        - surfaces a shader or copy wrote are still never evicted (bbhost holds state
          the guest memory underneath does not), matching BloodBorneButPc keeping
          GPU-written blocks resident.
      - **Rationale:** `BBHOST_VRAM_EVICT_S` is still honored (`=0` off), but with
        neither variable set the idle is now 30 s where bbhost's was 20 s -
        `BBHOST_VRAM_EVICT_S=20` keeps the old default. The percentage line lets the
        sweep start before the reserve is hit and sweep harder as the card fills.
      
      ## Direct memory pool - launch crash on a large scene
      
      - **Source:** `BB_DMEM_MB` (BloodBorneButPc gives a scene above 1080p the
        9152 MiB pool instead of 5056 MiB).
      - **Files:** `src/hle/kernel.cpp`.
      - **Change:** `BB_DMEM_MB` names the direct memory the game is told it has (the
        stock 6 GiB otherwise), clamped to bbhost's own direct-memory window: 6 GiB
        (the stock size) up to 7.75 GiB, the same range
        `hle_kernel_set_dmem_size()` grows the pool in. A value at or below the stock
        6 GiB is ignored rather than shrinking the pool the game's heaps live in.
      - **Rationale:** bbhost already grows the game's GFX heap and its direct memory
        for a scene above 1080p (`grow_gfx_heap` / `hle_kernel_set_dmem_size`,
        `engine/live_resolution.cpp`), so the >1080p policy is present; the switch
        exposes the pool size itself, and its 7.75 GiB window is the ceiling that
        BloodBorneButPc's 9152 MiB meets only as far as the window allows.
      
      ## Already present in bbhost (not re-ported)
      
      - Crash reports for host faults on a game thread (Linux `SIGSEGV` handler,
        `main.cpp`; `host/win_crash.cpp` on Windows).
      - Write faults at the end of a GPU mapping handled, unclaimed faults on guest
        pages handed access back (`core/write_watch.cpp`).
      - Unknown texture formats read as `VK_FORMAT_UNDEFINED` and are skipped instead
        of aborting; a lost/out-of-date swapchain is recreated
        (`host/window.cpp`).
      - Audio output follows the device's real rate (`host/audio.cpp`).
      - Patch write sites are checked against the expected bytes before any is
        written (`engine/patch_manifest.cpp`).
      - VM/launcher-only items (Windows error 1450 memory check, 10 GB pool, region
        patch prompt) do not apply to bbhost's Linux path.
````

```
a long frame can no longer free a texture out from under a submission. Track
the flip of a surface's last use alongside used_ms and guard both the
cold-texture sweep and the reused-memory retire.

memory reaches that share of the driver's budget (new vram_budget_bytes) it
evicts textures idle for BB_VRAM_IDLE_SECONDS (30 s; 10 s above 90%), in
addition to the existing reserve trigger.
```

```
## Workflow

- `master` always builds. Work on a branch named for the change
  (`render/...`, `perf/...`, `fix/...`) and open a pull request.
- Rebase on `origin/master` before opening it; keep history linear, one
  commit per logical change.
- CI builds Linux and Windows and runs the tests; it must pass. CI has no GPU
  and no game files, so evidence that a change works in game is yours to
  bring.
- A commit message says what changed and why: a short subject
  (`render: the woods' trees are instanced draws`), then the cause and how it
  was checked.

## Releasing

A release is an annotated tag on `master` whose message holds the release
notes:
```

```json
  "content": "# Notes for agents\n\nWhat the `awakechan-fixes` branch adds on top of `master`, and how to check it.\n`FIXES-LOG.md` is the detail for the first part, `docs/building.md` for the\nsecond.\n\n## Stability fixes ported from BloodBorneButPc\n\n- `src/host/textures.cpp` - the GPU hang guard (`BB_GC_RECENT_FRAMES` 48,\n  `BB_IMAGE_FREE_DELAY_FRAMES` 32, which share one floor) and the pressure-based\n  cold sweep (`BB_VRAM_PRESSURE_PERCENT` 85, `BB_VRAM_IDLE_SECONDS` 30; `0` off).\n- `src/hle/kernel.cpp` - `BB_DMEM_MB` names the direct memory pool, clamped to\n  the 6 GiB-7.75 GiB window `hle_kernel_set_dmem_size()` uses.\n- The switches default on, and the whole sweep still needs a VRAM reserve\n  (`vram_reserve_bytes()`, `textures.cpp`), so on an integrated GPU only the\n  hang guard is active. `FIXES-LOG.md` has the defaults and the `0` semantics.\n\n## AppImage packaging\n\n- `tools/package_appimage.sh [INPUT] [OUTDIR]` packs `tools/package_linux.sh`'s\n  tarball, or a bbhost binary (which it packs into that tarball first), into an\n  AppImage. `BB_APPIMAGE_BUILD=1` builds before packing - `CI_PORTABLE=1\n  tools/ci_build.sh`, so the binary inside runs on other machines - and\n  `BB_MARCH` says what to compile for. Output defaults to `build/appimage`.\n- `tools/package_appimage_steamdeck.sh` is the same with the Deck's settings\n  (`tools/steamdeck/bbhost-steamdeck.toml`, `STEAMDECK.md`) and `-march=znver2`,\n  which is what both Deck revisions are (Van Gogh and Sephiroth are Zen 2).\n- A mounted AppImage is read-only, so AppRun keeps the session's log and the F12\n  frame dumps under `~/.local/share/bbhost` instead of beside the binary.\n  Running one needs FUSE: `--appimage-extract-and-run` is the way out where\n  libfuse.so.2 is missing, which the Deck and Steam's runtime are known for.\n- Neither script has been run against real `appimagetool` (mksquashfs), and\n  `BB_APPIMAGE_BUILD=1` has not been run at all: both need Linux. The AppDir\n  contents, the icon and AppRun's behaviour were checked by hand instead.\n\n## Checking a change\n\n- `cmake -S . -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo`, `cmake --build build -j`,\n  then `cd build && ctest --output-on-failure`. Tests that read game files skip\n  unless `BBHOST_APP0` names a game folder.\n- `tools/ci_build.sh` is the from-scratch Linux build CI runs, and needs no game\n  files; `tools/win_syntax_check.sh <file>` checks one file for the Windows\n  target without a full cross build.\n- bbhost builds only on x86-64 Linux (and Windows from Linux), so a Darwin or\n  ARM host cannot compile it: a change here is unverified until it has been\n  built on Linux.\n\n## Known, left alone\n\n- `tools/linux_portable_build.sh:136` builds `bb_plugin_hello`, `randomizer`,\n  `boss_rush` and `mutators`, but not `bb_plugin_debug_menu`, while\n  `tools/package_plugins.sh` fails unless all four official plugins are present.\n  That packaging route fails its own check; `tools/ci_build.sh`, which builds\n  every target, is unaffected.\n"
```

One command does it — the Deck wrapper already sets the CPU flag:

```sh
git pull                                   # to get bf46888 with the scripts
BB_APPIMAGE_BUILD=1 CI_APT=0 tools/package_appimage_steamdeck.sh
```

What that expands to, in order:

1. `BB_MARCH=znver2` (the wrapper's default) → `CI_PORTABLE=1 CI_CMAKE_ARGS="-DCMAKE_C_FLAGS=-march=znver2 -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS=-march=znver2" tools/ci_build.sh`
2. `tools/package_linux.sh build-ci/build/bbhost build/linux`
3. packs it into **`build/appimage/bbhost-steamdeck-<rev>.AppImage`**

`-march=znver2` is right for every Deck — Van Gogh (LCD) and Sephiroth (OLED) are both Zen 2 — and it's what LLVM/Clang has taken since clang 9, including the clang 18 that `ci_build.sh` forces with `CC=clang CXX=clang++`. I checked the flag is accepted and actually changes codegen (`--target=x86_64-linux-gnu -march=znver2` emits `vfmadd213ss`); the plain form failed on this machine only because its default triple is arm64.

**Makeflags:** nothing to set. `ci_build.sh:26` is `JOBS=$(nproc)` and it builds `all` targets, so you already get one job per core and the plugins the packer needs.

**Overrides:** `BB_MARCH=x86-64-v3` (a portable AVX2 baseline), `BB_MARCH=native` if you're building *on* the Deck, or `BB_MARCH=` to leave it to the compiler. `CI_APT=0` skips apt — the prefix in `build-ci/prefix` is reused, so this run is mostly bbhost plus the pack.

**Check the flag actually landed**, rather than assuming:
```sh
grep -E '^CMAKE_(C|CXX)_FLAGS:' build-ci/build/CMakeCache.txt
```
It should read `-march=znver2`.

**The one thing that can bite you:** the glibc floor is the *build machine's*. On your Ubuntu 24.04 box that's 2.39, which is exactly what upstream's own Linux and Steam Deck packages require, so a Deck runs it. Build it on the server, not on a newer distro (Arch, Fedora 40+, Ubuntu 25.04), or the Deck may refuse to start it.

On the Deck: add the `.AppImage` as a non-Steam game and start it from Game Mode; if it won't mount, put `--appimage-extract-and-run` in its launch options.

Still unexecuted here: the `BB_APPIMAGE_BUILD=1` path itself, and any real `appimagetool` run — both need Linux. If you'd rather have the guaranteed-portable chroot route (`tools/linux_portable_build.sh`, Ubuntu 24.04 rootfs) carry `-march` too, that needs a small edit to pass build flags through to its cmake — say the word.

Yes — that command compiles bbhost with `-march=znver2`. Two scope caveats worth knowing.

**What it expands to**

`BB_MARCH` defaults to `znver2` in the wrapper (`package_appimage_steamdeck.sh:26`), which becomes:

```
CI_PORTABLE=1 CI_CMAKE_ARGS="-DCMAKE_C_FLAGS=-march=znver2 -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS=-march=znver2" tools/ci_build.sh
tools/package_linux.sh build-ci/build/bbhost build/linux
```

then packs `build/appimage/bbhost-steamdeck-<rev>.AppImage`. `BB_APPIMAGE_BUILD=1` survives the `bash ...` invocation since it's set as an environment prefix, and the wrapper `exec`s the main script by path.

**Caveat 1 — the flags reach bbhost and its plugins only.** `ci_build.sh:102` is the only line that consumes `CI_CMAKE_ARGS`; that's the bbhost project configure, and it builds every target, so bbhost and all four plugin `.so`s get `-march=znver2`. The vendored deps in `build-ci/prefix` do not:

- SDL3's configure (`ci_build.sh:72`) passes no `CMAKE_C_FLAGS`, only `-DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release`;
- ffmpeg's configure (`ci_build.sh:96`) passes only `--extra-cflags=-O2`.

And the prefix is reused if it already exists, so they keep whatever they were first built as. bbhost's HLE and engine code is the CPU-bound part, so this is the right place for the flag — I wouldn't rebuild ffmpeg/SDL3 for it.

**Caveat 2 — the server has to be x86-64.** On an arm64 host clang rejects the flag outright (`unsupported argument 'znver2' to option '-march='`, which is exactly what this Mac's arm64 clang said). Your build already succeeded, so your box is x86-64; that's just the sanity check.

**Also:** if `build-ci/build` was configured by an earlier run, the new `-D` still takes effect — CMake updates the cache entry and recompiles. And add `CI_APT=0` if the deps are already installed, to skip the apt step.

To confirm rather than trust it:

```sh
grep -E '^CMAKE_(C|CXX)_FLAGS' build-ci/build/CMakeCache.txt   # expect -march=znver2
```

Correct on all counts.

**Scoping:** `CMAKE_C_FLAGS`/`CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS` belong to one CMake project — the bbhost one at `ci_build.sh:100-102`. SDL3 (`:72`) and ffmpeg (`:89`) are configured by separate invocations that never see those variables, so nothing ffmpeg does can affect bbhost's codegen, and vice versa. Your run's own output confirms which project got the flag: it was the bbhost configure that printed those `-- bbhost:` lines.

**Mixing is safe, too.** A generic-compiled ffmpeg static lib linking into a `-march=znver2` bbhost is not a hazard: on x86-64 the psABI baseline doesn't move with `-march`, and znver2 is AVX2/FMA, not something like AVX-512 that changes argument passing. ffmpeg generic costs you nothing that matters — the movie decoder isn't the bottleneck.

Your pasted output looks right: `appimage: building (CI_PORTABLE, -march=znver2)` is my script's line, and the three `-- bbhost: ...found` lines are from `ci_build.sh:103` after a successful configure.

**Two things to eyeball when you run it**, both quick:

1. **The Deck config actually applied.** AppRun prints one line at startup; in my dry run of the Deck profile it read `bbhost: AppImage, config /…/bbhost-steamdeck.toml, log …`. If yours says `config the per-user one`, the profile didn't take and you'd be running 16:9 fullscreen-less defaults.
2. **The session log** is at `~/.local/share/bbhost/logs/bbhost-<date>-<time>.log`, and an F12 frame dump goes to `~/.local/share/bbhost/f12` — not next to the AppImage, because the mount is read-only. That's the intended behaviour, not a failure.

**On the Deck:** the artifact is `build/appimage/bbhost-steamdeck-<rev>.AppImage` on the server. Copy it over, add it as a non-Steam game, start it from Game Mode. First launch opens the setup window for the game folder and decrypted eboot — those stay in the per-user config, shared with any other bbhost you have. If it won't mount, add `--appimage-extract-and-run` to its launch options in Steam.

If anything goes wrong, send me the AppRun line plus the log from `~/.local/share/bbhost/logs` — that has the FUSE/mount failure, the config selection and the GPU init in one place.
