> _Reasoning_
> Now I understand the mechanism well enough to answer precisely and to implement.
> 
> **What the assert is**: `ReserveRecordData(bytes)` asserts `bytes + 1024 <= RecordChunk::Capacity` (128 KiB). Record data are the variable-length payloads a deferred command needs at execution time (descriptor write arrays + image/buffer infos, vertex-binding arrays, vkRuntime copies/upload regions). The chunk is a fixed 128 KiB block; commands point into it with raw pointers, and the chunk is recycled after execution. If a single draw's payload exceeds the chunk, there's nowhere to put it → assert → game stops (this is the fork's "oversized command data" crash).
> 
> **Can we "catch the error and try again"?** Two distinct notions:
> 1. Retry the *allocation* into a fallback place (spill block owned by the chunk): there's no failure left to catch, except genuinely running out of host memory. This is exactly the fork's fix, and it *is* "catch and continue" rather than "stop".
> 2. Retry the *operation* (re-run the draw): no — the payload is produced by the draw-recording pass from the guest's command stream; there's nothing to re-run and no way to make the payload smaller. The only choice is where to keep it.
> 
> So the answer: yes, we can make it degrade instead of stopping — by catching the "doesn't fit" case and putting that payload in a fallback allocation the chunk owns (spill), and if even that allocation fails, log once and skip the draw/pass instead of aborting. I can implement both:
> - `RecordChunk::Allocate(bytes, align)`: if `bytes > Capacity` (or the chunk is nearly full and the payload is bigger than the remaining room even in a fresh chunk — handled by reserve+retire), take a spill block.
> - `ReserveRecordData(bytes)`: no hard assert; log once if `bytes + 1024 > Capacity`; ensure the data will fit after retiring the chunk; for oversized payloads, reserve a spill block up front (kept in the chunk).
> - If the spill allocation itself fails (out of host memory): return a null span? That would break commands that deref it... Hmm. Better: make `RecordData` return the input span as a last resort? That's dangling if the caller's storage dies. Hmm, in the failure case the safe choice is to *not* defer: hmm.

> 1. Try the chunk (normal path).
> 2. void Scheduler::MaybeSplit() {
    if (workers.size() < 2 || current_segment + 1 >= MaxSegments || !IsRecordingDeferred() ||
        BbToggle::Disabled(BbToggle::ParallelRecording)) {
        return;
    }
    // Cutting inside a render pass closes and reopens it: only after a longer stretch.
    const size_t bytes = segment_bytes + CurrentChunk().Size();
    if (bytes < (is_rendering ? 2 * split_bytes : split_bytes)) {
        return;
    }
    if (is_rendering) {
        CarrySuspend(true);
        Record([](vk::CommandBuffer cmdbuf) { cmdbuf.endRendering(); });
        is_rendering = false;
        resume_rendering = true;
    } else {
        CarrySuspend(false);
    }
    if (async_submit) {
        // Its recording thread ends the segment's command buffer (the pool is that thread's).
        Record([](vk::CommandBuffer cmdbuf) { Check(cmdbuf.end()); });
    }
    HandOver();
    ++current_segment;
    batch->segments[current_segment] = vk::CommandBuffer{};
    segment_bytes = 0;
    active_worker.store(current_segment % workers.size(), std::memory_order_relaxed);
    // The next command buffer starts without dynamic state: the next draw sets all of it.

      struct SubmissionBatch {
          static constexpr u32 MaxSegments = 64;
          std::array<vk::CommandBuffer, MaxSegments> segments{}; ///< null until begun
          std::array<u32, MaxSegments> handed{}, recorded{};
          void Reset() {

      /// bbport: a block of deferred Vulkan commands. Commands are closures placed in
      /// fixed storage (no allocation per command) and run in order on the recording thread.
      class RecordChunk {
      public:
          static constexpr size_t Capacity = 128 * 1024;
      
          /// Returns false (and leaves `func` untouched) when the chunk has no room.
          template <typename Func>
          bool Push(Func&& func) {
              using Command = TypedCommand<std::decay_t<Func>>;
              static_assert(sizeof(Command) <= Capacity, "recorded command is too large");
              const size_t offset = (used + alignof(Command) - 1) & ~(alignof(Command) - 1);
              if (offset + sizeof(Command) > Capacity) {
                  return false;
              }
              auto* command = new (storage + offset) Command(std::forward<Func>(func));
              if (last) {
                  last->next = command;
              } else {
                  first = command;
              }
              last = command;
              used = offset + sizeof(Command);
              PrefetchAhead();
              return true;
          }
      
          /// Raw storage in the chunk for a command's variable-length data; null when full.
          void* Allocate(size_t bytes, size_t align) {
              const size_t offset = (used + align - 1) & ~(align - 1);
              if (offset + bytes > Capacity) {
                  return nullptr;
              }
              used = offset + bytes;
              PrefetchAhead();
              return storage + offset;
          }
      
          void Execute(vk::CommandBuffer cmdbuf) {
              for (CommandBase* command = first; command;) {
                  CommandBase* const next = command->next;
                  command->Execute(cmdbuf);
                  command->~CommandBase();
                  command = next;
              }
              first = last = nullptr;
              used = 0;
          }
      
          [[nodiscard]] bool Empty() const noexcept {
              return first == nullptr;
          }
      
          [[nodiscard]] size_t Size() const noexcept {
              return used;
          }

          SubmissionBatch* batch = nullptr; ///< the submission it belongs to (Scheduler)

          /// that must be recorded before this chunk runs.

          /// it back from that core. Requesting ownership a few lines ahead overlaps those

          void PrefetchAhead() const {

A payload beyond what a draw could carry (or a failed allocation) returns null; the\n    /// caller reports that instead of writing through it.\n    void* AllocateOversized(size_t bytes, size_t align) {\n        static constexpr size_t Ceiling = 16 * 1024 * 1024;\n        static constexpr size_t MinBlock = 128 * 1024;\n        if (bytes > Ceiling) {\n            return nullptr;\n        }\n        if (!spill_blocks.empty()) {\n            SpillBlock& block = spill_blocks.back();\n            std::byte* const base = block.bytes.get();\n            const auto address = reinterpret_cast<uintptr_t>(base) + block.used;\n            const auto aligned = (address + align - 1) & ~uintptr_t(align - 1);\n            const size_t offset = size_t(aligned - reinterpret_cast<uintptr_t>(base));\n            if (offset + bytes <= block.size) {\n                block.used = offset + bytes;\n                return base + offset;\n            }\n        }\n        const size_t size = std::max(bytes + align, MinBlock);\n        std::unique_ptr<std::byte[]> block{new (std::nothrow) std::byte[size]};\n        if (!block) {\n            return nullptr;\n        }\n        std::byte* const base = block.get();\n        const auto address = reinterpret_cast<uintptr_t>(base);\n        const auto aligned = (address + align - 1) & ~uintptr_t(align - 1);\n        const size_t offset = size_t(aligned - address);\n        spill_blocks.push_back(SpillBlock{std::move(block), size, offset + bytes});\n        return base + offset;\n    }\n\n    alignas(64) std::byte storage[Capacity];\n    size_t used = 0;\n    CommandBase* first{};\n    CommandBase* last{};\n    std::vector<SpillBlock> spill_blocks; ///< bbport: oversized payloads (AllocateOversized)\n};",

+    /// bbport: a block of its own for a payload the chunk cannot hold (BloodBorneButPc's spill).
+    /// Kept by the chunk and reused: a draw whose record data exceeds Capacity allocates its block
+    /// when the draw first shows up, not on every frame it appears in. Without one the payload had
+    /// nowhere to go and the assert in ReserveRecordData stopped the game ("oversized command
+    /// data").
+    struct SpillBlock {
+        std::unique_ptr<std::byte[]> bytes;
+        size_t size = 0;
+        size_t used = 0; ///< filled from the front each pass (Reset in Execute)
+    };
+
+    /// bbport: places an oversized payload in the block reserved last, or in a new one when it does
+    /// not fit. A payload beyond what a draw could carry (or a failed allocation) returns null; the
+    /// caller reports that instead of writing through it.
+    void* AllocateOversized(size_t bytes, size_t align) {
+        static constexpr size_t Ceiling = 16 * 1024 * 1024;
+        static constexpr size_t MinBlock = 128 * 1024;
+        if (bytes > Ceiling) {
+            return nullptr;
+        }
+        if (!spill_blocks.empty()) {
+            SpillBlock& block = spill_blocks.back();
+            std::byte* const base = block.bytes.get();
+            const auto address = reinterpret_cast<uintptr_t>(base) + block.used;
+            const auto aligned = (address + align - 1) & ~uintptr_t(align - 1);
+            const size_t offset = size_t(aligned - reinterpret_cast<uintptr_t>(base));
+            if (offset + bytes <= block.size) {
+                block.used = offset + bytes;
+                return base + offset;
+            }
+        }
+        const size_t size = std::max(bytes + align, MinBlock);
+        std::unique_ptr<std::byte[]> block{new (std::nothrow) std::byte[size]};
+        if (!block) {
+            return nullptr;
+        }
+        std::byte* const base = block.get();
+        const auto address = reinterpret_cast<uintptr_t>(base);
+        const auto aligned = (address + align - 1) & ~uintptr_t(align - 1);
+        const size_t offset = size_t(aligned - address);
+        spill_blocks.push_back(SpillBlock{std::move(block), size, offset + bytes});
+        return base + offset;
+    }
+
     alignas(64) std::byte storage[Capacity];
     size_t used = 0;
     CommandBase* first{};
     CommandBase* last{};
+    std::vector<SpillBlock> spill_blocks; ///< bbport: oversized payloads (AllocateOversized)
 };
